revised: Scientists estimate at least hundreds of billions in the part we can observe. The exact number is uncertain. Many galaxies are too faint or far away to see clearly. Better telescopes can change the estimates.
note: Explains gravity, the solar system, and the distance unit.

original: Our solar system is in the Milky Way. It has a wide, flat disk with spiral arms and a centre shaped like a bar. The main disk of stars is roughly 100,000 light-years across. A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.
revised: The Milky Way is the galaxy that contains our Sun and its planets. Most of its stars form a wide, flat disk. The disk has spiral arms and a bar-shaped center. It is roughly 100,000 light-years across. A light-year is how far light travels in one year.
note: Explains gravity, the solar system, and the distance unit.

original: In Judaism, becoming bar mitzvah means a boy takes on religious responsibilities, traditionally at age 13. A ceremony or celebration may mark the occasion. It does not mean he becomes an adult in every legal or practical sense.
revised: In Judaism, a bar mitzvah marks a boy taking on religious duties. This traditionally happens at age 13. A ceremony or celebration may mark the occasion. It does not mean he is an adult for every purpose. For example, legal age limits still apply separately.
note: Explains religious responsibility without implying legal adulthood.

original: Stir-frying is a cooking technique where you quickly cook ingredients in a wok or large pan over high heat, constantly stirring them.
revised: Stir-frying means cooking small pieces of food quickly over high heat. You use a wok or a large pan. Keep moving the food around as it cooks. A wok is a deep pan often used for this method.
note: Explains the cooking action and unfamiliar pan name.

original: An example of an element is oxygen. It's a gas that we need to breathe to stay alive. Oxygen is represented by the symbol "O" on the periodic table.
revised: Oxygen is an example of an element. An element is made from just one type of atom. Atoms are tiny building blocks of matter. Oxygen is a gas we need to breathe. On the periodic table, its symbol is O.
note: Explains element and atom while preserving the oxygen example.

original: First restart the computer and close programs you are not using. Check whether storage is nearly full or one app is using lots of memory. Built-in cleanup tools may help with disk space, but deleting files does not always fix slowness.
revised: Restart your computer first. Then close programs you are not using. Check whether the storage is almost full. Also check whether one app is using most of the computer's memory. A built-in cleanup tool may free some storage space. But deleting files does not solve every cause of a slow computer.
note: Separates checks and preserves the limits of cleanup.

original: Many snow guns spray tiny water droplets into cold air. The droplets freeze as they fall, forming small grains of ice on the slope. Temperature and humidity both matter: the air must let the droplets cool enough to freeze.
revised: Many snowmaking machines spray tiny drops of water into cold air. The drops freeze as they fall. They land as small grains of ice on the slope. The air must be cold enough for this to happen. The amount of moisture in the air also affects how well the drops cool.
note: Explains humidity in everyday words and keeps both conditions.

original: A journal publishes research papers in a field. Nature and Science are examples. JSTOR and ScienceDirect are platforms for finding papers, while Google Scholar is a search tool. Your topic will help decide which journals are useful.
revised: A research journal publishes studies about a subject. Nature and Science are examples of journals. JSTOR and ScienceDirect help you find papers from many journals. Google Scholar is a search tool for research. Which subject is your paper about?
note: Explains journals and open access and preserves access limits.

original: Try university lecture pages, Khan Academy, or course platforms such as edX and Coursera. Free access varies by course, and certificates may cost money. Check the course page before signing up.
revised: Try university lecture pages or Khan Academy. You can also look at edX and Coursera. Some courses are free to study, but others cost money. A certificate may cost extra. Check the course page before you sign up.
note: Explains journals and open access and preserves access limits.

original: Some academic journals offer free access to their articles, while others require a subscription. You can try searching for open-access journals or looking for journals that offer free trials or limited free access. Your university library may also provide free access to academic journals through their website.
revised: Yes. Some journals let anyone read their papers for free. These are often called open-access journals. Other journals charge for access. Your university library may already pay for access you can use. Start by searching the library's website.
note: Explains journals and open access and preserves access limits.

original: Look at the camera from time to time while speaking. That can feel like eye contact to others. You can also look at the screen to follow their reactions; you do not need to stare at the lens throughout the call.
revised: Look at the camera from time to time while you speak. This can look like eye contact to other people. Also look at the screen to see their reactions. You do not need to stare at the camera for the whole call.
note: Keeps flexible eye contact advice in short sentences.

original: The Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum, and Notre Dame Cathedral are must-visit places in Paris.
revised: The Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum, and Notre Dame Cathedral are popular choices. The best places for your trip depend on what you enjoy.
note: Explains tour choices and gives concrete comparison checks.

original: Yes, there are many guided tour options available, including audio guides, group tours, and private tours. You can book them online in advance.
revised: Yes. Options may include group tours, private tours, or recorded audio guides. An audio guide explains a place through headphones as you visit. Check the attraction's official website for available tours and booking details.
note: Explains tour choices and gives concrete comparison checks.

original: Start with the attraction’s own website for official tours or listed partners. For other companies, compare recent reviews, group size, guide language, what is included, and cancellation terms. A booking platform may list tours from many different operators.
revised: Start with the attraction's official website. It may list its own tours or approved partners. For other companies, read recent reviews. Check the group size, guide's language, and what the price includes. Also check the rules for cancelling. A booking website may sell tours run by several different companies.
note: Explains tour choices and gives concrete comparison checks.

original: If the eardrum is damaged, it can affect our ability to hear, and in some cases, may require medical attention to repair or treat the damage.
revised: Damage to the eardrum can make it harder to hear. Some damage needs medical treatment. A healthcare professional can check what happened and what care is needed.
note: Makes the possible hearing effect and need for assessment clear.

original: Yes, some people are born with color vision deficiency, which means they have trouble seeing certain colors. This is usually because they have a problem with one or more types of cones in their eyes.
revised: Yes. Some people are born with color vision deficiency. This means they have trouble telling certain colors apart. Cone cells in the eye help us see colors. In many cases, one or more types of cone cell work differently.
note: Explains the condition and cone cells without saying all color is absent.

original: Try skimming first to get the main idea: look at headings and key sentences. Scanning is different: it means looking quickly for a specific fact, name, or word. Use the approach that matches what you need to find.
revised: Start by looking at the headings and key sentences. This quick first look is called skimming. It helps you find the main idea. Scanning means looking for one specific thing, such as a date or name. Use skimming for an overview. Use scanning when you need a particular fact.
note: Explains both reading terms through their different purposes.

original: Check your heating and how well your home keeps heat in. Gather warm clothes and supplies before winter arrives.
revised: Check that your heating works before the weather turns cold. Check where your home may be losing heat. Get warm clothes ready. Gather supplies you may need if the power goes out.
note: Uses concrete winter checks and makes wiper replacement conditional.

original: Useful supplies include warm blankets, lights, spare batteries, water, and food for possible outages. In snowy areas, a shovel and suitable ice treatment can help. Plan for any medicines or other essentials you rely on.
revised: Keep warm blankets, drinking water, and food for a possible power cut. Have a flashlight and spare batteries ready. Remember medicines and other things you rely on. If snow is likely, a shovel may help. Choose an ice treatment that suits your paths.
note: Uses concrete winter checks and makes wiper replacement conditional.

original: Check your tyre pressure and tread. Replace your windscreen wipers and keep a winter kit in the car, with items such as a blanket, torch, and snacks.
revised: Check your tire pressure and the depth of the tire grooves. Check your windshield wipers and replace them if they are worn. Keep a winter kit in your car. Useful items include a blanket, flashlight, and snacks.
note: Uses concrete winter checks and makes wiper replacement conditional.

original: Dogs, cats, fish, and birds are common pets, but none are automatically easy to care for. Their needs, costs, and lifespans differ. Choose only after checking what your family can provide.
revised: Dogs, cats, fish, and birds are common family pets. Each needs regular care. Their costs and needs differ, and some live much longer than others. Find out what an animal needs before choosing it. Make sure your family can provide that care.
note: Replaces perfect-pet claims with matching care needs.

original: You can adopt a pet from a local animal shelter or rescue organization. They usually have many animals waiting for a forever home, and the staff can help you find the perfect pet for your family.
revised: Contact a local animal shelter or a group that rehomes animals. Tell the staff about your home and family. They can help you find an animal whose needs you can meet. Spend time learning about the animal before deciding.
note: Replaces perfect-pet claims with matching care needs.

original: I can suggest books. What kind do you enjoy, such as mystery, fantasy, history, or biography?
revised: What kinds of books do you enjoy? For example, do you like mysteries, fantasy, history, or life stories?
note: Uses familiar genre wording and preserves the library access limit.

original: Agatha Christie’s mysteries and the Sherlock Holmes stories are classic options. For a library copy, check your local catalog; I cannot see what it currently has available.
revised: Agatha Christie's mysteries and the Sherlock Holmes stories are classic choices. Check your library's list of books for a copy. I cannot see which books your library has available.
note: Uses familiar genre wording and preserves the library access limit.

original: Europe has a lot to offer. What type of vacation are you looking for (beach, city, history, food, etc.)?
revised: What would you most like to do in Europe? You might focus on beaches, history, food, or city visits.
note: Keeps travel advice conditional and makes lodging search practical.

original: In that case, I'd recommend visiting Rome, Italy, and Paris, France. Both cities are rich in history and culture, with famous landmarks like the Colosseum and the Eiffel Tower.
revised: Rome in Italy and Paris in France could suit you. Both have many historic sites and cultural attractions. Rome has the Colosseum, and Paris has the Eiffel Tower.
note: Keeps travel advice conditional and makes lodging search practical.

original: Yes, there are many affordable options for accommodations in Rome and Paris, including hostels, guesthouses, and budget hotels. You can also consider staying in nearby neighborhoods or suburbs for lower prices.
revised: Look for hostels, guesthouses, and budget hotels. Places outside the city center may cost less. Compare the full price before booking. Also check how you would reach the places you want to visit.
note: Keeps travel advice conditional and makes lodging search practical.

original: The libero specializes in receiving serves and defending attacks from the back row. Under FIVB rules, a libero cannot block or complete an attack when the ball is entirely above the net, regardless of where the libero is on the court.
revised: The libero is a volleyball player who mainly defends from the back row. This player receives serves and tries to keep attacks off the floor. Under FIVB rules, a libero cannot block. A libero also cannot finish an attack with the ball entirely above the net. That limit applies anywhere on the court.
note: Explains the role while preserving the stated FIVB restriction.

original: A wall-mounted bike rack is space-efficient and keeps your bike off the floor, making it easier to clean and move around the room.
revised: It keeps your bike off the floor and saves floor space. That makes it easier to walk around the room. You can also clean the floor under the bike more easily.
note: Replaces space-efficient with its concrete effect.

original: Penny, tassel, and horsebit loafers are common styles. Loafers are slip-on shoes; the names describe details such as a strap, tassels, or metal decoration.
revised: Loafers are shoes you slip on without tying laces. Penny loafers have a strap across the top. Tassel loafers have small hanging decorations called tassels. Horsebit loafers have a metal decoration across the top.
note: Explains how to recognize each named shoe style.

original: There are many online forums and social media groups dedicated to specific types of collecting. You can also find local collector clubs and attend events like conventions and trade shows.
revised: You can join online discussion groups for the things you collect. Some groups meet through social media. You may also find a local collectors' club. Collector fairs and shows let you meet people and see their collections.
note: Replaces community and event jargon with plain descriptions.

original: Some common annual events include family reunions, summer picnics, or attending cultural festivals. These events help strengthen family bonds and create lasting memories.
revised: Families may meet each year for a reunion or summer picnic. A reunion is a planned gathering of relatives. Some families also go to a local or cultural festival together. These events can give them time to catch up and make shared memories.
note: Explains reunion and keeps family benefits possible rather than guaranteed.

original: Some popular workplace environments include open offices, co-working spaces, and remote work setups. Many companies also offer hybrid models that combine these options.
revised: Some people work in shared offices, while others work from home. A co-working space is an office shared by people from different businesses. A hybrid job mixes office days with work from home. Other jobs take place in shops, factories, or similar workplaces.
note: Explains workplace terms and makes restaurant advice actionable.

original: Yes, restaurants are a type of workplace environment, often with a fast-paced and dynamic atmosphere. They can include kitchens, dining areas, and bars, and require strong teamwork and communication among staff.
revised: Yes. A restaurant is a workplace too. Staff may work in the kitchen, dining area, or bar. Busy periods can move quickly. Workers need to share information and help one another.
note: Explains workplace terms and makes restaurant advice actionable.

original: Be prepared for a fast-paced environment, and be willing to learn and multitask. Good communication skills and attention to detail are also important for providing excellent customer service.
revised: Be ready to learn and work with other people. Busy periods may involve several tasks at once. Ask how your team decides which task comes first. Listen carefully to orders and check details when you are unsure.
note: Explains workplace terms and makes restaurant advice actionable.

original: One easy swap is using olive oil instead of butter for cooking. Olive oil is rich in healthy fats and can add flavor to your dishes.
revised: For some dishes, try a little olive oil in place of butter. This can be a better choice for your heart. Olive oil can also add flavor. Choose the oil and amount to suit the recipe.
note: Cross-review: removed the vague unsaturated-fat gloss. Explains the practical swap in familiar words, keeps quantities and recipe suitability, and qualifies the heart-health benefit using NHS guidance.

original: Buoyancy is the upward push from a liquid or gas on something partly or fully inside it. For example, water pushes upward on a boat.
revised: Buoyancy is an upward push from water, another liquid, or a gas. It acts on an object partly or fully inside that material. For example, water pushes upward on a boat. That upward push helps the boat float.
note: Explains the force with the existing boat example.

original: The crisp snack kind is usually made by pressing puffed rice into a round shape. Rice cakes can also mean soft foods made from rice or rice flour in other cuisines.
revised: The crisp snack called a rice cake is usually made from puffed rice. The rice is pressed into a flat, often round shape. Rice cake can also mean a soft food in other cooking traditions. Those versions may be made with rice or rice flour.
note: Separates the snack from other meanings of rice cake.

original: Reading is an excellent hobby for relaxation. It can help reduce stress and expand your knowledge on different topics.
revised: Reading can be a relaxing hobby. You can choose stories or books about subjects you enjoy. It may help you feel less stressed. You can also learn something new while you read.
note: Uses familiar language and keeps relaxation a possible benefit.

original: Begin with short, comfortable periods of jogging mixed with walking, rather than forcing yourself to run continuously. Build up gradually and allow recovery. If you have pain or a health concern, get suitable advice before increasing the effort.
revised: Start with short periods of easy jogging. Walk between them when you need a break. Gradually add more jogging as it feels manageable. Leave time to rest between runs. If you have pain or a health concern, get advice before doing more.
note: Turns the gradual running approach into clear steps and preserves caution.

original: Yes, I'd be happy to help. Which route are you planning to take and when do you want to travel?
revised: Which route do you want to take? What date and time would you like to travel?
note: Asks only for the details needed to help with tickets.

original: Yes, be respectful of those around you. Turn off your phone or put it on silent mode, and avoid talking loudly during the performance. Also, follow the venue's rules about photography and recording.
revised: Put your phone on silent or turn it off. Avoid loud conversations during the music. Follow the venue's rules about photos and recordings. Give the people around you space to enjoy the concert.
note: Splits concert etiquette into clear actions.

original: A magnetic field describes the strength and direction of magnetic effects around an object. Depending on how magnets face each other, they can pull together or push apart.
revised: A magnetic field describes how magnetism acts around an object. It tells us how strong the magnetic effect is and which way it acts. Two magnets may pull together or push apart. The result depends on which ends face each other.
note: Explains strength and direction through two magnets.

original: Voltage is a difference in electrical energy between two points, measured for each unit of charge. Think of water pressure: a pressure difference can make water flow. A voltage difference can help drive electric current. Voltage itself is not a force.
revised: Voltage is a difference in electrical energy between two points. It tells us the energy difference for each unit of electric charge. A voltage difference can help electric current flow. Think of how a difference in water pressure can make water flow. That is a comparison, though: voltage itself is not a force.
note: Breaks down the definition and labels the water comparison.

original: Yes, another strategy you can try is to summarize what you've read after you finish a chapter or section. This can help you make sure you understand the main ideas and can also help you review the material more easily.
revised: After a chapter, write its main idea in your own words. Add a few points that explain it. Then check those points against the text. This can show you what you understood and what needs another look.
note: Turns summarizing into concrete checking steps.

original: Orion has three stars in a row that form its belt. A constellation is a named area of the sky with a familiar star pattern. When you can see Orion depends on where you are and the season. The Big Dipper is another easy pattern, but it belongs to the constellation Ursa Major.
revised: Try looking for Orion's Belt: three bright stars in a row. The belt is part of Orion. A constellation is a named area of sky with a familiar star pattern. Whether you can see Orion depends on your location and the season. The Big Dipper is another familiar pattern. It is part of the constellation Ursa Major.
note: Separates the pattern from the constellation and preserves viewing conditions.

original: A meter and a yard are units of length, but they are not equal. One meter is about 1.09 yards.
revised: Both measure length, but a meter is slightly longer than a yard. One meter is about 1.09 yards.
note: Makes the direction of the size difference explicit.

original: For an emergency preparedness list, consider adding non-perishable food items, bottled water, first aid kit, flashlights, and batteries. It's also a good idea to include a battery-powered radio and extra cash.
revised: Include drinking water and food that keeps without a fridge. Add a first aid kit, flashlights, and spare batteries. A battery-powered radio can help you get updates. Some extra cash may also be useful.
note: Explains non-perishable food in familiar words.

original: Common family celebrations include birthdays, weddings, graduations, holidays, and milestone events like retirement parties.
revised: Families often celebrate birthdays, weddings, holidays, and graduations. They may also mark a big change, such as retirement. Your mom's retirement party is one example.
note: Explains milestone events without jargon.

original: You can try making pasta with tomato sauce, chicken and rice, or lentil soup. They're all quick and delicious.
revised: You could make pasta with tomato sauce, chicken and rice, or lentil soup. Each can be made using one pot. Choose a recipe based on the ingredients and time you have.
note: Separates cooking steps and preserves the cooked-ingredient requirement.

original: Cook the pasta in water according to the packet, then drain it. In the same pot, heat crushed tomatoes with a little olive oil and herbs until the sauce tastes cooked. Return the pasta to the pot and stir it into the sauce.
revised: Cook the pasta in water, following the packet instructions. Drain it and set it aside. In the same pot, heat crushed tomatoes with olive oil and herbs. Let the sauce cook until it tastes ready. Put the pasta back in and stir it through the sauce.
note: Separates cooking steps and preserves the cooked-ingredient requirement.

original: Yes. You can add cooked chicken, cooked sausage, or tofu to the sauce and heat it through. Beans or lentils are other options. Use ingredients that are already cooked or ready to eat, rather than adding raw meat at the end.
revised: Yes. Add cooked chicken, cooked sausage, or ready-to-eat tofu. Heat it through in the sauce. Cooked beans or lentils are other options. Do not add raw meat at the end. It needs proper cooking first.
note: Separates cooking steps and preserves the cooked-ingredient requirement.

original: Some popular sports include football, basketball, tennis, and cricket. They are widely watched and played globally.
revised: Football, basketball, tennis, and cricket are popular examples. Many people around the world play or watch these sports.
note: Uses direct wording without global jargon.

original: Playing music is a great hobby. It can be very relaxing and fun.
revised: You could try playing an instrument. Choose one you enjoy listening to and start with a simple tune. Making music can be relaxing and fun.
note: Adds a concrete first step to the music suggestion.

original: Some common light sources at home are light bulbs, lamps, and televisions.
revised: Light bulbs, lamps, and television screens give off light at home. Sunlight coming through a window is another source.
note: Makes the shared property clear with familiar examples.

original: Granite forms when melted rock, called magma, cools slowly deep underground. This makes it an igneous rock, a rock formed from melted material. It contains visible grains of minerals such as quartz and feldspar.
revised: Granite is a rock that forms deep underground. Melted rock, called magma, cools slowly there. Rocks made from cooled melted material are called igneous rocks. Granite has visible mineral grains. Quartz and feldspar are two minerals often found in it.
note: Explains magma and igneous rock before naming minerals.

original: The Eiffel Tower is a famous iron tower in Paris, France. It was built for the 1889 World's Fair and is one of the most recognizable landmarks in the world.
revised: The Eiffel Tower is a large iron tower in Paris, France. It was built for the 1889 World's Fair. It is now one of the city's best-known landmarks.
note: Splits the location, material, and history into short sentences.

original: A pet can keep you company, reduce stress, and help you meet people. Caring for one can also give you a purpose and encourage you to be more active.
revised: A pet can give you company and a daily routine. Caring for it may help you feel less stressed. Some pets also encourage activity or help you meet people. The benefits depend on the pet and your situation.
note: Explains benefits conditionally and makes first-owner preparation concrete.

original: A pet lives with a person or family as a companion. A therapy animal is trained to comfort other people, often during visits to hospitals or care homes.
revised: A pet lives with a person or family for company. A therapy animal is trained to comfort other people. For example, it may visit people in a hospital or care home.
note: Explains benefits conditionally and makes first-owner preparation concrete.

original: No. First-time owners can give pets a good home. But learn what the animal needs and what caring for it involves before deciding.
revised: No. You can care for a pet even if you have never owned one. First, learn what that animal needs every day. Check that you can provide the time, space, and care it needs.
note: Explains benefits conditionally and makes first-owner preparation concrete.

original: Your body needs protein to build and repair parts such as muscles, bones, and skin. It also uses protein to make enzymes, which speed up chemical reactions, and hormones, which carry messages in the body.
revised: Protein helps your body build and repair muscles, bones, and skin. Your body also uses it to make enzymes and hormones. Enzymes help chemical changes happen in the body. Hormones carry messages between different parts of the body.
note: Explains both necessary biological terms in separate sentences.

original: Check that the store is real, read independent reviews, and use a trusted payment method. HTTPS protects the connection, but a scam website can use HTTPS too. Do not enter payment details just because you see a lock symbol.
revised: Check that the shop is real before you pay. Read reviews on websites outside the shop itself. Use a payment method you trust. HTTPS protects information as it travels between you and the site. But a fake shop can use HTTPS too. A lock symbol alone does not prove the shop is safe.
note: Explains HTTPS and preserves the distinction between connection and shop safety.

original: It's best to avoid using public Wi-Fi for online shopping, as it may not be secure. Instead, use a private and trusted internet connection to protect your personal information.
revised: Use a private internet connection you trust when possible. A public Wi-Fi network may be less safe. Avoid entering payment details if you are unsure about the connection.
note: Explains HTTPS and preserves the distinction between connection and shop safety.

original: You have several options, including hotels, hostels, and homestays. Homestays are a great way to experience local culture and daily life.
revised: You could stay in a hotel, hostel, or homestay. A hostel often has shared rooms, though some have private ones. A homestay means staying in someone's home. It can give you a closer look at local daily life.
note: Explains lodging names rather than only listing them.

original: A stepbrother is your parent’s partner’s son when you do not share a biological parent. A brother who shares one biological parent with you is a half-brother, not a stepbrother.
revised: A stepbrother is the son of your parent's partner. You and your stepbrother do not share a birth parent. A half-brother is different: you share one birth parent with him.
note: Explains the family terms while retaining the condition.

original: If your mother’s husband is the father of your stepbrothers and is not your biological father, he is your stepfather. Family terms can vary, so it is fine to use the wording your family prefers.
revised: If your mom married their father, he may be your stepdad. That assumes he is not also your birth father. Families sometimes use these words differently. You can use the names your family prefers.
note: Explains the family terms while retaining the condition.

original: Great choice. For beginners, I recommend starting with push-ups, squats, lunges, and planks. These exercises work multiple muscle groups and are easy to learn.
revised: Bodyweight exercises use your own weight instead of gym weights. Examples include squats, lunges, push-ups, and planks. A plank means holding your body steady in a straight position. Choose easier versions if the full movements are too hard.
note: Explains reps and sets and avoids fixed exercise demands.

original: Start with a small number of controlled repetitions and a few sessions spread through the week. Choose easier versions when needed, and rest between hard sessions. Add more only when the current amount feels manageable.
revised: A rep is one complete movement. A set is a group of reps. Start with a small number you can do slowly and with control. Try a few sessions spread across the week. Rest between hard sessions. Add more only when the current amount feels manageable.
note: Explains reps and sets and avoids fixed exercise demands.

original: You can use a fitness app or a workout log to track your progress. Set achievable goals and reward yourself when you reach them. Also, find a workout buddy or join a fitness community for motivation and support.
revised: Write down what you did after each workout. A notebook or fitness app can help. Choose a small goal you can reach. Notice when the same exercise starts to feel easier. Exercising with someone else may help you keep going.
note: Explains reps and sets and avoids fixed exercise demands.

original: Yes, some popular online cooking channels include Binging with Babish, Tasty, and Gordon Ramsay's channel.
revised: Examples include Binging with Babish, Tasty, and Gordon Ramsay's cooking channel. Browse their recipes and choose one that matches your skill level.
note: Keeps named examples without claiming a current ranking.

original: Five miles is about 8.05 kilometers. Multiply 5 by about 1.609 to convert miles to kilometers.
revised: Five miles is about 8.05 kilometers. To convert miles to kilometers, multiply by about 1.609. Here, 5 times 1.609 gives 8.045, which rounds to 8.05.
note: Shows the conversion step behind the answer.

original: Congratulations on your new home! Common housewarming party activities include a BBQ or potluck, giving tours of the new home, and having a small ceremony to mark the new beginning.
revised: You could invite people for a barbecue or shared meal. At a potluck, each guest brings a dish to share. You might also show guests around your new home. Some families include a small ceremony to mark the move.
note: Explains potluck and avoids implying all families share the same holidays.

original: Some popular family celebrations include birthdays, holidays like Christmas or Thanksgiving, and milestones like graduations or weddings.
revised: Birthdays, weddings, and graduations are common family celebrations. Families may also celebrate holidays such as Christmas or Thanksgiving. The celebrations depend on the family's culture and traditions.
note: Explains potluck and avoids implying all families share the same holidays.

original: Smaller, regular family gatherings like weekend dinners can be just as special and are a great way to bond and create lasting memories with your loved ones.
revised: A weekend dinner can be a celebration too. It gives everyone time to talk and enjoy a meal together. A gathering does not need to be large to feel special.
note: Explains potluck and avoids implying all families share the same holidays.

original: Authoritarian parents are strict and expect children to follow rules. Permissive parents set fewer limits and give more freedom. Authoritative parents combine clear rules with warmth and care for the child's feelings.
revised: Three common names are authoritarian, permissive, and authoritative parenting. Authoritarian parents set strict rules and expect children to obey. Permissive parents set fewer limits and allow more freedom. Authoritative parents combine clear rules with warmth. They also listen to the child's feelings.
note: Keeps the names while explaining each in plain words.

original: The key factors that affect the quality of work include setting clear goals, managing your time effectively, staying organized, and minimizing distractions.
revised: Start by making the goal clear: what should good work look like? Plan time for the main tasks. Keep your materials and notes easy to find. Reduce distractions while you work. These habits can help you do more careful work.
note: Replaces abstract performance factors with actions.

original: Yes, consider wearing lightweight, breathable fabrics like cotton, linen, or bamboo. They allow for airflow and can help keep you cool.
revised: Try loose clothes made from light fabrics, such as cotton or linen. Clothes that let air move through can feel cooler. Check the fabric and fit, rather than relying only on a label like bamboo.
note: Explains breathable clothing and avoids promising all bamboo-labelled fabrics perform alike.

original: Look for a product made for your pet’s species and skin needs, with clear instructions. Refillable packaging or durable grooming tools can reduce waste, but natural ingredients do not automatically make a product safer.
revised: Choose grooming products made for your type of pet and its skin needs. Follow the instructions on the label. Refill packs may reduce packaging waste. Strong brushes and other tools can last longer. Natural ingredients do not automatically make a product safe.
note: Explains waste reduction while preserving pet suitability and safety limits.

original: Some popular family celebration ideas include hosting a backyard barbecue, having a dinner at a favorite restaurant, or organizing a weekend getaway. You could also consider having a game night or a movie night with close family and friends.
revised: You could have a backyard barbecue or a meal at a favorite restaurant. A game night or movie night is another option. For a longer celebration, consider a weekend trip. Choose something that suits your family's interests and budget.
note: Uses clear choices and a relevant condition.

original: Choose a plant that suits the light and climate where you will grow it. Some herbs or compact flowering plants can be good starting points. Tomatoes need sun and regular care, while many succulents need strong light and careful watering.
revised: Choose a plant that suits your weather and the light you have. Some herbs or small flowering plants can be a good start. Tomatoes need plenty of sun and regular care. Succulents store water in thick leaves or stems. Many need strong light and careful watering.
note: Explains plant terms and turns design advice into steps.

original: Start by thinking about how you want to use your space. Do you want a patio for entertaining, a garden for relaxation, or a play area for kids? Then, sketch out a rough layout and consider the sunlight, soil, and existing features in your yard.
revised: First, decide how you want to use the yard. You might want room to sit, grow plants, or play. Draw a simple plan on paper. Mark sunny and shady areas. Also note the soil and anything you want to keep.
note: Explains plant terms and turns design advice into steps.

original: Yes, consider using vertical planters, hanging baskets, or compact varieties of plants. These can help maximize your space and still allow you to enjoy gardening.
revised: Grow plants in pots, hanging baskets, or planters fixed above the ground. These let you use different parts of a small space. Choose plant varieties that stay small. Check that each plant still gets the light it needs.
note: Explains plant terms and turns design advice into steps.

original: Progressive muscle relaxation is a technique where you tense and then relax different muscle groups in your body to release physical tension and calm your mind.
revised: Progressive muscle relaxation means tightening and then relaxing muscles in turn. You work through different parts of your body. This can help you notice and release tension. It may also help you feel calmer.
note: Explains the relaxation method while preserving gentle practice limits.

original: Sit or lie comfortably and gently tense one muscle group for a few seconds, then release it and notice the difference. Keep breathing normally. Skip injured or painful areas and avoid straining.
revised: Sit or lie in a comfortable position. Gently tighten one group of muscles for a few seconds. Let go and notice how the muscles feel. Keep breathing normally. Skip painful or injured areas, and do not strain.
note: Explains the relaxation method while preserving gentle practice limits.

original: A good morning routine often includes a consistent wake-up time, some stretching or light exercise, and a healthy breakfast to give you energy.
revised: Try getting up at the same time each day. Start with a gentle stretch or a little movement. Have breakfast if it suits your routine. Keep the plan simple enough to repeat on busy mornings.
note: Turns routine advice into manageable actions without guaranteed effects.

original: The main difference is size and purpose. Commercial airliners are large planes that carry many passengers, while private jets are smaller and usually used for personal or business travel with a few passengers.
revised: An airliner carries passengers on airline flights. These planes are often large and carry many people. A private jet usually carries a smaller group for personal or business travel. Size is a common difference, but the purpose matters too.
note: Avoids making size an absolute distinction.

original: Relaxed fit clothing is very popular for comfort. You can consider sweatpants, hoodies, or oversized t-shirts.
revised: Look for clothes with a loose, comfortable fit. Sweatpants, hoodies, and roomy T-shirts are common choices. Choose fabric that feels comfortable against your skin.
note: Explains relaxed fit in familiar words.

original: Cats need things to do with both their minds and bodies. Try a puzzle toy with treats inside or a safe climbing structure.
revised: Give your cat things to explore, play with, and climb. A puzzle toy can hide treats for her to find. A safe climbing structure can also keep her active.
note: Makes enrichment ideas concrete and avoids treating digging as always boredom.

original: Dogs may dig because they are bored or have energy to use. More walks and play may help. Your friend could also try games that involve following scents or moving through obstacles.
revised: Some dogs dig because they are bored or have energy to use. More walks and play may help. Your friend could try a game where the dog follows a scent. Simple obstacle games are another option. Digging can have other causes too.
note: Makes enrichment ideas concrete and avoids treating digging as always boredom.

original: Yes, one key tip is to rotate toys regularly to keep things interesting for your pet. You can also try hiding treats or toys around the house to encourage searching and problem-solving.
revised: Put some toys away and swap them with others later. This can make old toys interesting again. You can also hide suitable treats or toys for your pet to find. Choose hiding places and games that are safe for that animal.
note: Makes enrichment ideas concrete and avoids treating digging as always boredom.

original: The New York City subway map is a complex network of lines and stations. It's usually color-coded to help you navigate. You can find maps at most subway stations or download a subway app on your phone.
revised: The subway map shows train routes and stations across New York City. Colors help group the routes. Look for your starting station and the station you want to reach. You can view a map at many stations or save one on your phone.
note: Explains the map and MTA while retaining availability limits.

original: The MTA provides visitor information and language help, but the available map versions can change. Check its official website for the languages and formats you need.
revised: The MTA runs the subway and offers visitor information and language help. Available map versions can change. Check the official MTA website for the language and format you need.
note: Explains the map and MTA while retaining availability limits.

original: Ask station staff or check an MTA customer service location. Printed copies may not be available everywhere, so saving the official map on your phone is a useful backup.
revised: Ask station staff or an MTA customer service office. They may have paper maps, but copies are not available everywhere. Save the official map on your phone as a backup.
note: Explains the map and MTA while retaining availability limits.

original: Attackers can trick people with fake messages, harmful apps, or stolen passwords. Outdated software can also have weaknesses. I would not name one route as the most common without current evidence.
revised: Attackers may use fake messages, harmful apps, or stolen passwords. Older software can also have security weaknesses. I cannot reliably name one method as the most common without current evidence.
note: Uses concrete protection steps and explains the limit of a VPN.

original: Keep the phone and apps updated, use a strong screen lock, and check links before opening them. Get apps from trusted sources and review their permissions. A VPN does not protect you from every scam or harmful app.
revised: Keep your phone and apps updated. Use a strong screen lock. Check links before opening them. Download apps from sources you trust, and check what they can access. A VPN protects some network traffic, but it cannot stop every scam or harmful app.
note: Uses concrete protection steps and explains the limit of a VPN.

original: Yes, that's a great idea. Using a strong password, fingerprint, or facial recognition can add an extra layer of security to prevent unauthorized access to your phone.
revised: Yes. A strong passcode helps stop other people from opening your phone. A fingerprint or face lock can help too. Set up the lock options your phone supports.
note: Uses concrete protection steps and explains the limit of a VPN.

original: Practice separating a claim from the evidence for it. Ask what is known, what is assumed, and what other explanation might fit. Listening carefully helps you understand the claim before judging it.
revised: Focus on checking what supports a claim. A claim is something someone says is true. Ask what evidence supports it and what is only a guess. Then consider whether another explanation could fit. Listen carefully before deciding.
note: Explains claim and turns critical thinking into questions.

original: Some popular types of pies include apple, pumpkin, cherry, and chocolate cream.
revised: Some popular types of pies include apple, pumpkin, cherry, and chocolate cream.
note: Already a clear short list answering the question.

original: Yes, make sure to wear bright or reflective clothing, especially in low light conditions, and follow traffic rules and signals. It's also a good idea to stay aware of your surroundings and avoid distractions like using your phone while walking.
revised: Wear bright or reflective clothing, especially when it is dark. Reflective material shines back light from car headlights. Follow traffic signals and use safe crossing places. Look around you as you walk. Put your phone away when it distracts you.
note: Explains reflective material and separates walking precautions.

original: Yes, you can try making a vinaigrette with olive oil, lemon juice, and herbs like basil or cilantro. It's a simple and tasty option that's naturally gluten-free.
revised: You can mix olive oil, lemon juice, and herbs for a simple dressing. Basil or cilantro can add flavor. Plain versions of these ingredients do not contain gluten. Check labels on any prepared mixtures you use.
note: Explains vinaigrette in everyday words and keeps ingredient checking relevant.

original: A pressure cooker traps steam in a sealed pot. The higher pressure lets water get hotter than it does in an open pot, so many foods cook faster.
revised: A pressure cooker keeps steam inside a sealed pot. This raises the pressure inside. The water can then get hotter than in an open pot. That extra heat helps many foods cook faster.
note: Breaks the cause and effect into short sentences.

original: Networking is a great way to advance your career. You can start by attending industry events, joining professional organizations, and connecting with people on LinkedIn.
revised: Networking means getting to know people connected to your work. You could attend an event for your field or join a professional group. Introduce yourself and ask about other people's work. You can also make contacts on LinkedIn.
note: Explains networking through concrete social actions.

original: Visual merchandising means arranging products so they look appealing and catch shoppers' attention. It includes displays in shop windows and inside the shop.
revised: Visual merchandising means arranging products to catch a shopper's attention. A shop might put matching clothes together in a window. It can also use displays inside the store. The aim is to make products appealing and easy to notice.
note: Explains the retail term with a labelled example.

original: Yes, there are many adaptive sports options. Some popular ones include wheelchair basketball, adaptive skiing, and para-swimming. These sports are designed to be inclusive and accessible for people with different abilities.
revised: Adaptive sports change rules or equipment to suit different needs. Examples include wheelchair basketball, adapted skiing, and para-swimming. The right choice depends on the person and the support available.
note: Explains adaptive sports and keeps suitability individual.

original: Options may include seated exercise classes, adapted resistance exercises, or wheelchair sports. The right choice depends on the person's movement, comfort, and goals. A coach with experience in adapted exercise can help choose suitable activities.
revised: Options include seated exercise classes and wheelchair sports. Some strength exercises can also be adapted. Choose movements that suit the person's comfort, abilities, and goals. A coach experienced in adapted exercise can help.
note: Explains adaptive sports and keeps suitability individual.

original: During hibernation, an animal's body slows down and uses much less energy. Its temperature and activity can drop for long periods when food is hard to find. This is more than normal sleep.
revised: Hibernation is a state in which an animal uses much less energy. Its body slows down, and its temperature may drop. It can stay less active for long periods when food is scarce. This is different from ordinary sleep.
note: Explains hibernation and preserves the sleep distinction.

original: What are her interests? Does she like reading, shopping, or something else?
revised: What are her interests? Does she like reading, shopping, or something else?
note: Preserves the useful preference question and makes gift suggestions direct.

original: In that case, you could consider gifting her a gift card to her favorite clothing store, a fashion magazine subscription, or a beautiful piece of jewelry.
revised: You could give her a gift card for her favorite clothing store. A fashion magazine subscription or a piece of jewelry could also work. Choose something that matches her taste.
note: Preserves the useful preference question and makes gift suggestions direct.

original: You can start with a mouse or a device you already own, though a pressure-sensitive pen often makes drawing easier. Some drawing tablets have screens; others connect to a computer and control the pointer on a separate screen.
revised: No. You can start with a mouse or a device you already have. A drawing pen can make it easier to control your lines. Some pens also respond to how hard you press. Some drawing tablets have a screen. Others connect to a computer, where you watch a separate screen as you draw.
note: Answers the need question directly and explains tablet types.

original: That sounds fun! You could consider going for a hike, having a picnic, or playing a game of soccer or flag football.
revised: You could go for a walk or hike, have a picnic, or play soccer. Flag football is another option. Choose an activity that suits your family's interests and abilities.
note: Review fix: the opening user message mentions family, not children; later child-specific advice stays in the follow-up.

original: Some leagues have playful beginner sessions for preschool or early primary-school children. Check local age groups and look for a program that matches your children’s interest and readiness.
revised: Some leagues offer playful sessions for preschool and early school-age children. Check the age groups at your local club. Look for a class that suits your children's interest and readiness.
note: Keeps age guidance conditional and avoids assuming a league was chosen.

original: You're welcome! I hope you and your family have a great time at the soccer league.
revised: You're welcome. I hope your family enjoys the outing.
note: Keeps age guidance conditional and avoids assuming a league was chosen.

original: Some popular types of desserts include cakes, cookies, pies, and chocolates. Do you have a specific preference?
revised: Cakes, cookies, pies, and chocolate are popular sweet choices. Which of those sounds best to you?
note: Uses familiar examples and a relevant preference question.

original: There are many types, including wall-mounted, floor-to-ceiling, and corner cabinets. What kind of storage are you looking for?
revised: You can choose cabinets fixed to a wall, tall cabinets, or corner cabinets. What do you want to store in them?
note: Avoids a single guaranteed best option and retains practical support needs.

original: A wall-mounted cabinet with shelves would be a great option. It will keep your items organized and add a decorative touch to your room.
revised: A cabinet with shelves could work for books and decorations. A wall-mounted one can save floor space. Make sure the cabinet and its fixings can support the weight of your books.
note: Avoids a single guaranteed best option and retains practical support needs.

original: Waste from factories and chemicals used in farming can pollute soil. These include pesticides, which control pests, and fertilisers. Pollution can harm plants and animals.
revised: Factory waste and farming chemicals can pollute soil. Pesticides are chemicals used to control pests. Fertilizers help plants grow, but too much can also cause harm. Soil pollution can hurt plants and animals.
note: Explains chemical terms and connects prevention to sources.

original: Yes. Polluted soil can harm crops, make underground water unsafe, and affect people's health.
revised: Yes. Polluted soil can damage crops and affect people's health. Pollution may also reach water underground and make it unsafe.
note: Explains chemical terms and connects prevention to sources.

original: We can use farming methods that cause less harm, use fewer chemicals, and dispose of factory waste safely.
revised: Use farming methods that need fewer harmful chemicals. Apply necessary chemicals carefully. Factories must handle and dispose of waste safely. These steps can help keep pollution out of the soil.
note: Explains chemical terms and connects prevention to sources.

original: Plein air painting is a type of outdoor painting where artists paint landscapes and scenes directly from nature, usually in natural light.
revised: Plein air painting means painting outdoors. You look directly at a real scene, such as a garden or landscape. You usually work in natural daylight.
note: Explains the French term and avoids making extra equipment mandatory.

original: Not at all. You'll need some basic painting supplies like a portable easel, paints, and brushes. You can start by practicing simple exercises and gradually move on to more complex scenes.
revised: You can begin with a small set of paints, brushes, and a surface to paint on. A portable easel can help hold your work, but it is not always needed. Start with a simple scene and build your skills with practice.
note: Explains the French term and avoids making extra equipment mandatory.

original: Yes, start by choosing a simple location with good lighting, and don't be afraid to make mistakes. Practice regularly, and you'll see improvement over time.
revised: Choose a simple subject in a place with enough light. Paint the main shapes first. You do not need to capture every detail. Treat mistakes as part of practice, and try again regularly.
note: Explains the French term and avoids making extra equipment mandatory.

original: Yes, I can definitely help you with that. You can try stretching your neck by gently tilting your head to the side, or rolling your shoulders to loosen them up.
revised: Try gently tilting your head to one side, then the other. You can also slowly roll your shoulders. Keep the movements comfortable. Stop if a movement hurts.
note: Turns break suggestions into gentle concrete actions.

original: Taking a short walk outside or doing some deep breathing exercises can be great ways to clear your mind and come back to your work feeling more focused.
revised: Take a short walk if you can. Or pause for a few slow, comfortable breaths. A brief change from your desk may help you return with a clearer mind.
note: Turns break suggestions into gentle concrete actions.

original: Some popular board games include Monopoly, Scrabble, and Chess. They're classics and enjoyed by many people.
revised: Monopoly, Scrabble, and chess are familiar choices. Monopoly involves buying and trading property. Scrabble is a word game. Chess is a strategy game played by two people.
note: Explains what each named game involves.

original: No, there are many other examples of wedges, such as knives, doorstops, and shovels. Any object with a narrow edge that is used to separate or push things apart can be considered a wedge.
revised: No. Knives and doorstops are other examples. A wedge has a thin edge that widens behind it. Pushing that edge into a space can separate things or hold them apart. An axe uses this shape to split wood.
note: Explains the wedge shape and effect with familiar examples.

original: There are many types, such as Italian, Chinese, Mexican, and Indian restaurants. You can also find fast-food places, cafes, or buffets.
revised: Some restaurants focus on a cooking tradition, such as Italian, Chinese, Mexican, or Indian food. Others are fast-food places, cafes, or buffets. These differ in both food and how you are served.
note: Explains buffet serving and keeps pricing and variety conditional.

original: At a buffet, food is set out so you can choose and serve yourself. Some buffets charge one fixed price for as much as you want. Others charge by plate or by weight, so check before taking food.
revised: At a buffet, dishes are set out for you to choose from. You serve yourself. Some charge one price for as much food as you want. Others charge by the plate or by weight. Check the price rules before taking food.
note: Explains buffet serving and keeps pricing and variety conditional.

original: Yes, buffets often have a wide variety of food options, including salads, soups, main courses, and desserts. They can be a good choice if you want to try a little bit of everything.
revised: Often, yes. A buffet may have salads, soups, main dishes, and desserts. This lets you try small amounts of different foods. The choice depends on the restaurant.
note: Explains buffet serving and keeps pricing and variety conditional.

original: The biggest planet in our solar system is Jupiter. It's a gas giant and is much larger than Earth.
revised: Jupiter is the biggest planet in our solar system. It is much larger than Earth. It is called a gas giant because it is made mostly of gas.
note: Explains gas giant immediately.

original: Look for a beginner class from a qualified dance-fitness instructor, including official Zumba resources. Check the pace and choose a lesson with easier movement options.
revised: Look for an online beginner class from a trained dance-fitness instructor. Official Zumba resources are one place to start. Check how fast the class moves. Choose one that offers easier versions of the movements.
note: Makes class suitability checks concrete.

original: You can book a rental car through the company's website, mobile app, or by calling their customer service number.
revised: Use the rental company's official website or app. You can also call its customer service team to book.
note: Keeps the booking answer short and direct.

original: The main app stores are the Apple App Store for iOS devices and the Google Play Store for Android devices.
revised: Apple devices such as iPhones use the Apple App Store. Most Android phones use the Google Play Store. Your device determines which store you can use.
note: Explains the device names and avoids treating all Android devices alike.

original: Some popular music streaming platforms include Spotify, Apple Music, and Amazon Music. They all offer a wide selection of songs and playlists.
revised: Spotify, Apple Music, and Amazon Music are examples. They let you listen to music over the internet. Each offers many songs and playlists.
note: Explains streaming and discovery tools while retaining a short farewell.

original: Look for discovery playlists, artist radio, and recommendations you can tune with likes or skips. Spotify is one example, but other services also offer discovery tools. Try the features with music you know to see which suits you.
revised: Look for playlists that suggest music you do not already know. Some services also play music similar to an artist you choose. Spotify has tools like these, as do other services. Try them with music you like and see which suggestions suit you.
note: Explains streaming and discovery tools while retaining a short farewell.

original: You're welcome! Enjoy exploring Spotify and discovering new music.
revised: You're welcome! Enjoy exploring Spotify and discovering new music.
note: Explains streaming and discovery tools while retaining a short farewell.

original: Yes, I do. Joining professional associations related to your field is a great way to meet and connect with others who share similar interests and goals.
revised: Join a professional group for people in your field. Attend a meeting or event and introduce yourself. Ask people about their work. This can help you meet others with similar interests.
note: Turns networking into concrete actions.

original: Air traffic control is a service that guides planes safely through takeoff, landing, and flying, making sure they don't collide with each other.
revised: Air traffic control helps guide aircraft safely. Controllers give pilots instructions during takeoff, flight, and landing. They help keep aircraft far enough apart to avoid collisions.
note: Explains the service through what controllers do.

original: The main difference is texture. Chocolate pudding is smooth and creamy, while chocolate mousse is light and airy, often made with whipped cream.
revised: The main difference is how they feel when you eat them. Pudding is smooth and creamy. Mousse is lighter because it contains tiny air bubbles. Whipped cream is often used to give mousse that airy texture.
note: Explains texture and airy mousse in familiar words.

original: Cultural exchange programs allow people to visit and live in another country, immersing themselves in the local culture and customs. It's a great way to learn about a new culture and share your own with others.
revised: A cultural exchange program lets people spend time in another country. They learn about local life, customs, and beliefs. Some live with a host family. They can also share things about their own culture.
note: Explains cultural exchange without the term immersion.

original: You can try using earplugs, white noise machines, or soundproofing materials for your windows and walls. These can help reduce the outside noise and create a more peaceful environment for sleep.
revised: Earplugs may reduce the noise you hear. A white-noise machine makes a steady sound that can cover other noises. Materials added to windows or walls may also reduce outside sound. These options can help, but may not block every noise.
note: Explains white noise and avoids promising full soundproofing.

original: There are several main types of music, including classical, jazz, rock, pop, and folk. Each type has its own unique style and sound.
revised: Common types include classical, jazz, rock, pop, and folk music. Each name covers a range of sounds and styles.
note: Explains playwright and preserves the overlap between plays and musicals.

original: A play usually tells its story mainly through spoken dialogue and action. A musical uses songs as a major part of telling the story, often with dance too. A play can still include some music or singing.
revised: A play usually tells a story through speech and action. A musical also uses songs to tell important parts of the story. It often includes dancing. A play can still have some music or singing.
note: Explains playwright and preserves the overlap between plays and musicals.

original: Some famous playwrights include William Shakespeare, known for plays like Romeo and Juliet, and Oscar Wilde, known for plays like The Importance of Being Earnest.
revised: A playwright is someone who writes plays. William Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet. Oscar Wilde wrote The Importance of Being Earnest. Both are well-known playwrights.
note: Explains playwright and preserves the overlap between plays and musicals.

original: Yes, sneakers are always a great option for casual wear. What's your favorite brand or style?
revised: Sneakers can be a comfortable choice for everyday wear. Do you have a brand or style you already like?
note: Explains canvas and preserves the need to compare individual models.

original: Converse is associated with classic canvas sneakers, Vans with skate shoes, and Adidas with sportswear and sneakers. Each brand has many styles, so those are broad associations. Compare the individual shoes for fit, support, and comfort.
revised: Converse is known for classic canvas sneakers. Canvas is a strong cloth. Vans is often linked with skate shoes, while Adidas makes sports shoes and casual sneakers. Each brand has many different models. Compare the actual shoes for fit, support, and comfort.
note: Explains canvas and preserves the need to compare individual models.

original: Yes, there are many fun pet toys available. You can try squeaky chew toys, plush toys, or interactive puzzle toys.
revised: You could try a chew toy, soft toy, or puzzle toy. A puzzle toy lets your dog work out how to find a treat. Choose toys suited to your dog's size and chewing habits.
note: Explains toys through play steps and keeps swallowing warnings.

original: You could hide a few treats in a clean cardboard box for a supervised search game. Choose a simple activity suited to your dog, and stop if the dog starts chewing off and swallowing pieces. Homemade toys are not automatically safe.
revised: You could hide a few treats in a clean cardboard box. Let your dog search while you watch. Stop the game if your dog tears off and swallows pieces. A homemade toy is not automatically safe.
note: Explains toys through play steps and keeps swallowing warnings.

original: Try placing a treat under one of two sturdy cups, then let your dog find it while you watch. Avoid loose stuffing, small parts, and brittle plastic that a dog could swallow. Put the materials away after the game.
revised: Hide a treat under one of two sturdy cups. Let your dog find it while you watch. Avoid small parts, loose filling, or plastic that breaks easily. Your dog could swallow those pieces. Put the cups away when the game ends.
note: Explains toys through play steps and keeps swallowing warnings.

original: Common systems use door and window sensors, motion detectors, and an alarm. Some send phone alerts or connect to a monitoring service. Police notification depends on the service and local arrangements; it is not automatic for every system.
revised: Many systems use sensors on doors and windows. A sensor notices when something changes, such as a door opening. Motion detectors notice movement, and an alarm makes a warning sound. Some systems also send alerts to your phone or a monitoring service. They do not all notify the police automatically.
note: Explains system parts and avoids guaranteed crime prevention.

original: Yes, security cameras can be very useful. They can deter intruders, provide evidence if a crime occurs, and allow you to monitor your home remotely.
revised: Cameras can let you check your home when you are away. Their recordings may provide evidence if a crime happens. A visible camera may also discourage someone from entering. But a camera does not prevent every break-in.
note: Explains system parts and avoids guaranteed crime prevention.

original: If you're not comfortable with the installation process, it's recommended to hire a professional. They can ensure the system is installed correctly and provide guidance on how to use it effectively.
revised: Hire an installer if you are unsure how to fit the system. They can help position and connect the equipment correctly. Ask them to show you how to use it and check that it works.
note: Explains system parts and avoids guaranteed crime prevention.

original: Some popular smartphone brands include Apple, Samsung, and Google. They offer a range of models with different features and price points.
revised: Apple, Samsung, and Google are examples of smartphone brands. Each sells models with different features and prices.
note: Explains operating system and app permissions.

original: The main difference is the operating system - iPhones run on iOS, while Samsung phones run on Android. This affects the user interface, app selection, and overall user experience.
revised: The main difference is the software that runs the phone. This is called its operating system. iPhones use iOS, while Samsung phones use Android. That affects the menus, settings, and apps you can use.
note: Explains operating system and app permissions.

original: Start with only the apps you actually need, such as messaging, maps, banking, or work tools. Social media is optional. Use the official app store and check permissions before adding more.
revised: Start with apps you need for everyday tasks. These might include messages, maps, banking, or work tools. You do not have to add social media apps. Use the official app store. Check what each app wants permission to access.
note: Explains operating system and app permissions.

original: Earthy tones like olive green, terracotta, and mustard yellow are popular for fall. You can also incorporate rich jewel tones like emerald green and navy blue.
revised: Olive green, warm orange-brown, and mustard yellow are common autumn choices. Dark green and navy blue can also suit the season. Choose colors you enjoy wearing.
note: Replaces unexplained color-family terms with familiar colors.

original: Sit with one leg extended and the other bent. Keeping your back comfortable, lean forward from the hips until you feel a gentle pull behind the thigh. Do not force your toes to be reached or continue through pain.
revised: Sit with one leg straight and the other bent. Lean forward gently from your hips. Stop when you feel a mild stretch behind your thigh. Keep your back comfortable. You do not need to reach your toes, and the stretch should not hurt.
note: Breaks the stretch into steps and preserves pain limits.

original: Air traffic controllers are trained professionals. Some work in airport towers, while others work in control centers that guide aircraft between airports. They use communication and tracking systems to help keep aircraft safely separated.
revised: Trained air traffic controllers do this work. Some work in airport towers. Others work in control centers between airports. They track aircraft and talk to pilots. Their instructions help keep aircraft safely apart.
note: Explains the work with concrete verbs.

original: Magnetic levitation, or maglev, uses magnetic forces to lift something and hold it in the air without touching it.
revised: Magnetic levitation means using magnets to lift something without touching it. Magnetic forces can also hold the object in the air. The short name is maglev.
note: Explains the term before giving its abbreviation.

original: Reading is a great hobby. You can explore different genres, learn new things, and escape into different worlds.
revised: You could try reading. Choose stories or a subject that interests you. Books can help you learn, relax, or imagine different places and lives.
note: Explains reading benefits without unexplained metaphors.

original: Well-known literary awards include the Pulitzer Prize, the National Book Award, and the Booker Prize. Looking through past winners can help you find books to try.
revised: Examples include the Pulitzer Prize, the National Book Award, and the Booker Prize. These awards recognize books and other writing. Past winners can give you ideas for what to read.
note: Explains journalism and replaces blanket praise with a reading step.

original: The Pulitzer Prize is an annual award that recognizes outstanding work in journalism, literature, and music. In literature, it awards fiction and nonfiction books, as well as poetry and drama.
revised: The Pulitzer Prizes are given each year for work in journalism, writing, and music. Journalism means reporting news and information. Writing categories include fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and plays.
note: Explains journalism and replaces blanket praise with a reading step.

original: That's a great idea! Many Pulitzer Prize-winning books are considered classics and are definitely worth reading.
revised: The list of past winners is a useful place to start. Read a short description of each book to find one that interests you.
note: Explains journalism and replaces blanket praise with a reading step.

original: Of course, I'd be happy to help. What subjects do you have homework in and what are the deadlines for each assignment?
revised: Which subjects do you have homework for? For each task, tell me when it is due. Then we can put the work in order.
note: Asks for the exact information needed to organize homework.

original: Window displays are meant to showcase products and attract customers into the store. They're also a form of advertising and can be very visually appealing.
revised: A window display shows products to people passing the shop. It aims to catch their attention and make them want to come inside. It also advertises the shop and what it sells.
note: Explains the display's purpose directly.

original: People can differ in how directly they state a request, how they show respect, and how much background they expect others to know. Culture can influence these habits, but personality and setting matter too. Direct speech can still be polite.
revised: People may make requests in different ways. Some speak directly, while others give more background or hints. Ways of showing respect can also differ. Culture may influence these habits, but personality and the situation matter too. Direct speech can still be polite.
note: Separates cultural influences and avoids rigid group rules.

original: There are mainly two types: wired and wireless keyboards. Wired keyboards connect directly to your computer, while wireless keyboards use Bluetooth or a USB receiver.
revised: One choice is between a wired and a wireless keyboard. A wired keyboard connects with a cable. A wireless keyboard usually connects through Bluetooth or a small USB receiver. The receiver plugs into the computer.
note: Explains connections without claiming they are the only keyboard types.

original: It depends on your preference. Wired keyboards are generally more reliable and don't require battery replacements, but wireless keyboards offer more flexibility and convenience.
revised: Choose a wired keyboard if you want a cable connection without battery charging. A wireless keyboard gives you more freedom to place it. But it needs batteries or charging. The better choice depends on how you use your desk.
note: Explains connections without claiming they are the only keyboard types.

original: There is no standard bone called the fastest. If you mean the longest bone, that is the femur in the thigh. Bones grow at different rates depending on age and the part of the body.
revised: There is no standard name for a fastest bone. If you mean the longest bone, it is the femur in your thigh. If you mean bone growth, different bones grow at different rates. Age affects that growth too.
note: Explains puberty and keeps variation in growth timing.

original: A major growth spurt often happens during puberty, but the timing varies a lot. It tends to begin earlier in girls than in boys, and not everyone grows at the same pace.
revised: A major growth spurt often happens during puberty. Puberty is when a child's body starts changing toward an adult body. The spurt often begins earlier in girls than in boys. But the timing varies widely from person to person.
note: Explains puberty and keeps variation in growth timing.

original: You can take care of your bones by eating a balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D, exercising regularly, and getting enough sleep. This will help your bones grow strong and healthy.
revised: Eat a varied diet that includes calcium and vitamin D. These nutrients help support your bones. Regular movement and enough sleep matter too. Together, these habits help support healthy growth.
note: Explains puberty and keeps variation in growth timing.

original: A carnivore eats mainly animals, like a lion. An herbivore eats mainly plants, like a cow. An omnivore eats both, like a human or a brown bear.
revised: A carnivore mainly eats other animals. A lion is one example. An herbivore mainly eats plants, like a cow. An omnivore eats both plants and animals. Humans and brown bears are examples of omnivores.
note: Corrects the user's only interpretation while preserving species differences.

original: Many bears, such as brown and black bears, eat a mix of plant and animal foods. What they eat changes with the species, season, and location. They do not need to be hunting all the time.
revised: Carnivore means mainly animal food; it does not always mean only animal food. Many bears eat both plants and animals. Their food choices depend on the type of bear, season, and place. Brown and black bears do not hunt all the time.
note: Corrects the user's only interpretation while preserving species differences.

original: Brown bears and black bears are good examples. Bears are not all alike: polar bears eat mostly animal food, while giant pandas eat mainly bamboo.
revised: Brown bears and black bears are good examples. But not every bear eats the same way. Polar bears mostly eat animal food. Giant pandas mostly eat bamboo.
note: Corrects the user's only interpretation while preserving species differences.

original: Crossed arms do not have one fixed meaning. Someone may be cold, comfortable, thinking, or feeling defensive. Look at the situation and listen to what they say instead of drawing a conclusion from one gesture.
revised: Crossed arms do not have one fixed meaning. A person may be cold, comfortable, thinking, or feeling defensive. Defensive means they feel a need to protect themselves. Look at the situation and listen to their words too.
note: Explains defensive and preserves uncertainty in body-language interpretation.

original: Avoiding eye contact can have many reasons, including comfort, culture, concentration, or nervousness. It is not reliable evidence that someone is dishonest.
revised: There are many possible reasons. A person may feel nervous, prefer less eye contact, or be concentrating. Their culture can also matter. Looking away does not reliably show that someone is lying.
note: Explains defensive and preserves uncertainty in body-language interpretation.

original: Give the speaker your attention, let them finish, and ask a relevant follow-up question. Eye contact or nodding can help when comfortable, but listening matters more than copying a fixed gesture.
revised: Give the speaker your attention and let them finish. Ask a question about what they said. You can nod or make eye contact if that feels comfortable. Careful listening matters more than using a particular gesture.
