note: Explains defensive and preserves uncertainty in body-language interpretation.

original: Key factors for improving job performance include setting clear goals, prioritizing tasks, and maintaining open communication with your team.
revised: Make your work goals clear. Decide which tasks matter most and do those first. Keep your team informed about progress and problems. Ask questions when an instruction is unclear.
note: Turns work-performance factors into actions.

original: Each drum has a stretched skin over a large bowl. A pedal changes the tension of the skin, which changes the note it makes. Players often use several drums tuned to different notes.
revised: A timpani drum has a large bowl with a tight skin stretched over it. Pressing a pedal changes how tightly the skin is stretched. That changes the note you hear. Players often use several drums, each set to a different note.
note: Explains tension and tuning without assuming musical vocabulary.

original: One strategy is to set specific, achievable goals, like exercising for 30 minutes, 3 times a week. Having a clear plan can help you stay on track.
revised: Choose a small, clear goal that fits your current ability. For example, you might plan a 30-minute session three times a week. Start with less if that is too much. Write down when you plan to exercise.
note: Labels the schedule as an example and makes consistency concrete.

original: Tracking your progress and celebrating small victories can be very effective. You can use a fitness app or journal to monitor your progress and reward yourself when you reach milestones.
revised: Keep a simple record of what you do. A notebook or fitness app can help. Notice small changes, such as an exercise feeling easier. Mark those improvements so you can see your progress.
note: Labels the schedule as an example and makes consistency concrete.

original: Consistency is key. Focus on making healthy habits a part of your daily routine, rather than trying to make drastic changes that might not stick.
revised: Focus on habits you can repeat. A small routine you keep doing is useful. Large, sudden changes can be harder to maintain. Choose a plan that fits your daily life.
note: Labels the schedule as an example and makes consistency concrete.

original: Assessing student progress in project-based learning can be done through regular check-ins, peer reviews, and self-assessments. You can also use rubrics to evaluate the final project and provide feedback to students.
revised: Check in with students while they work, not only at the end. Ask them to explain their choices and what they have learned. Let them review their own work and give classmates feedback. Use a clear list of goals to judge the final project. That list is often called a rubric.
note: Explains assessment methods and rubric in plain language.

original: The aim is to catch shoppers' attention, make the shop and its products look appealing, and encourage people to buy.
revised: The goal is to catch shoppers' attention. Attractive displays help people notice products. They also encourage people to enter the shop and buy something.
note: Splits the retail goal into short sentences.

original: Choose activities that suit the animal. A dog may enjoy walks or fetch, while a cat may prefer a toy it can chase. Let the pet approach at its own pace and notice when it wants a break.
revised: Choose something your pet enjoys. A dog may like a walk or a game of fetch. A cat may prefer chasing a toy. Let the animal approach in its own time. Stop or take a break when it seems to have had enough.
note: Uses simple language and preserves the animal's choice.

original: For most vegetables, a temperature of 425°F (220°C) works well. This brings out their natural sweetness and gives them a nice caramelized flavor.
revised: About 425°F, or 220°C, works for many vegetables. The heat can brown the outside and bring out a sweet flavor. Check your recipe, since vegetables and ovens differ.
note: Preserves cooking estimates and explains seasoning steps.

original: Roasting time depends on the type and size of the vegetables. Generally, smaller pieces like broccoli or Brussels sprouts take 15-20 minutes, while larger pieces like carrots or sweet potatoes take 30-40 minutes. Just keep an eye on them until they're tender and lightly browned.
revised: Small pieces of broccoli or Brussels sprouts may take about 15 to 20 minutes. Larger pieces of carrot or sweet potato may need 30 to 40 minutes. These are guides, not fixed times. Check that the vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
note: Preserves cooking estimates and explains seasoning steps.

original: Simply toss the vegetables with olive oil, salt, and your choice of herbs and spices. You can also add some minced garlic or lemon juice for extra flavor. Keep it simple and let the natural flavors of the vegetables shine through.
revised: Coat the vegetables lightly with olive oil. Add salt and herbs or spices you like. Finely chopped garlic or a little lemon juice can add flavor too. Mix everything so the pieces are evenly coated.
note: Preserves cooking estimates and explains seasoning steps.

original: Dogs, cats, and some small pets can live well with families, but none is care-free. Think about daily care, space, cost, and how your children behave around animals. An adult needs to take responsibility for the pet.
revised: Dogs, cats, and some smaller animals can suit families with children. But every pet needs care. Think about the time, space, and money your family can provide. Also consider how your children behave around animals. An adult must be responsible for the pet.
note: Keeps pet choice conditional and adult care explicit.

original: Polar bears have two layers of fur and a thick layer of fat called blubber to keep them warm in cold temperatures. They also have white fur that helps them blend in with the snow.
revised: Polar bears have two layers of fur that help keep heat in. They also have a thick layer of fat under their skin. This fat is called blubber. Their white-looking fur also helps them blend into the snow.
note: Explains blubber and separates warmth from camouflage.

original: Examples include croissants, Danish pastries, éclairs, fruit tarts, and cream puffs.
revised: Examples include croissants, Danish pastries, éclairs, fruit tarts, and cream puffs.
note: Explains pastry differences and filling terms.

original: A danish is usually a sweet pastry filled with fruit or cream. An eclair is long and thin, with cream inside and a sweet glaze on top.
revised: A Danish is a layered pastry, often with fruit or cream. An éclair is long and has a cream filling. It usually has a sweet coating on top. The dough and shape are different.
note: Explains pastry differences and filling terms.

original: Cream puffs have a light, hollow shell made from dough called choux pastry. After baking, the shells are filled with whipped cream or pastry cream. The dough uses simple ingredients, but making it takes practice.
revised: Cream puffs have a light shell with space inside. The shell is made from a dough called choux pastry. After baking, it is filled with whipped cream or pastry cream. Pastry cream is a thick, custard-like filling. Making the shells takes practice.
note: Explains pastry differences and filling terms.

original: A well-known Japanese spring tradition is hanami, or flower viewing. People gather to enjoy cherry blossoms, often with a picnic. It is a seasonal custom rather than one national holiday held on a single date.
revised: Hanami is a Japanese spring tradition of enjoying flowers, especially cherry blossoms. People often gather for picnics under the trees. It happens during the blossom season. It is not one national holiday on a fixed date.
note: Explains the custom and food while preserving the holiday distinction.

original: Sakura mochi is one spring sweet associated with cherry-blossom season. It is a rice sweet with red bean filling, wrapped in a pickled cherry leaf. People may also bring a range of ordinary picnic foods to a hanami gathering.
revised: Sakura mochi is one sweet linked with cherry-blossom season. It is made from rice and filled with sweet red bean paste. A pickled cherry leaf is wrapped around it. People also bring ordinary picnic foods to hanami gatherings.
note: Explains the custom and food while preserving the holiday distinction.

original: Accuracy refers to how close a measurement is to the true value, while precision refers to how close the measurements are to each other when repeated. Think of it like shooting darts: accuracy is hitting the bullseye, and precision is hitting the same spot multiple times.
revised: Accuracy means how close a result is to the true value. Precision means how close repeated results are to each other. Imagine throwing darts. Accuracy means landing near the bullseye. Precision means the darts land close together, even if they miss the bullseye.
note: Explains both terms through distinct concrete examples.

original: Yes, that's correct. If you're consistently measuring something incorrectly, you can have precise measurements, but they won't be accurate. For example, if your scale is calibrated wrong, you might get the same weight every time, but it won't be the true weight.
revised: Yes. A faulty scale might show the same wrong weight every time. Its repeated readings are close together, so they are precise. But they are not close to the true weight, so they are inaccurate.
note: Explains both terms through distinct concrete examples.

original: Water is an example. You drink it and wash with it. It is also in the air as a gas called water vapour.
revised: Water is an example. You drink it and wash with it. It is also in the air as a gas called water vapour.
note: Already uses a familiar example and explains water vapor.

original: The valedictorian is usually the student with the highest achievement in the graduating class. During the ceremony, they give a speech for their classmates and reflect on their time at school.
revised: The valedictorian gives a speech at graduation. They speak about the class's time at school. The role usually goes to a student with very high achievement. The way the student is chosen can vary.
note: Answers the role first and avoids a universal selection rule.

original: Yes, Khan Academy is a well-known online learning platform. It offers free video lessons and exercises in different subjects, including math, science, and humanities.
revised: Yes. Khan Academy offers free lessons and practice online. Subjects include math, science, and some arts and history topics.
note: Uses familiar subject words and separates the two services.

original: Khan Academy includes subjects such as math and science for a wide range of learners. Its separate Khan Academy Kids app is designed for ages 2–8 and includes early reading, writing, and math activities.
revised: Khan Academy has math and science material for different learning levels. Khan Academy Kids is a separate app for ages 2 to 8. It includes early reading, writing, and math activities.
note: Uses familiar subject words and separates the two services.

original: Disagreements between siblings are common. But frequent fighting can still be upsetting, and threats or physical harm are not something you have to accept.
revised: Arguments between siblings are common. But frequent fighting can still be upsetting. Threats or physical harm are not things you have to accept.
note: Keeps uncertainty and the distinction between disagreement and harm.

original: It could involve sharing space, fairness, attention, or different habits. I cannot tell the reason from this alone. Try talking when everyone is calm, and ask a trusted adult for help if arguments become hurtful or unsafe.
revised: You might disagree about space, fairness, attention, or different habits. I cannot tell the cause from this alone. Try talking when everyone is calm. Ask a trusted adult for help if the fights become hurtful or unsafe.
note: Keeps uncertainty and the distinction between disagreement and harm.

original: One easy option is a fruit salad. Just mix your favorite fruits, such as grapes, strawberries, and pineapple, in a bowl and serve.
revised: Try a fruit salad. Wash your fruit and cut larger pieces into bite-sized pieces. Mix them in a bowl. Grapes, strawberries, and pineapple are possible choices.
note: Makes the no-cook snack into clear preparation steps.

original: Japan is a country with a rich culture and history. One thing you should know is that respect for elders is very important. You should also be prepared to remove your shoes before entering homes or some traditional restaurants.
revised: Customs vary, but polite and respectful behavior matters in many settings. Respect toward older people is often important. You may need to remove your shoes before entering a home. Some traditional restaurants ask this too. Follow your host's lead or ask if you are unsure.
note: Explains customs without treating every situation alike.

original: Japan has several gift-giving customs. Omiyage means a souvenir or small gift brought back from a trip. Neat wrapping is often appreciated. Customs vary, so asking your host or a local friend can help.
revised: Gift-giving is part of several Japanese customs. Omiyage means a small gift or souvenir brought back from a trip. Neat wrapping is often appreciated. Ask your host or a local friend what suits the occasion. Customs can vary.
note: Explains customs without treating every situation alike.

original: Some popular ones include Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Pac-Man, and Donkey Kong. You can also try newer retro-style games like Shovel Knight or Axiom Verge.
revised: Older games to explore include Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Pac-Man, and Donkey Kong. Shovel Knight and Axiom Verge are newer games with an older style. That style is often called retro.
note: Separates older games from newer retro-style games.

original: You can share your photos on platforms like Instagram and Facebook, or use specialized travel photography communities like Flickr or 500px.
revised: You can post travel photos on Instagram or Facebook. Flickr and 500px are other options focused on photography. They are not only for travel photos. Choose a place where the people you want to share with can see them.
note: Corrects the overly narrow description of photography platforms.

original: Before a game, it's best to eat a balanced meal that includes complex carbohydrates, protein, and healthy fats. Examples include whole-grain pasta with chicken and vegetables, or a sandwich with lean turkey and avocado.
revised: Before a game, choose food that gives you energy and sits comfortably in your stomach. A meal earlier in the day could include pasta, chicken, and vegetables. Pasta supplies carbohydrates, which your body uses for energy. The amount and timing matter, especially close to play.
note: Explains nutrient roles without making a large meal mandatory before play.

original: After a game, it's essential to refuel your body with a mix of carbohydrates and protein to help with muscle recovery. Good options include a banana with peanut butter, a protein shake with fruit, or a meal with grilled chicken and sweet potatoes.
revised: After a game, eat food with carbohydrates and protein. Carbohydrates help replace used energy. Protein helps muscles repair. Examples include a banana with peanut butter or chicken with sweet potatoes. A normal meal can provide both.
note: Explains nutrient roles without making a large meal mandatory before play.

original: Another helpful technique is progressive muscle relaxation, where you tense and then relax different muscle groups in your body. This can help release physical tension and promote relaxation.
revised: You could try progressive muscle relaxation. This means gently tightening and then relaxing muscles in turn. Notice the difference between tense and relaxed muscles. It may help your body feel less tight. Avoid painful or injured areas.
note: Explains the technique and keeps it gentle and conditional.

original: Follow your teacher’s instructions before starting any experiment. Wear the eye protection and other safety equipment required for the chemicals you are using. Keep food and drinks out of the lab.
revised: Follow your teacher's instructions before starting an experiment. Wear the eye protection and other safety equipment they require. Different chemicals may need different protection. Keep food and drinks out of the lab.
note: Separates basic lab rules while retaining teacher guidance.

original: DNA stores instructions used by living things. A gene is a section of DNA. You get DNA from your parents. It helps shape your features, along with the world around you.
revised: DNA holds instructions that living things use to grow and work. A gene is one section of DNA. You inherit DNA from your parents. It helps shape your features, but your surroundings and experiences also matter.
note: Explains inheritance and keeps environmental influence.

original: Sound waves make your eardrum shake. Three tiny bones in the middle ear pass that movement to the inner ear, helping you hear.
revised: Sound waves make your eardrum move back and forth. Three tiny bones pass this movement through the middle ear. The movement reaches the inner ear. Your ear then sends signals that your brain reads as sound.
note: Explains the hearing sequence in short steps.

original: I don't have information about you, so I don't know what your favorite color is. Would you like to tell me?
revised: I do not know your favorite color unless you tell me. What is it?
note: Keeps the knowledge limit short and clear.

original: Yes, some popular break activities include taking a short walk, chatting with coworkers, or reading a book.
revised: You could take a short walk, chat with a coworker, or read a few pages. Choose something that gives you a break from your usual work.
note: Gives concrete break choices without empty introduction.

original: A physical adaptation is a body feature that helps an animal survive where it lives. For example, thick fur helps polar bears stay warm.
revised: A physical adaptation is a body feature that helps an animal survive where it lives. For example, thick fur helps polar bears stay warm.
note: Already explains the term with a clear polar bear example.

original: Examples include your shoes gripping the ground, a box resisting a push across the floor, and brake pads rubbing against a wheel rim or brake disc. Friction can be useful for grip even when it makes sliding harder.
revised: Your shoes use friction to grip the ground. Friction is the resistance between surfaces that touch. It also makes a box harder to slide across a floor. Brake pads use friction by pressing against a wheel rim or brake disc. So friction can help us stop or keep our footing.
note: Explains friction through the supplied everyday examples.

original: That sounds exciting! What style are you thinking of? Modern, traditional, or a mix of both?
revised: What would you most like to change in the bathroom? Do you prefer a modern look, a traditional look, or a mixture?
note: Explains planning steps and replaces vanity and fixtures jargon.

original: A walk-in shower with built-in storage might suit that goal. Measure the room and plan where doors, fixtures, and plumbing can go before choosing a size. Adding a large vanity could reduce space, so prioritize the features you need.
revised: A walk-in shower with storage might suit you. Measure the room first. Mark where doors, taps, pipes, and other items need to go. Then work out how much space the shower can use. A large sink cabinet could leave less room, so decide what matters most.
note: Explains planning steps and replaces vanity and fixtures jargon.

original: Longitude tells you how far east or west a place is from a starting line called the prime meridian. This line runs through Greenwich, England. Longitude is measured from 0° there to 180° east or west.
revised: Longitude tells us how far east or west a place is. We measure from a starting line called the prime meridian. That line passes through Greenwich, England. Its longitude is 0 degrees. Other places can be up to 180 degrees east or west of it.
note: Explains the reference line and measurement step by step.

original: Many smart speakers listen locally for a wake phrase, so the microphone must be active to detect it. They may then send audio for processing, and accidental activations can happen. Check the device’s recording settings and physical microphone controls.
revised: Many smart speakers keep their microphone on to detect a wake phrase. That is a phrase that tells the speaker to respond. The device usually checks for it locally first. After activation, it may send audio away for processing. It can also activate by mistake. Check recording settings and the microphone switch.
note: Explains wake phrase and local storage while preserving privacy limits.

original: Yes. A connected camera can have security weaknesses, so use supported devices, install updates, and protect the account. A familiar brand alone does not prove that a camera is secure.
revised: Yes. An internet-connected camera can have security weaknesses. Install updates and protect its account with a strong password. Choose a device that still receives security updates. A well-known brand does not by itself prove the camera is secure.
note: Explains wake phrase and local storage while preserving privacy limits.

original: I would compare specific devices rather than promise that a whole brand protects privacy. Look for clear recording controls, a physical microphone or camera switch where relevant, local storage options, and a stated update-support period.
revised: Compare individual devices rather than trusting a whole brand. Look for controls that clearly show when recording happens. Check for a physical microphone or camera switch where relevant. Local storage keeps recordings on a device you control. Also check how long the maker promises security updates.
note: Explains wake phrase and local storage while preserving privacy limits.

original: Being indoors is not automatically unhealthy. Sitting still for long periods or working without breaks can leave you feeling tired. A short walk outside, when practical, can give you movement and a change of scene.
revised: Being indoors is not automatically unhealthy. But long periods of sitting or working without breaks can leave you tired. A short walk outside may help when possible. It gives you movement and a change of scene.
note: Preserves the distinction between indoors and prolonged inactivity.

original: It can be useful in many settings, but it is not equally suited to every task. Students need enough understanding to explain accurately, and the teacher still needs to guide them and check learning.
revised: Teaching classmates can help in many subjects, but not every task suits it. Students need enough knowledge to explain the topic correctly. The teacher still needs to guide them and check their understanding.
note: Replaces peer-teaching jargon and keeps its limits.

original: Emotional intelligence is the ability to recognize and understand your emotions, as well as the emotions of others. It helps you manage stress and build stronger relationships.
revised: Emotional intelligence means noticing and understanding feelings. These include your own feelings and other people's feelings. It also involves thinking about how to respond to them. This may help you manage stress and handle relationships.
note: Explains the term without promising fixed benefits.

original: Pancakes are usually flat and round, while waffles are thicker and have a grid pattern due to being cooked in a waffle iron.
revised: Pancakes are usually flat and round. They cook on a flat surface. Waffles cook in a special iron that makes a grid pattern. They are often thicker than pancakes.
note: Explains the cooking tool and visible difference.

original: Yes, Rugby is a popular sport played globally, with a huge following in countries like New Zealand, Australia, and the UK.
revised: Yes. Rugby is played in many countries. It has a strong following in places such as New Zealand, Australia, and the UK.
note: Keeps the answer direct without vague superlatives.

original: Competition rules set a time limit, which can depend on the level and event. For an exact limit, check the rules for the competition you mean.
revised: The time limit depends on the competition rules and level. Check the rules for the event you mean. Which competition or level are you asking about?
note: Asks for needed context instead of inventing a fixed rule.

original: You can use a mix of your favorite fruits, such as strawberries, bananas, grapes, and pineapple.
revised: You can use a mix of your favorite fruits, such as strawberries, bananas, grapes, and pineapple.
note: Already a simple answer with familiar fruit examples.

revised: For example, 3 + 1 = 4. If you have three apples and add one, you have four.
note: Adds a concrete illustration of the sum.

original: Some countries have overnight passenger trains, while others have few or none. Availability depends on the route and can change, so check the train operator for your planned journey.
revised: Some countries have overnight passenger trains. Others have few or none. It also depends on the route. Check the train operator for the journey you want, since services can change.
note: Keeps route and time dependence in short sentences.

original: Waffles are a popular breakfast choice. They're tasty and can be topped with many things like fresh fruit, whipped cream, or syrup.
revised: You could have waffles. Add toppings you enjoy, such as fruit, cream, or syrup.
note: Keeps a simple food suggestion naturally short.

original: One strategy is to summarize what you've read after each chapter or section. This helps you understand the main ideas and retain the information better.
revised: After a section, explain its main idea in your own words. Try saying it aloud or writing a few lines. Then check the text for anything you missed. This can help you understand and remember what you read.
note: Turns summarizing into an explicit action without copying style-guide wording.

original: Old oil can lead to engine damage, overheating, and higher fuel use. Repairs can then cost a lot, so follow the car's oil-change schedule.
revised: Old oil may stop protecting the engine well. This can cause damage, overheating, or higher fuel use. Repairs may be expensive. Follow the oil-change schedule for your car.
note: Explains the consequence and preserves uncertainty.

original: Yes, many people live with their siblings when they are growing up. As they get older, they may move out and live on their own or start their own families.
revised: Many children live with their brothers and sisters. As adults, they may move into separate homes. Some continue living together. It depends on the family and their circumstances.
note: Preserves variation in family living arrangements.

original: Yes, taking short breaks can really help. You could try some deep breathing exercises, go for a short walk, or practice some simple stretches.
revised: Try a short walk, gentle stretches, or a few slow breaths. Choose something comfortable that gives you a break from work.
note: Explains guided meditation and avoids an unverified free-access promise.

original: Yes. You can spend a few minutes sitting quietly and noticing your breath or surroundings. It helps some people relax, but a short walk or another calm activity may suit you better.
revised: Yes. Sit quietly for a few minutes and notice your breathing or the room around you. When your mind wanders, gently bring your attention back. This helps some people relax. A walk or another quiet activity may suit you better.
note: Explains guided meditation and avoids an unverified free-access promise.

original: Headspace and Calm are two popular meditation apps that offer short sessions for stress relief. You could also try Insight Timer, which has a wide range of free guided meditations.
revised: Headspace, Calm, and Insight Timer are examples of meditation apps. They offer sessions with a voice guiding you. Check which sessions are free and which need payment before choosing one.
note: Explains guided meditation and avoids an unverified free-access promise.

original: Starting with a morning routine can be helpful. Try doing something simple like stretching, drinking water, or reading for a few minutes to get yourself going.
revised: Choose one or two simple things to do after waking. You might stretch, drink water, or read for a few minutes. A short routine can make the start of the day feel more settled.
note: Makes the morning routine concrete and manageable.

original: Start by decluttering one room at a time, getting rid of items you no longer need or use. This will make it easier to see what you have left to organize.
revised: Start with one small area or room. Sort out things you no longer need or use. Then look at what is left and decide where it should go. You do not need to organize the whole apartment at once.
note: Explains storage furniture and labels time suggestions as examples.

original: Consider using multi-functional furniture, like a storage ottoman or a desk with built-in shelves. You can also use wall-mounted shelves, hooks, and baskets to maximize your space.
revised: Choose furniture that also stores things. For example, a storage footstool has space inside it. A desk with shelves can hold work supplies. Wall shelves, hooks, and baskets may also help you use a small space.
note: Explains storage furniture and labels time suggestions as examples.

original: Set aside some time each week to maintain your space, like tidying up for 10-15 minutes a day or dedicating an hour on the weekend to organizing. This will help keep your space clutter-free and organized.
revised: Set a regular time to put things back. For example, spend 10 to 15 minutes tidying each day. Or choose a longer session at the weekend. Pick a routine you can keep.
note: Explains storage furniture and labels time suggestions as examples.

original: Yes. Magnetic construction sets and puzzles use attraction to connect or move pieces. Small, loose magnets are dangerous if swallowed, so use age-appropriate toys and keep damaged magnetic toys away from children.
revised: Yes. Some building toys and puzzles use magnets to hold pieces together. Loose, small magnets can be dangerous if swallowed. Choose toys meant for the child's age. Keep damaged magnetic toys away from children.
note: Explains magnetic attraction through the toy's action and keeps the warning.

original: One strategy that might help is to make connections between what you're reading and your own life. Ask yourself how the material relates to your experiences or interests.
revised: Connect the text to something you already know. Ask yourself whether it reminds you of an experience or interest. For example, a story about moving may remind you of changing schools. That link can help you remember the story.
note: Adds a labelled personal connection example.

original: There are several types of trains, including passenger trains, freight trains, and high-speed trains. There are also subtypes like commuter trains, long-distance trains, and bullet trains.
revised: Passenger trains carry people. Freight trains carry goods. Commuter trains often take people between home and work. Long-distance trains travel between places farther apart. Some passenger trains are high-speed trains, also called bullet trains in some settings.
note: Explains categories rather than listing unexplained subtypes.

original: No. Einstein's theory of relativity says clocks can measure different amounts of passing time depending on their motion and the gravity around them.
revised: No. Clocks can record different amounts of passing time. Their motion and the gravity around them affect this. Einstein's theory of relativity explains those differences. So this is about time itself, not just different time zones.
note: Explains the kind of time difference and keeps the physical causes.

original: Coastal communities may develop fishing traditions, boat-building skills, or foods based on local seafood. In dry regions, ways of storing and sharing water can become important. These are possible influences, not rules that describe every person in a place.
revised: People near the sea may develop fishing and boat-building traditions. Local seafood may become part of their cooking. In dry areas, storing and sharing water can be especially important. These are possible influences. They do not describe every person who lives in those places.
note: Keeps cultural examples conditional and avoids stereotypes.

original: Cats, dogs, hamsters, and guinea pigs are common pets, but none is automatically easy to care for. Compare their needs for space, daily care, companionship, and veterinary care before choosing.
revised: Cats, dogs, hamsters, and guinea pigs are common choices. But none is automatically easy to care for. Compare the space, daily care, company, and vet care each needs. Choose an animal only if you can meet those needs.
note: Explains care factors and keeps the beginner suitability limit.

original: Basic guitar chords can let you play simple songs fairly early. Changing chords smoothly takes practice, and sore fingertips can make the first sessions challenging. Whether it feels easy depends on the person.
revised: You may learn a few guitar chords fairly quickly. A chord is a group of notes played together. A few chords can be enough for a simple song. Moving smoothly between them takes practice. Your fingertips may feel sore at first. How easy it feels differs from person to person.
note: Explains chords while retaining effort and individual variation.

original: It moves water around Earth so plants and animals can use it. It also affects weather and climate.
revised: The water cycle moves water between the air, land, and oceans. This helps provide water for plants and animals. It also affects rain and other weather. Over time, it influences climate too.
note: Explains the movement and distinguishes weather from longer-term effects.

original: Yes, many families have special traditions during holidays. For example, some families open one gift on Christmas Eve, while others have a big Easter egg hunt on Easter morning. Some families also attend church services or participate in other religious observances during these holidays.
revised: Some families open a gift on Christmas Eve. Others have an Easter egg hunt. Some attend church services or mark the holiday in another religious way. Traditions differ between families, so there is no single set everyone follows.
note: Gives concrete traditions and preserves variation.

original: A display case can keep dust off your toys while letting you see them. Open shelves can also look good, but they do not keep dust out. You could group the toys by type, age, or color.
revised: A glass display case lets you see your toys while keeping dust off them. Open shelves work too, but collect more dust. Try grouping toys by type, age, or color.
note: Uses concrete display choices and an example tied to toy cars.

original: Soft lighting can help bring out the colors and details of your toys. You can use LED strips or spotlights to create a warm and cozy glow around your display.
revised: Use soft light to show the toys' colors and small details. LED strips or small spotlights can help. Position them so you can see the toys without a harsh glare.
note: Uses concrete display choices and an example tied to toy cars.

original: Adding a simple background or decorations that match the theme of your toys can improve the overall display. For example, if you're displaying vintage cars, you could use a cityscape or road-themed backdrop.
revised: A simple background can help the toys stand out. For example, put a road picture behind a collection of toy cars. Keep extra decorations simple so the toys remain easy to see.
note: Uses concrete display choices and an example tied to toy cars.

original: Yes, it's a good idea to wash your silicone spoon after each use to prevent the buildup of bacteria and food residue.
revised: Yes. Wash the spoon after each use to remove leftover food and germs.
note: Replaces residue and bacterial buildup with familiar words.

original: Some popular family dinner traditions include having a weekly roast dinner, making pasta together, or having a taco night. Many families also enjoy having a special meal on Sundays.
revised: You could have a weekly roast dinner, pasta-making evening, or taco night. Some families cook a special meal on Sundays. Choose a meal your family enjoys making or eating together.
note: Makes family dinner traditions clear and optional.

original: Some popular refrigerator brands include Samsung, LG, Whirlpool, and GE. They offer a range of styles and features to suit different needs.
revised: Samsung, LG, Whirlpool, and GE are examples of refrigerator brands. They sell models with different sizes and features.
note: Keeps a simple brand list without a current popularity ranking.

original: Stress can be overwhelming. One simple technique to try is deep breathing exercises. Take slow, deep breaths in through your nose and out through your mouth to help calm your mind and body.
revised: Feeling stressed can be hard. Try a few slow, comfortable breaths. Breathe in gently and let the air out slowly. This may help your body feel calmer.
note: Makes relaxation gentle and keeps the acknowledgement short.

original: Yes, physical activity can also help reduce stress. Try going for a short walk or doing some light stretching exercises to release tension and improve your mood.
revised: A short walk or gentle stretching may help too. Choose a movement that feels comfortable. It can give you a break and help release some tension.
note: Makes relaxation gentle and keeps the acknowledgement short.

original: You're welcome! Remember to take care of yourself and don't hesitate to reach out if you need further guidance or support.
revised: You're welcome. I hope you find something that helps.
note: Makes relaxation gentle and keeps the acknowledgement short.

original: For beginners, I'd recommend starting with Canva or Lightroom. They're both user-friendly and offer a lot of features to improve your photos.
revised: Canva and Lightroom are options to explore. Try simple changes first, such as cropping a photo or adjusting brightness. Choose a tool whose basic controls make sense to you.
note: Turns broad software praise into a beginner trial method.

original: A cube is a 3D shape with six square faces, all the same size.
revised: A cube is a solid shape with six square faces. Every face is the same size. A normal six-sided die is shaped like a cube.
note: Explains the shape with a familiar object.

original: Yes, in the number 4560, the 4 is in the thousands place.
revised: Yes. The 4 in 4560 means four thousand. That is why it is in the thousands place.
note: Explains the place value rather than only confirming it.

original: That sounds like fun. For a talent show, popular acts often include singing, dancing, playing a musical instrument, or telling jokes. You could also consider doing a magic trick or a skit with friends.
revised: You could sing, dance, play an instrument, or tell jokes. A magic trick is another option. With friends, you could perform a short acted scene. Choose something you can practise before the show.
note: Explains skit and gives a relevant choice condition.

original: It can be tough when parents put pressure on us. What do you think would help you feel more supported by them?
revised: That sounds stressful. What could your parents do that would help you feel supported?
note: Keeps empathy while replacing abstract validation language.

original: That's a great point. Sometimes, all we need is someone to listen and validate our feelings. Have you tried talking to them about how you feel when they don't listen?
revised: It makes sense to want them to listen. Have you told them how you feel when you cannot get your point across?
note: Keeps empathy while replacing abstract validation language.

original: That sounds frustrating. You cannot make them listen, but you could ask for one short conversation about a specific issue and say what support you need. If that still goes nowhere, a trusted relative or counselor may help you talk it through.
revised: That sounds frustrating. Try asking for a short talk about one specific problem. Say clearly what help you need. You cannot make them listen. If talking still does not help, a trusted relative or counselor may support you.
note: Keeps empathy while replacing abstract validation language.

original: Sorry to hear that. Have you tried updating the software or checking your internet connection?
revised: Have you updated the meeting app? Also check whether the internet connection stays stable during a call.
note: Provides distinct troubleshooting steps after the user's checks.

original: Check whether your computer is short of memory or busy with other programs. Try turning off background effects, closing unused apps, and testing the camera in another program. A different device can help narrow down the cause.
revised: Your computer may be busy running other programs. Close apps you do not need and turn off background effects. Test the camera in a different app. If possible, try the meeting on another device. These checks can help narrow down the cause.
note: Provides distinct troubleshooting steps after the user's checks.

original: The Milky Way has a spiral shape and contains hundreds of billions of stars, including our Sun. It is about 100,000 light-years across. A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.
revised: The Milky Way is our galaxy. It contains hundreds of billions of stars, including the Sun. Its main disk has a spiral shape and is about 100,000 light-years across. A light-year is how far light travels in one year.
note: Explains the distance unit and identifies the measured disk.

original: One key tip is to practice active listening. This means focusing on what the other person is saying and responding thoughtfully, rather than interrupting or planning your response while they speak.
revised: Try active listening. This means paying close attention while someone speaks. Let them finish before you answer. Then check your understanding by briefly repeating the main point. Avoid planning your reply while they are still talking.
note: Explains active listening through actions.

original: The Roman numeral for 5 is V.
revised: The Roman numeral for 5 is V.
note: Already a direct factual answer.

original: Electric motors generally turn a larger share of their input energy into motion than combustion engines do. But running cost and environmental impact also depend on the car, energy source, and how you use it. Compare actual models rather than judging by fuel type alone.
revised: Electric motors usually turn more of their input energy into movement. Engines that burn fuel lose more energy in other ways, such as heat. But cost and environmental impact also depend on the car and energy source. Compare actual models and how you would use them.
note: Explains combustion in everyday words and preserves efficiency versus cost distinctions.

original: A hybrid combines a combustion engine with an electric motor. A battery-electric car uses an electric motor powered by a rechargeable battery and has no combustion engine. Charging needs, range, and running costs vary by model.
revised: A hybrid has both an electric motor and an engine that burns fuel. A battery-electric car runs on an electric motor and rechargeable battery. It has no fuel-burning engine. Range, charging needs, and running costs differ between models.
note: Explains combustion in everyday words and preserves efficiency versus cost distinctions.

original: You can usually find local intramural leagues through your school or community recreation center. You can also search online for leagues in your area or check websites like Meetup.com.
revised: Ask your school or local recreation center about sports leagues. You can also search for local groups online, including on Meetup. Check who is allowed to join, since some school leagues are only for students.
note: Makes the league search clear while retaining eligibility differences.

original: There is no required number. Start with clothes that cover your normal week, weather, and laundry routine. Try using that smaller set for a while, then add an item only when you notice a real gap.
revised: There is no fixed number. Pick enough clothes for your normal week, weather, and washing routine. Use that smaller set for a while. Add something only when you notice a need it does not meet.
note: Explains wardrobe gaps in concrete terms.

original: Try sharing rides with others. You can split fuel costs and reduce the gases released by separate car trips.
revised: Try sharing rides with others. You can split fuel costs and reduce the gases released by separate car trips.
note: Already uses a simple action and explains its benefits.

original: A simple green salad or garlic bread are both great options to go with pasta primavera.
revised: A simple green salad or garlic bread are both great options to go with pasta primavera.
note: Already a short useful side-dish answer.

original: Look for hat shops, department stores, or souvenir shops in the parts of Paris you plan to visit. Check each shop's own listing for its location and opening hours. Try on the beret if you can, because fit and fabric can vary.
revised: Try hat shops, department stores, or souvenir shops near your planned stops. Check the shop's own website for its address and opening hours. Try on the beret if possible. Sizes and fabrics can feel different.
note: Separates shopping checks and keeps fit advice.

original: Yes, some schools may have Easter egg hunts, parties, or other spring-themed activities, but it varies by school and location.
revised: Some schools have Easter egg hunts, parties, or spring activities. Others do not. It depends on the school and where it is.
note: Makes the school variation explicit.

original: Web pages commonly use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML describes the page's structure, CSS controls its appearance, and JavaScript adds behavior. Strictly speaking, HTML is a markup language and CSS is a style language; JavaScript is a programming language.
revised: Web pages commonly use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML marks out parts of a page, such as headings and paragraphs. CSS controls how those parts look. JavaScript adds actions, such as responding to a button click. JavaScript is a programming language. HTML and CSS instead describe page structure and style.
note: Explains each web technology with concrete tasks.

original: Usually, it's best if a family member can take care of your pets when you're away. If not, you can also consider hiring a pet sitter.
revised: Ask a reliable person who understands your pets' needs. That could be a family member or a pet sitter. Make sure they can handle feeding, care, and any medicines while you are away.
note: Avoids assuming family or children can take sole responsibility safely.

original: That's great! Assigning pet care responsibilities to your kids can be a good learning experience for them. Just make sure to guide them and create a routine for feeding, walking, and playing with your pets.
revised: Older children can help with tasks they understand and can manage safely. Show them the routine for feeding, walks, and play. A responsible adult should still be available to check the care and handle problems.
note: Avoids assuming family or children can take sole responsibility safely.

original: You can start by choosing a specific day and time that works for everyone, and creating a simple agenda to guide the conversation.
revised: Choose a time when everyone can join. Write a short list of things to discuss. This list is your agenda. Share it before the meeting so people know what to expect.
note: Explains agenda through the meeting steps.

original: If you count from birth, the first stage is infancy, when you are a baby. Development also happens before birth. Different guides use different names and age ranges for the stages.
revised: If you start counting at birth, the first stage is infancy. That means the time when you are a baby. Development also happens before birth. Different lessons may use different stage names and ages.
note: Explains stage terms and preserves variation in classifications.

original: After infancy comes childhood, when movement, language, and learning develop a lot. Later comes adolescence, the stage of growing toward adulthood.
revised: Childhood comes after infancy. Children develop movement, language, and many other skills. Later comes adolescence, the period of growing toward adulthood.
note: Explains stage terms and preserves variation in classifications.

original: There is no single official number. One simple list is infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Some lessons split these further or include development before birth.
revised: There is no single official number. One common list has five stages: infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Other lists divide the stages further or include the time before birth.
note: Explains stage terms and preserves variation in classifications.

original: Yes, I can help with that. Some popular family traditions include having a weekly dinner together, playing board games on Friday nights, or going on an annual vacation to the same place.
revised: You could share a weekly dinner or play board games every Friday. Another idea is visiting the same place each year. Choose something your family can enjoy and repeat.
note: Keeps tradition ideas concrete and optional.

original: Yes, I do. For example, during summer, people often buy more fruits, salads, and BBQ-related items. Would you like me to suggest some items for your summer shopping list?
revised: I can help make a seasonal list. For summer, examples include fruit, salad ingredients, and food for a barbecue. Which season are you shopping for, and how many people?
note: Avoids claiming a stored list and asks for useful planning details.

original: I cannot check the current date here. A reliable moon-phase calendar can tell you when the next full moon will be.
revised: I cannot check the current date here. Use a reliable moon-phase calendar to find the next full moon.
note: Keeps the access limit and lookup instruction clear.

original: A ryokan is a traditional Japanese inn that offers a unique cultural experience. They usually have tatami-matted rooms, futon beds, and shared baths. Many ryokans also offer traditional Japanese meals and activities, such as tea ceremonies.
revised: A ryokan is a traditional Japanese inn. Rooms often have woven floor mats called tatami. Guests may sleep on futons, which are bedding laid out on the floor. Some inns have shared baths and serve Japanese meals. Facilities and activities differ, so check the inn before booking.
note: Explains tatami and futon and preserves variation between inns.

original: For a very formal event, follow the dress code. Ordinary loafers may be too casual, while special formal slippers can suit some black-tie outfits.
revised: Sometimes, but ordinary loafers may be too casual for a very formal event. Check the invitation's dress code. Special formal slippers can suit some black-tie outfits. They are different from everyday loafers.
note: Explains the limitation without a blanket footwear rule.

original: You could catch up on news, take a walk, read a book, or run some personal errands. What sounds most interesting to you?
revised: You could take a walk, read a few pages, or do a small personal task. Checking the news is another option. What would feel most useful or restful?
note: Makes the phone list task concrete.

original: Yes, you can use the notes app on your phone to make a list, or download a specific grocery list app like Out of Milk or AnyList.
revised: Use your phone's notes app to write a shopping list. You can tick off items as you shop. Apps such as Out of Milk or AnyList are other options.
note: Makes the phone list task concrete.

original: Choose a bike for the routes you expect to ride. A hybrid can suit paved paths and light gravel, while rough trails may call for a mountain bike. Fit and comfort matter, so try a few sizes and ask a bike shop for help.
revised: Choose a bike for the places you plan to ride. A hybrid bike can suit paved paths and light gravel. A mountain bike may be better for rough trails. Try different sizes, because fit and comfort matter. A bike shop can help you choose.
note: Links bike type to routes in short sentences.

original: There are many types, such as Italian, Mexican, Chinese, and American diners.
revised: You can find restaurants serving Italian, Mexican, or Chinese food. American diners are another type of eating place.
note: Explains the category relationship clearly.

original: A diner is a type of restaurant. It is usually casual and often serves familiar meals such as breakfast dishes, burgers, and sandwiches. The word restaurant covers diners and many other kinds of eating places.
revised: A diner is one kind of restaurant. It is usually relaxed and serves familiar meals. Examples include breakfast dishes, burgers, and sandwiches. Restaurant is the wider word that includes diners.
note: Explains the category relationship clearly.

original: A suit has a matching jacket and trousers. A tuxedo is formal evening wear, often with satin details on the lapels and trouser sides and worn with a bow tie. It does not have to be black.
revised: A suit has a matching jacket and trousers. A tuxedo is made for formal evening events. It often has shiny satin details and is worn with a bow tie. Satin is a smooth, shiny fabric. A tuxedo does not have to be black.
note: Explains satin and keeps the invitation as the main condition.

original: Follow the invitation’s dress code. Black tie usually points to a tuxedo, while a suit suits many other weddings. Time of day alone does not decide; ask the hosts if you are unsure.
revised: Follow the dress code on the invitation. Black tie usually means a tuxedo. A suit works for many other weddings. The time of day alone does not decide. Ask the hosts if the invitation is unclear.
note: Explains satin and keeps the invitation as the main condition.

original: For a wedding, a navy blue or charcoal gray suit is usually a safe and stylish choice.
revised: Navy blue or dark gray are common choices. Check that the color suits the wedding's dress code.
note: Explains satin and keeps the invitation as the main condition.

original: A food chain shows one path of energy through living things, such as grass → rabbit → hawk. A food web connects many of these paths. It shows the different things each animal eats and what eats it.
revised: A food chain shows one route that energy takes through living things. For example, grass feeds a rabbit, and a hawk eats the rabbit. A food web joins many food chains. It shows several foods each animal may eat, and what may eat that animal.
note: Explains the energy path through the existing example.

original: Yes. A food web joins many food chains and shows how living things depend on each other for food.
revised: Yes. It joins many food chains in one picture. This helps show how living things rely on one another for food.
note: Explains the energy path through the existing example.

original: You do not owe anyone a follow-back. Follow accounts you want to see, whether or not they follow you. If you know the person, you can still keep in touch in other ways.
revised: You do not have to follow someone just because they follow you. Choose accounts you want to see. You can still keep in touch with someone in other ways.
note: Uses clear online-boundary language and preserves the user's choice.

original: You can respond if you want to, but you are not required to. Be cautious with links, requests for money, or pressure to share private information. Ignore, block, or report messages that feel suspicious or abusive.
revised: You can reply if you want, but you do not have to. Be careful with links, money requests, or pressure to share private details. You can ignore, block, or report suspicious or hurtful messages.
note: Uses clear online-boundary language and preserves the user's choice.

original: If someone leaves a mean comment, it's best to ignore it and not engage. Block the user if necessary, and report the comment to the platform if it's harassment or bullying.
revised: You do not need to argue with someone trying to upset you. You can ignore the comment or block the account. Report bullying or harassment using the platform's reporting tools.
note: Uses clear online-boundary language and preserves the user's choice.

original: Wind speed is the rate at which air moves through the atmosphere, usually measured in miles per hour (mph) or kilometers per hour (km/h).
revised: Wind speed tells us how fast the air is moving. It is often measured in miles per hour or kilometers per hour. The short forms are mph and km/h.
note: Explains speed and units without atmosphere jargon.

original: Exactly, they refer to the same time periods. BCE is equivalent to BC, and CE is equivalent to AD. They're just different labels used to measure time.
revised: Yes. BCE uses the same year numbers as BC. CE uses the same year numbers as AD. The labels differ, but the dates refer to the same years.
note: Makes equivalence specific to dates and year numbers.

original: Test the soil's pH, which shows how acidic or alkaline it is. Also check its nutrients, the substances plants need to grow. You can buy a home test kit or ask a local plant nursery for help.
revised: Test the soil before adding anything. A pH below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, and above 7 is alkaline. Different plants need different pH conditions. Also check nutrients, which plants need to grow. A home test kit or local plant nursery may help.
note: Review fix: replaces a circular pH explanation with clear numeric labels and plant-dependent needs. RHS guidance checked.

original: First check the pH range your plants need. A soil-test service can advise whether to add lime to raise pH or sulfur to lower it, and how much. Compost can improve soil structure, but it does not automatically correct the pH.
revised: First, find out the pH range your chosen plants need. A soil-testing service can advise on changes and amounts. Lime can raise pH, while sulfur can lower it. Do not guess how much to add. Compost can improve the soil, but it does not always fix pH.
note: Explains soil terms and preserves treatment-specific guidance.

original: Planting time depends on the plant and your local climate. Check local guidance for frost dates and the crop you want to grow. If you added a soil treatment, also follow its directions about when to plant.
revised: It depends on the plants and your local weather. Check local advice about planting times and frost. If you treated the soil, read the product instructions too. Some treatments affect when you should plant.
note: Explains soil terms and preserves treatment-specific guidance.

original: Some popular types of houseplants include Snake Plants, Spider Plants, and Peace Lilies. They're all relatively easy to care for.
revised: Snake plants, spider plants, and peace lilies are common houseplants. Their light and watering needs differ. Choose one that suits the space where you will keep it.
note: Avoids claiming every named plant is easy in every home.

original: Options depend on your country and route. FlixBus and Greyhound are examples of intercity coach brands in some regions. Check which operator actually serves your journey before comparing prices and stops.
revised: It depends on your country and route. FlixBus and Greyhound are examples in some regions. First check which company serves your journey. Then compare prices, stops, and travel times.
note: Keeps amenities and ticket rules specific to the booked service.

original: Yes, most intercity buses have restrooms on board for passenger convenience. They may also offer free Wi-Fi and power outlets.
revised: Many intercity coaches have a toilet, but not every service does. Some also offer Wi-Fi or power outlets. Check the details for the specific bus you plan to book.
note: Keeps amenities and ticket rules specific to the booked service.

original: Many operators accept mobile tickets, but policies differ. Check the instructions for your booking, and save the ticket so you can open it without a connection. Bring any identification the operator requires.
revised: Many companies accept tickets on a phone, but rules differ. Read the instructions for your booking. Save the ticket so you can open it without internet access. Bring any identification the company requires.
note: Keeps amenities and ticket rules specific to the booked service.

original: Tiny living things called phytoplankton use sunlight to make food. Small drifting animals eat them. Small fish eat those animals, and larger fish eat the small fish. Phytoplankton include algae and some bacteria, not just plants.
revised: Here is one example: phytoplankton are tiny living things that make food using sunlight. Small drifting animals eat them. Small fish eat those animals, and larger fish eat the small fish. Phytoplankton include algae and some bacteria. They are not all plants.
note: Explains the food-chain starting point and keeps the biological distinction.

original: Some popular smartwatch brands include Apple, Samsung, and Fitbit. Each brand offers a range of models with different features and price points.
revised: Apple, Samsung, and Fitbit are examples of smartwatch brands. Their models differ in features and price. Check that a watch works with your phone.
note: Keeps brand examples simple and adds relevant compatibility context.

original: Yes. Cloning makes copies of DNA, cells, or whole living things. Cloned living things have very similar DNA. But they are not the same in every way, because their surroundings and experiences can differ.
revised: Yes. Cloning means making copies of DNA, cells, or whole living things. DNA carries instructions used by living things. Cloned animals may have very similar DNA. But different surroundings and experiences mean they are not identical in every way.
note: Explains DNA and preserves the limit of clone similarity.

original: That sounds like fun. For a science fair, good projects usually involve experiments or demonstrations that can be easily explained and shown to others. Some ideas could be building a volcano, creating a solar oven, or making a homemade lava lamp.
revised: Choose a project with a question you can explain and investigate. Ideas include a model volcano, solar oven, or homemade lava lamp. A solar oven uses sunlight to heat things. Check that your teacher approves the project and materials.
note: Makes the demonstration clear and preserves the no-sealing warning.

original: A baking-soda-and-vinegar volcano can be a simple demonstration. Use a small open container on a tray, and build the model around it. Do not seal the container; the reaction makes gas that needs a way out.
revised: A baking-soda-and-vinegar volcano can be a simple demonstration. Use a small open container on a tray. Build the model around that container. Never seal it. The reaction makes gas, and the gas needs a way to escape.
note: Makes the demonstration clear and preserves the no-sealing warning.

original: Good luck with your project, and I hope you have fun at the science fair.
revised: Good luck with your project, and I hope you have fun at the science fair.
note: Makes the demonstration clear and preserves the no-sealing warning.

original: The printing press was mainly used to print books, newspapers, and other written materials. It played a key role in the spread of literacy and education during the Renaissance and beyond.
revised: The printing press made copies of books, newspapers, and other written material. It helped writing reach more people. This supported reading and education during the Renaissance and later periods.
note: Explains the effect of printing without literacy jargon.

original: There is no single most popular period for everyone. Vintage clothing can include styles from many decades, such as 1950s dresses, 1970s denim, or 1990s sportswear.
revised: There is no single most popular style for everyone. Vintage clothes come from many past decades. Examples include 1950s dresses, 1970s denim, and 1990s sportswear.
note: Keeps popularity uncertain and explains vintage through dated examples.

original: Ask the shelter or rescue what support it offers. Some provide advice about settling in, training, or behavior. Check what is included and whether any veterinary costs are covered.
revised: Ask the shelter what help it offers after adoption. Some give advice about training, behavior, or settling into a new home. Check whether that help costs extra. Also ask whether any vet care is included.
note: Turns adoption support into specific questions.

original: You can use stock, wine, or even water, depending on the recipe and the flavors you want to achieve. The liquid should cover about half of the food, and you can add aromatics like onions and herbs for extra flavor.
revised: Use stock, wine, or water, depending on the recipe. Stock is a liquid made by cooking ingredients such as vegetables or bones in water. Many braising recipes use enough liquid to reach about halfway up the food. Onions and herbs can add flavor. Follow your recipe for the amount.
note: Explains stock and makes the liquid level recipe-dependent.

original: The biggest planet in our solar system is Jupiter. It's a gas giant and is much larger than the other planets.
revised: Jupiter is the biggest planet in our solar system. It is a gas giant, which means it is made mostly of gas. It is much larger than the other planets.
note: Explains gas giant immediately.

original: You could try fresh fruit, plain yogurt, or carrot sticks with hummus. Choose something you enjoy that fits your needs.
revised: Try fruit, plain yogurt, or carrot sticks with hummus. Hummus is a spread usually made from chickpeas. Choose a snack that fits your needs and that you enjoy.
note: Explains hummus and gives clear smoothie adjustments.

original: One popular smoothie recipe is a banana-berry mix. Combine frozen banana, mixed berries, and a splash of milk in a blender for a quick and nutritious drink.
revised: Try blending frozen banana with mixed berries. Add a splash of milk so the blender can mix it smoothly. You can adjust the milk to make the drink thicker or thinner.
note: Explains hummus and gives clear smoothie adjustments.

original: Yes. Try oats to make it more filling, plain yogurt for a thicker texture, or a little spinach. Taste it before adding sweetener, since the fruit may be sweet enough.
revised: Yes. Oats can make it more filling. Plain yogurt makes it thicker. You could also add a little spinach. Taste it before adding sugar or another sweetener. The fruit may already be sweet enough.
note: Explains hummus and gives clear smoothie adjustments.

original: Some sound bounces back, some is taken in by the wall, and some may pass through it. If the returning sound reaches you after the first sound, you can hear it as an echo.
revised: Some sound bounces back from the wall. Some is absorbed by the wall, and some may pass through. Absorbed means the sound's energy is taken in by the material. If reflected sound reaches you after the first sound, you may hear an echo.
note: Explains absorption and the delay needed for an echo.

original: Yes, some popular mountain retreats include the Rocky Mountains in Colorado, the Blue Ridge Mountains in North Carolina, and the Sierra Nevada in California.
revised: You could explore Colorado's Rocky Mountains, North Carolina's Blue Ridge Mountains, or California's Sierra Nevada. These are large regions, so choose a town or route within one. The best choice depends on the season and activities you want.
note: Keeps broad destinations while making seasonal suitability clear.

original: The Rocky Mountains offer a wide range of activities, such as hiking, skiing, and wildlife viewing. You can also visit popular destinations like Aspen, Vail, and Estes Park.
revised: You can hike, watch wildlife, or ski when conditions allow. Aspen, Vail, and Estes Park are places people visit. Choose activities that suit the season and your experience.
note: Keeps broad destinations while making seasonal suitability clear.

original: A physical change is when a substance changes form, but stays the same, like ice melting to water. A chemical change is when a substance turns into something new, like wood burning to ash.
revised: In a physical change, a material changes form but stays the same substance. Ice melting into water is one example. In a chemical change, new substances form. Burning wood is an example: it produces ash and gases.
note: Preserves the substance distinction and clarifies burning products.

original: It depends on the version. Traditional Valencian paella uses rice, chicken, rabbit, beans, tomato, and seasonings such as saffron. Seafood paellas use different ingredients. Chorizo is not a standard ingredient in traditional Valencian paella.
revised: It depends on the type of paella. Traditional Valencian paella uses rice, chicken, rabbit, beans, and tomato. Saffron is one seasoning. Seafood versions use different ingredients. Chorizo is not a standard ingredient in traditional Valencian paella.
note: Separates recipe types without changing their distinction.

original: That sounds great. If you enjoy cooking, you might consider meal planning as a hobby. It involves planning and organizing meals for the week, which can be a fun and creative challenge.
revised: You might enjoy planning a week's meals around new recipes. Meal planning means choosing meals ahead of time. It lets you try different dishes and organize the ingredients you need.
note: Explains meal planning with an optional theme and simple tool steps.

original: One tip is to start by planning around a theme or ingredient, such as a specific cuisine or a seasonal vegetable. You can also use online recipes and meal planning tools to help you get started.
revised: Start with one theme or ingredient. For example, choose meals that use a vegetable in season. Find a few recipes that fit your time and skill level. Then make a list of the ingredients you need.
note: Explains meal planning with an optional theme and simple tool steps.

original: A notebook, calendar, or simple spreadsheet can work well. Write down meals, ingredients, and what you already have. If you prefer an app, look for shared grocery lists and easy recipe storage.
revised: A notebook, calendar, or simple spreadsheet can work. List your meals and the ingredients for each. Mark what you already have. If you prefer an app, look for easy recipe storage and shopping lists you can share.
note: Explains meal planning with an optional theme and simple tool steps.

original: On a windy day, it's best to wear wind-resistant clothing like a windbreaker or a jacket with a hood.
revised: A jacket that blocks wind can help. A windbreaker is a light jacket made for this. A hood can also protect your head from the wind.
note: Separates wind resistance from rain protection.

original: Not always. Wind resistance and waterproofing are different. Some jackets resist a light shower but soak through in steady rain, so check the label for the protection you need.
revised: Not always. A jacket can block wind without keeping out rain. Some handle a light shower but get wet through in steady rain. Check the label for the rain protection you need.
note: Separates wind resistance from rain protection.

original: While animals can't understand human language like we do, some animals, like dogs and parrots, can learn to recognize and respond to certain words or phrases.
revised: Some animals can learn to respond to certain human words or phrases. Dogs and parrots are examples. That does not mean they understand language in the same way people do.
note: Preserves the distinction between word response and human language understanding.

original: Being a middle child is not inherently good or bad. Birth order alone does not determine your personality. Your family relationships and how people treat one another matter more than a label.
revised: Being a middle child is not automatically good or bad. Birth order alone does not decide your personality. Your relationships and how your family treats one another matter more than the label.
note: Uses familiar wording without birth-order stereotypes.

original: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 30% of the Earth's land area.
revised: Asia is the largest continent. It covers about 30 percent of Earth's land area.
note: Separates the direct answer from its quantity.

original: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian artist, inventor, and scientist from the 15th and 16th centuries. He is famous for painting the Mona Lisa and designing flying machines.
revised: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian artist, inventor, and scientist. He lived in the 1400s and 1500s. He painted the Mona Lisa. He also drew designs for machines, including flying machines.
note: Uses familiar date wording and distinguishes designs from built machines.

original: NASA's website explains comets, asteroids, and other space topics. Apps such as Sky Map or Star Walk can help you identify things in the sky. Many planetariums and observatories also run public viewing nights and classes.
revised: Start with NASA's website for explanations of comets and asteroids. Sky apps can help identify objects overhead. You could also visit a planetarium, which shows the sky in an indoor theater. Some observatories offer public viewing nights with telescopes. Check local event listings.
note: Explains viewing venues and makes the learning route concrete.

original: English is spoken in many countries. Arabic is spoken across parts of the Middle East and North Africa. Spanish is spoken in many countries in Central and South America.
revised: English is spoken in many countries. Arabic is spoken across parts of the Middle East and North Africa. Spanish is spoken in many countries in Central and South America.
note: Already gives clear language examples without claiming exclusivity.

original: Where available, choose an electricity plan supplied from renewable sources or consider suitable solar power. Saving electricity is also useful, but saving energy is different from changing its source.
revised: You could choose an electricity plan using renewable sources, if one is available. Renewable sources include sunlight and wind. Solar panels may be another option if they suit your home. Using less electricity also helps, but it does not change where the electricity comes from.
note: Explains renewable sources and retains the source-versus-saving distinction.

original: Examples include watches, rings, and wristbands that support contactless payments. The available features depend on the device, payment service, bank, and country.
revised: Some watches, rings, and wristbands can make contactless payments. You hold the device near a payment machine to pay. Support depends on the device, payment service, bank, and country.
note: Explains payment operation and keeps acceptance and security limits.

original: Many use a substitute number instead of sharing your actual card number. Device locks provide another layer of protection. No system is risk-free, so set up its security features and follow the provider’s steps if it is lost.
revised: Many devices send a substitute number instead of your real card number. A screen lock or other device lock adds protection. No system is completely risk-free. Set up the security features. If the device is lost, follow the provider's instructions to stop payments.
note: Explains payment operation and keeps acceptance and security limits.

original: Only where your card and the device's payment service are accepted. A contactless symbol is a useful clue, but support varies by country, bank, and payment machine.
revised: No. The shop must accept your card and the device's payment service. A contactless symbol is a useful sign, but not a guarantee. Support can vary between banks, countries, and payment machines.
note: Explains payment operation and keeps acceptance and security limits.

original: A cousin is the child of your parent's sibling. For example, if your mom has a sister and that sister has a child, that child is your cousin.
revised: Your cousin is the child of your parent's brother or sister. For example, your aunt's child is your cousin.
note: Replaces sibling with the family relationship it names.

original: The pH scale shows how acidic or basic a solution is. Acids usually have a pH below 7, while bases usually have one above 7. Both can burn or damage materials. Handle them carefully and follow lab instructions.
revised: The pH scale helps tell acids and bases apart in a solution. Acids usually have a pH below 7. Bases usually have a pH above 7. Both can cause burns or damage materials. Follow your lab instructions when handling either one.
note: Keeps the pH distinction and warning in separate sentences.

original: A mobile app is a program installed on your phone or tablet. A web app runs through a browser and can be used on different devices.
revised: A mobile app is installed on a phone or tablet. A web app runs in a browser, such as Chrome or Safari. You can often use the same web app on different devices.
note: Explains browser and offline access while retaining project-dependent choice.

original: A mobile app can be useful when you need close access to a phone’s features. A web app can be easier to share and update across devices. Some web apps work offline too, so choose based on the features your project needs.
revised: A mobile app may suit tasks that need close access to phone features. A web app can be easier to share across different devices. It can also be easier to update for everyone. Some web apps work without internet access too. Choose based on the features your project needs.
note: Explains browser and offline access while retaining project-dependent choice.

original: Yes. Decide what your project needs to do, then choose the option that fits those needs.
revised: Yes. Decide what your project needs to do, then choose the option that fits those needs.
note: Explains browser and offline access while retaining project-dependent choice.

original: A saucepan is usually smaller and suits sauces or small meals. A Dutch oven is a larger, heavy pot often used for slow cooking, roasting, or braising, which means cooking gently with a little liquid.
revised: A saucepan is usually smaller and useful for sauces or small meals. A Dutch oven is a larger, heavy pot with a lid. It is often used for slow cooking or roasting. It also suits braising, which means cooking gently with a little liquid.
note: Explains both cookware types and braising.
