original: Japanese cuisine is known for its emphasis on fresh ingredients and seasonality. Popular dishes include sushi, ramen, and tempura.
revised: Japanese cooking often pays attention to fresh ingredients and what is in season. Sushi, ramen, and tempura are familiar examples. Ramen is a noodle soup. Tempura is food coated in a light batter and fried.
note: Explains unfamiliar dish names with short descriptions.

original: Refined canola, peanut, or a vegetable oil sold for frying can work. Check the label, because oils vary and unrefined versions can behave differently in heat. Choose an oil with a neutral flavor if you want the chicken's seasoning to stand out.
revised: Use an oil labelled as suitable for frying. Refined canola, peanut, or vegetable oil can work. Refined means processed to remove some parts of the oil. Unrefined versions may behave differently when heated. Choose a mild-tasting oil if you want the chicken's seasoning to stand out.
note: Explains refined and preserves label-based suitability.

original: Bright Angel is a well-known trail into the canyon, but it is steep and can be strenuous. A short walk along a suitable section of the Rim Trail may be a better fit for a casual visit. Choose a route you can safely return from.
revised: Bright Angel Trail is a well-known route into the canyon. It is steep and can be tiring, especially on the way back up. A short, suitable part of the Rim Trail may suit a casual visit better. Choose a distance you can safely walk back from.
note: Explains strenuous through the return climb and preserves route limits.

original: One helpful tip is to create a schedule. Set specific times for studying, doing homework, and breaks. This can help you stay organized and on track.
revised: Make a schedule with time for homework, study, and breaks. Start with tasks that are due soon. Seeing the work on a page can make it easier to plan.
note: Makes scheduling and asking for help specific.

original: Start by writing down all your tasks, including homework, study time, and any other activities you want to fit in. Then, assign specific times for each task, making sure to leave some free time for relaxation. You can use a planner, calendar, or app to stay organized.
revised: List your homework, study tasks, and other activities. Give each a realistic time slot. Leave some free time and breaks between tasks. Use a paper planner, calendar, or app. Adjust the plan if a task takes longer than expected.
note: Makes scheduling and asking for help specific.

original: Don't worry, there are many resources available to help you. You can ask your teacher for extra help, work with a classmate or tutor, or search for online resources and study guides.
revised: Ask your teacher, a classmate, or a tutor for help. Show them the part you do not understand. A study guide or clear online lesson may also help. Try to explain what you have already attempted.
note: Makes scheduling and asking for help specific.

original: Verbal communication means using words to share a message. In everyday discussions it often means speaking, such as talking with a friend. Some definitions also include written words.
revised: Verbal communication means sharing a message with words. People often use the term for speaking, such as talking with a friend. Some definitions include writing too.
note: Explains the terms and keeps differences between definitions.

original: Yes, verbal communication can happen in any language that people speak. It's an important way for people to connect and share ideas across cultures and languages.
revised: Yes. People can use spoken words in any language to share ideas. To understand each other, they need a shared language or help such as translation.
note: Explains the terms and keeps differences between definitions.

original: No. Language is a system of words or signs and rules for combining them. Communication is the act of sharing meaning. People can use language to communicate, but they can also communicate through gestures, expressions, or pictures.
revised: No. A language is a system of words or signs with rules. Communication is the act of sharing meaning. Language is one way to do that. People can also share meaning through gestures, facial expressions, or pictures.
note: Explains the terms and keeps differences between definitions.

original: An adaptation is a feature passed from parents to young that helps them survive or have young of their own. Thick fur, for example, helps keep animals warm. These features become common over many generations.
revised: An adaptation is an inherited feature that helps a living thing survive or have young. Inherited means passed from parents to their young. Thick fur is one example because it helps keep animals warm. Adaptations become common over many generations.
note: Explains inherited adaptation and corrects the follow-up misconception.

original: Migration means moving between places, often with the seasons. It can itself be an adaptation, such as birds moving to places with more food. An individual adjusting to a new place is a different kind of change.
revised: Migration means moving between places, often as the seasons change. A regular migration pattern can be an adaptation. For example, birds may travel to places with more food. One animal getting used to a new place is a different kind of change.
note: Explains inherited adaptation and corrects the follow-up misconception.

original: The ideas are different, but can overlap. A regular migration pattern may be an adaptation passed down through generations. It does not mean an animal develops a new inherited feature during one trip.
revised: They can overlap, but there is an important difference. A migration pattern can be inherited over many generations. An animal does not gain a new inherited feature during one journey.
note: Explains inherited adaptation and corrects the follow-up misconception.

original: That's a great idea. Always be aware of your surroundings, follow traffic signals, and wear bright or reflective clothing to increase visibility.
revised: Pay attention to the traffic and people around you. Follow crossing signals. Wear bright or reflective clothing so drivers can see you more easily.
note: Keeps crossing conditions and visibility advice clear.

original: Use a suitable crossing where available and follow its signals. Look in every direction traffic may come from, including turning vehicles, and check that drivers have stopped before you enter their path. Do not assume that seeing a driver means they have seen you.
revised: Use a suitable crossing when there is one. Follow its signals and look in every direction traffic could come from. Watch for turning vehicles too. Make sure drivers have stopped before crossing their path. Seeing a driver does not mean the driver has seen you.
note: Keeps crossing conditions and visibility advice clear.

original: If it's dark, consider carrying a flashlight or wearing lights on your clothing to make yourself more visible to drivers. You can also try to stick to well-lit routes whenever possible.
revised: Choose a well-lit route when possible. A flashlight or light on your clothing can make you easier to see. Keep watching traffic even when you are wearing lights.
note: Keeps crossing conditions and visibility advice clear.

original: You can try classic tomato sauce, creamy Alfredo, or a simple pesto sauce.
revised: Tomato sauce is one option. Alfredo is a creamy sauce. Pesto is another choice, often made with basil, oil, and other ingredients blended together.
note: Explains the named sauces rather than only listing them.

original: Some benefits of Pilates include improved balance and coordination, increased core strength, and better overall flexibility. It's also a great way to reduce stress and improve your overall physical fitness.
revised: Pilates may help with balance and controlled movement. It can strengthen the muscles around your middle, often called your core. It may also help you move more freely. Some people find it relaxing.
note: Explains core and replaces guaranteed fitness claims with possible benefits.

original: Spotting is when someone assists you during a lift, especially when you're trying a heavy weight, to help you complete the exercise safely and correctly.
revised: Spotting means having someone ready to help during a lift. A spotter watches and assists if you cannot finish safely. Ask a trainer to show you how spotting works for that exercise.
note: Explains the role and keeps exercise-specific guidance.

original: From the outside inward, Earth's four main layers are the crust, mantle, outer core, and inner core. The crust is the thin outside layer. The mantle lies below it, and the two parts of the core are at the centre.
revised: Earth has four main layers. The crust is the thin outer layer we live on. Below it is the mantle. Deeper inside is the outer core, with the inner core at the center. These names describe the layers from outside to inside.
note: Maps each layer to a simple location.

original: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'. Examples are 'He ran like a cheetah' and 'She sings as sweetly as a bird.'
revised: A simile compares two things using like or as. For example, 'He ran like a cheetah' compares his speed to a cheetah's. 'She sings as sweetly as a bird' is another simile.
note: Explains what the comparison does through the supplied examples.

original: An electromagnet uses electric current to make a magnetic field. One way to make it is to wrap wire around a centre piece, called a core, and pass current through the wire.
revised: An electromagnet is a magnet made using electric current. One design has wire wrapped around a center piece called a core. When current flows through the wire, it creates a magnetic field. That is the area where magnetic effects act.
note: Explains core and field and preserves the electrical safety boundaries.

original: You can make a small demonstration electromagnet, but use a low-voltage educational kit or a teacher-approved setup with supervision. A wire connected directly across a battery can get hot. Never use a wall socket, and disconnect the circuit when you are not testing it.
revised: You can make a small demonstration with a low-voltage learning kit. Use a teacher-approved setup and supervision. A wire across a battery can get hot. Never connect it to a wall socket. Disconnect the circuit when you are not testing it.
note: Explains core and field and preserves the electrical safety boundaries.

original: Clean the walls and repair small holes according to the filler’s instructions. Before sanding or scraping old paint, check whether it could contain lead and get suitable advice if unsure. Follow the paint maker’s guidance for preparing the surface.
revised: Clean the walls and fill small holes, following the filler's instructions. Before sanding old paint, check whether it could contain lead. Get suitable advice if you are unsure. Follow the paint maker's instructions for preparing the wall.
note: Separates preparation steps and preserves lead and product-direction conditions.

original: Latex paint is usually the best choice for living rooms because it's water-based, easy to clean up, and dries quickly. It's also less likely to have strong fumes.
revised: Water-based latex paint is often a useful choice for living-room walls. It usually dries quickly and is easier to clean up than oil-based paint. It may also have less strong-smelling vapor. Follow the product's directions for use and ventilation.
note: Separates preparation steps and preserves lead and product-direction conditions.

original: Use suitable painter’s tape and press its edges down well. Apply paint carefully without flooding the tape edge. Follow the tape maker’s instructions for when to remove it, and pull it off slowly to avoid lifting the paint.
revised: Use painter's tape made for the surface. Press the edges down firmly. Paint carefully without letting paint pool against the tape. Follow the maker's instructions about when to remove it. Pull it off slowly so it does not lift the paint.
note: Separates preparation steps and preserves lead and product-direction conditions.

original: Water pushes upward on an object. The object floats if it pushes aside enough water for that upward force to balance its weight. The whole object's mass compared with its size matters. This is why a hollow object may float even when its material is denser than water.
revised: Water pushes upward on an object. The object floats when that push can balance its weight. To get enough upward push, the object must move enough water aside. Its weight compared with its total size matters. A hollow object may float even if its material alone would sink.
note: Explains displacement without leaving dense force terminology unexplained.

original: It's a good idea to turn the compost pile every week or two to keep it aerated and help it break down faster.
revised: Turning the pile every week or two can help it break down faster. Turning brings air into the material. The best timing depends on the pile and composting method.
note: Explains aeration and makes the schedule conditional.

original: Both take off from a backward outside edge. In a toe loop, the other foot’s toe pick helps push off the ice. In a loop, the skater takes off without that toe-pick assist.
revised: Both jumps start on a backward outside edge of the skate blade. In a toe loop, the other skate's toe pick helps push off. A toe pick is the set of teeth at the front of a blade. In a loop jump, the skater takes off without that extra push.
note: Explains toe pick while retaining the takeoff difference.

original: Common career development goals include learning new skills, taking on more responsibilities, and networking with colleagues and industry leaders.
revised: People often aim to learn a new skill or take on a larger task. Another goal is meeting more people in their field. Choose a goal that supports the kind of work you want to do.
note: Replaces career-development jargon with concrete goals.

original: A good place to start is by planning out your meals for the week. Consider what ingredients you already have at home and what your dietary goals are. You can also look up recipes online for inspiration.
revised: Look at the ingredients you already have. Choose a few meals that use them and fit your needs. Write down the missing ingredients. Start with a simple recipe you can prepare ahead.
note: Turns meal-prep planning into short steps.

original: Teachers are community helpers because they educate and support children, helping them grow and learn new things.
revised: Teachers help children learn skills and understand new ideas. They also support children as they grow. This helps the children and the wider community.
note: Explains the community-helper role in familiar words.

original: About 20,000 years ago, huge ice sheets covered much of northern North America and northern Europe. This time is called the last glacial maximum. Later, the climate warmed and many ice sheets shrank. This was one part of a longer ice age, not the whole ice age.
revised: About 20,000 years ago, huge ice sheets covered parts of North America and Europe. This period is called the last glacial maximum. It was a time when the ice sheets were especially large. Later, the climate warmed and many ice sheets shrank. This period was only one part of a longer ice age.
note: Explains the named period and retains its distinction from the whole ice age.

original: Canis Major means the Great Dog. It is a named star pattern in the southern sky and contains Sirius. You can see it from many places in both the northern and southern halves of Earth.
revised: Canis Major means the Great Dog. It is a constellation, or a named area of sky with a star pattern. It contains the star Sirius. It lies in the southern sky. People in many northern and southern places can see it at suitable times.
note: Explains constellation and keeps visibility conditional.

original: Energy conversion means changing energy from one form to another. For example, a coal power plant uses energy stored in coal to make electricity.
revised: Energy conversion means changing energy from one form to another. A power plant can use energy stored in coal to produce electricity. The energy changes form instead of simply appearing from nowhere.
note: Explains conversion through the given power-plant example.

original: Density tells you how much mass fits into a certain space. A rock is denser than Styrofoam because a same-sized piece has more mass.
revised: Density tells us how much mass is packed into a space. Mass is the amount of matter in something. Compare equal-sized pieces of rock and Styrofoam. The rock has more mass in the same space, so it is denser.
note: Explains mass and makes the same-size comparison explicit.

original: Several factors affect internet speed, including your internet service provider, the type of connection you have (e.g., fiber, cable, or DSL), and the number of devices connected to your network.
revised: Your internet plan and type of connection both matter. Activity on your network matters too. Several devices downloading or streaming at once may share the available speed. Weak Wi-Fi can also slow the connection to your device.
note: Explains bandwidth and separates internet capacity from Wi-Fi coverage.

original: First see whether a device is downloading, streaming, or backing up a lot of data. Pause those tasks and compare the connection near the router or with a cable. A Wi-Fi extender helps only some coverage problems and does not automatically make the internet faster.
revised: Check whether a device is downloading, streaming, or backing up large files. Pause those tasks and test again. Try moving near the router or connecting with a cable. A Wi-Fi extender may help reach a distant room. It does not fix every cause of slow internet.
note: Explains bandwidth and separates internet capacity from Wi-Fi coverage.

original: Bandwidth is the amount of data a connection can carry per second. Think of it as the width of a road for data. More bandwidth can support more activity at once, but delays and weak Wi-Fi can still make a connection feel slow.
revised: Bandwidth is how much data a connection can carry each second. Imagine a road that can carry several cars side by side. More bandwidth can support more activity at once. But weak Wi-Fi or delays can still make the connection feel slow.
note: Explains bandwidth and separates internet capacity from Wi-Fi coverage.

original: That's correct. Carpooling can save you money on fuel, tolls, and vehicle maintenance. It also helps reduce traffic congestion and air pollution.
revised: Carpooling means sharing a car trip with other people. You can split costs such as fuel and tolls. Fewer separate car trips may also reduce traffic and air pollution.
note: Explains carpooling and gives concrete agreement steps.

original: Besides cost savings, carpooling can also reduce stress, provide social interaction, and even offer a more relaxed commute since you can take turns driving.
revised: You can take turns driving if that works for the group. This may make the journey less tiring. You also have time to talk with other people. Whether it feels relaxing depends on the group and trip.
note: Explains carpooling and gives concrete agreement steps.

original: Check whether your workplace or local transport service has a carpool board. You can also look for local groups. Agree on the route, costs, and pickup times before sharing regular trips.
revised: Ask your workplace or local transport service about ride-sharing groups. Local online groups may help too. Before starting, agree on pickup times, the route, and how to share costs.
note: Explains carpooling and gives concrete agreement steps.

original: Dumbbells are small weights you hold in each hand, while barbells are long bars with weights on each end. Dumbbells are more versatile, but barbells allow for heavier lifts.
revised: A dumbbell is a short weight held in one hand. You can move each arm separately with dumbbells. A barbell is a long bar with weights at both ends. It can be useful for heavier lifts. The better choice depends on the exercise and your experience.
note: Explains the equipment without a blanket versatility ranking.

revised: 5 - 3 = 2. If you start with five and take away three, two remain.
note: Adds the concrete meaning of subtraction.

original: Options include marching in place, dancing, or simple step movements. Jumping jacks and burpees are more demanding choices. Pick movements you can do comfortably and make enough clear space around you.
revised: Try marching in place, dancing, or simple stepping movements. These can raise your breathing and heart rate. Jumping jacks and burpees are harder options. Choose movements you can do comfortably and clear enough space around you.
note: Explains cardio and plank and avoids telling the beginner to rush into exercise.

original: Burpees can be demanding because they combine several movements. An easier version can involve stepping back into a plank and returning to standing without a push-up or jump. Learn the movement slowly, and ask a qualified trainer for help if you are unsure of the form.
revised: Burpees can be hard because they combine several movements. An easier version leaves out the push-up and jump. You step back into a plank, then return to standing. A plank is a position with your body held straight. Learn slowly and ask a trainer if you are unsure.
note: Explains cardio and plank and avoids telling the beginner to rush into exercise.

original: No, you don't need any equipment for these exercises. Just find some space in your home, put on some music, and get started!
revised: You do not need special equipment for the basic versions. Use a clear space with a safe surface. You can add music if you enjoy it.
note: Explains cardio and plank and avoids telling the beginner to rush into exercise.

original: A theatre director needs to explain ideas clearly, work well with others, and notice details. They also need creative ideas and a clear picture of how to tell the story on stage.
revised: A theater director needs to explain ideas clearly and work well with people. They must notice details and make creative choices. They also need a clear idea of how the story should appear on stage.
note: Keeps the skill list in connected short sentences.

original: You can join a reading challenge. Many libraries and book clubs offer challenges where you can set a goal for the number of books to read in a year and track your progress.
revised: Try a reading challenge from a library or book club. You choose a goal, such as a number of books to read this year. Keep a list of the books you finish. Pick a goal that makes reading enjoyable rather than stressful.
note: Explains the challenge and progress tracking.

original: Communication is key in any family. Setting aside dedicated time to talk and actively listening to each other can really help.
revised: Choose a time when everyone can talk without rushing. Let each person finish before others reply. Try to understand what they mean before giving your own view.
note: Explains listening and boundaries through family actions.

original: Discuss what each person needs, such as privacy, quiet time, or shared chores. Agree on clear, realistic rules together and revisit them when circumstances change. Boundaries should be respectful; they are not a way to control every part of someone else’s life.
revised: Talk about what each person needs, such as privacy, quiet time, or help with chores. Agree on clear rules you can realistically follow. Review them when your situation changes. A boundary protects a person's needs. It should not control every part of someone else's life.
note: Explains listening and boundaries through family actions.

original: Community theaters often produce different shows, including classic plays, musicals, and original works. They may also offer children's productions, comedy acts, and other special events.
revised: You may see older plays, musicals, or new plays written for the group. Some theaters also stage children's shows or comedy. Check the local program, since each theater offers different events.
note: Replaces production jargon with familiar show descriptions.

original: A decade is 10 years.
revised: A decade is 10 years.
note: Already a complete simple definition.

original: Generally, subways are safe, but it's always a good idea to be aware of your surroundings and keep an eye on your belongings.
revised: Many people use subways safely every day. Still, pay attention to what is happening around you. Keep your belongings close and follow station guidance. Safety can vary with the place and situation.
note: Avoids promising safety for an unspecified subway.

original: A smile, for instance, can convey friendliness and approachability without saying a word. It's a simple yet effective example of how non-verbal cues can communicate a lot.
revised: A smile can show friendliness without words. It may make someone feel more comfortable starting a conversation. The situation still matters, since a smile does not always mean the same thing.
note: Explains the example without assuming a universal gesture meaning.

original: Use less plastic, share car trips or use public transport, and support groups that protect wildlife and the places it lives.
revised: Help protect the places where wildlife lives. You can support local conservation groups and reduce plastic waste. Sharing car trips or using public transport can also reduce pollution. These steps can help protect the living things linked in food chains.
note: Explains the connection between actions and food chains.

original: Ceramics include pottery, bricks, and porcelain. They are non-metal materials often made by shaping and heating clay or similar ingredients. Many are hard and cope well with heat, but can break if hit.
revised: Ceramics include pottery, bricks, and porcelain. They are materials that are not metal. Many are made by shaping clay and heating it strongly. They are often hard and resist heat. But they can crack or break when hit.
note: Explains ceramic properties with familiar verbs.

original: You might want to update the fixtures, such as the sink and toilet, and consider new tile for the floor and shower. Adding a double vanity or more storage can also be helpful.
revised: Common changes include a new sink, toilet, or floor tiles. You might also replace shower tiles or add storage. A cabinet with two sinks is another option if there is enough room. Choose changes that fit your space and needs.
note: Explains double vanity and keeps space limits.

original: Transparent materials allow light to pass through, like glass or water, while opaque materials block light, like wood or metal.
revised: Transparent materials let light through so you can see clearly through them. Clear glass is one example. Opaque materials block light, so you cannot see through them. Wood and metal are common examples.
note: Explains each light-transmission term and preserves clear versus cloudy distinctions.

original: Some common examples of transparent materials include windows, ice, and clear plastics.
revised: Examples include clear window glass, clear ice, and clear plastic. Cloudy versions may let some light through without giving a clear view.
note: Explains each light-transmission term and preserves clear versus cloudy distinctions.

original: Yes. Frosted glass lets light through but sends it in different directions, so you cannot see a clear image through it. This is called translucent. Tinted clear glass mainly reduces the amount of light while keeping the view clear.
revised: Yes. Frosted glass lets light through but scatters it in different directions. You cannot see a clear picture through it. This is called translucent. Tinted clear glass is different. It reduces the light but can still leave the view clear.
note: Explains each light-transmission term and preserves clear versus cloudy distinctions.

original: That sounds like a great initiative. To get started, you can begin by identifying the areas that need the most attention, such as parks or streets with a lot of litter. Then, reach out to your local government or community organizations to see if they can provide any support or resources.
revised: Choose an area that needs cleaning, such as a park with litter. Decide which part your group can realistically cover. Ask the local council or a community group about support and supplies.
note: Turns event planning into clear practical stages.

original: You can use social media to spread the word and create an event page to invite people. You can also post flyers in local businesses and community centers. Also, consider offering incentives, such as free food or drinks, to those who participate.
revised: Share the time, meeting place, and tasks on social media. Put up notices where local people will see them, with permission. Explain what people should bring. Simple refreshments may encourage people to stay and help.
note: Turns event planning into clear practical stages.

original: To make a lasting impact, consider partnering with local schools or community groups to make the event a regular occurrence. You can also encourage participants to take ownership of the event by assigning them specific tasks or areas to focus on. Finally, be sure to follow up after the event to thank participants and gather feedback for future events.
revised: Give volunteers clear tasks or areas to clean. Work with local groups if you want to repeat the event. Afterwards, thank the volunteers and ask what could work better. Use their ideas to plan the next cleanup.
note: Turns event planning into clear practical stages.

original: Relaxed fit clothing is looser and more spacious than regular fit, allowing for a full range of motion and greater comfort.
revised: Relaxed-fit clothes are looser than regular-fit clothes. They leave more room around your body. This may make movement more comfortable, depending on the garment and fit.
note: Explains the cut without guaranteeing comfort.

original: One of the most important things to do is to wash your hands often, especially after using the restroom and before eating.
revised: Washing your hands is one useful habit. Do it after using the toilet and before eating. It helps reduce the spread of germs.
note: Resolves the source's inconsistency about routine disinfection.

original: Clean up spills and crumbs, keep shared equipment tidy, and wash your hands at useful times. Use a product suitable for each surface; disinfection is not always needed for routine cleaning.
revised: Wipe up spills and remove crumbs. Keep shared equipment tidy. Choose a cleaner that is safe for each surface. Disinfecting means using a product to kill germs. It is not always needed for ordinary cleaning.
note: Resolves the source's inconsistency about routine disinfection.

original: Look for products that are labeled as 'disinfectants' and follow the instructions on the label. You can also use a mixture of soap and water to clean surfaces.
revised: For ordinary cleaning, use a suitable cleaner or soap and water where the surface allows it. If disinfection is needed, use a product labelled for that purpose. Follow the label instructions, including how long it must stay on the surface.
note: Resolves source inconsistency about mandatory disinfectant for routine cleaning; CDC cleaning guidance checked, with product and workplace directions still relevant.

original: To convert a fraction to a decimal, you divide the top number by the bottom number. For example, the fraction 3/4 becomes the decimal 0.75 when you divide 3 by 4.
revised: Divide the top number by the bottom number. For example, 3/4 means 3 divided by 4. The result is 0.75. That is the fraction written as a decimal.
note: Makes the conversion a short worked example.

original: People differ in how strictly they follow schedules and how they balance time with relationships. Customs can vary between communities, workplaces, and situations. It is too simple to assign one view of time to a whole country or culture.
revised: People differ in how closely they follow a schedule. Expectations may change between a workplace and a family gathering. They can also vary within the same community. It is too simple to give a whole country one view of time.
note: Keeps the cultural discussion tied to situations rather than stereotypes.

original: For example, a workplace may expect meetings to start exactly on time, while a family gathering may have a flexible start. Ask what is expected in that setting instead of guessing from someone’s background.
revised: For example, a meeting may be expected to start exactly on time. A family party may have a more flexible start. Ask what people expect in that situation. Do not guess only from someone's background.
note: Keeps the cultural discussion tied to situations rather than stereotypes.

original: Yes. It helps to learn what people expect and agree on times clearly. Individual preferences matter as well as shared customs.
revised: Yes. Learn what others expect and agree on clear times. Shared customs can matter, but individual preferences matter too.
note: Keeps the cultural discussion tied to situations rather than stereotypes.

original: An adoptive family is a family. Adoption creates a parent-child relationship, even when the parent and child are not biologically related.
revised: An adoptive family is a family too. Adoption makes someone a child's parent. They do not need to be related by birth.
note: Explains adoption without biological jargon.

original: Gases such as carbon dioxide and methane trap heat and affect the climate. Cutting down forests, pollution, and burning coal and oil also affect it.
revised: Gases such as carbon dioxide and methane trap heat in the air. Burning coal and oil adds heat-trapping gases. Cutting down forests also affects the climate. Other forms of pollution can affect it too.
note: Separates causes and preserves the main role of human activity.

original: Yes. Volcanoes and changes in Earth's path around the Sun affect climate too. But human activities are the main cause of the climate change happening now.
revised: Yes. Volcanoes and changes in Earth's path around the Sun can affect climate. But human activities are the main cause of the warming happening now.
note: Separates causes and preserves the main role of human activity.

original: Turn off lights and devices when you are not using them. Using less energy can reduce your effect on the climate.
revised: Turn off lights and devices when you do not need them. This saves electricity. Using less energy can reduce the pollution linked to producing it.
note: Separates causes and preserves the main role of human activity.

original: Yes, that's right. When you have clear goals, you know what you're working towards and can focus your efforts. This can help you stay motivated and achieve more.
revised: Yes. A clear goal tells you what you are trying to achieve. It helps you decide which tasks matter most. You can also check whether your work is moving you toward that goal.
note: Explains how a goal affects actions and review.

original: The wingers spread out on the sides and help the striker. The three central midfielders control the pace of play and create chances to score.
revised: The wingers play toward the sides and support the main striker. Wingers are the wide attacking players. The three central midfielders work in the middle of the field. They help control the pace and create chances to score.
note: Explains positional jargon in the tactic.

original: Look for a tool that lets you save meals, build a grocery list, and check what you already have. A shared note or spreadsheet may be enough; you do not need a special app to get started.
revised: Choose a tool that stores meals and makes a shopping list. It should also help you check ingredients you already have. A shared note or spreadsheet may be enough. You do not need a special app to begin.
note: Makes tool criteria plain without adding unnecessary products.

original: Some popular vegetarian main courses include vegetable stir-fry, pasta primavera, and veggie burgers.
revised: Try a vegetable stir-fry, vegetable pasta, or a veggie burger. Pasta primavera is pasta with vegetables. Check ingredients such as sauces and toppings if you need the whole meal to be vegetarian.
note: Explains primavera and preserves ingredient suitability.

original: Weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces that become part of soil. Rocks can break through physical forces, chemical reactions, or the action of living things. These are called mechanical, chemical, and biological weathering.
revised: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces. Those pieces become part of soil. Physical forces can break rock apart, such as water freezing in cracks. Chemical changes can alter the rock. Living things, such as growing roots, can break it too. These are physical, chemical, and biological weathering.
note: Explains the three types through actions and examples.

original: Adding plants can really brighten up a room. Some popular indoor plants for living rooms include snake plants, spider plants, and peace lilies. They're all easy to care for and look great.
revised: Snake plants, spider plants, and peace lilies are common indoor choices. Check how much light your room gets. Then choose a plant with care needs you can meet. No plant is easy in every room.
note: Avoids the source's blanket easy-care promise.

original: In healthcare, some main job categories include medical professionals like doctors and nurses, administrative roles like hospital managers, and support staff like medical assistants and technicians.
revised: Doctors and nurses provide patient care. Hospital managers organize services and staff. Medical assistants and technicians carry out support tasks or work with equipment. Healthcare includes both care jobs and jobs that help services run.
note: Explains broad job groups through their work.

original: Changing weather can bring droughts, floods, and extreme temperatures. These can damage crops and reduce how much farmers harvest.
revised: Droughts, floods, and extreme heat or cold can harm crops. Changing weather can make these risks harder to manage. Farmers may harvest less food when crops are damaged.
note: Explains organizational roles and preserves location limits.

original: They can protect soil, use water carefully, vary planting times, and choose crops suited to changing conditions. The useful approach depends on the farm, so local advice and forecasts matter.
revised: Farmers can protect soil, use water carefully, and change planting times. They can also choose crops suited to changing conditions. The best approach depends on the farm. Local advice and weather forecasts can help.
note: Explains organizational roles and preserves location limits.

original: In the United States, NOAA and the USDA provide information and support. They can help farmers plan for changing weather and climate.
revised: In the United States, NOAA provides weather and climate information. The USDA, the Department of Agriculture, also offers farming information and support. Farmers can use these resources to plan for changing conditions.
note: Explains organizational roles and preserves location limits.

original: Yes, one tip is to set a regular family meeting time, so everyone can share their thoughts and opinions.
revised: Set aside a regular time for family discussions. Let each person explain their view without being interrupted. Make sure everyone knows which decision you need to make.
note: Explains compromise through the action it involves.

original: In that case, try to focus on finding a compromise that works for everyone, and remind each other that it's okay to disagree sometimes.
revised: Look for a compromise: a choice where people each give up something. Ask which needs matter most to each person. You may not agree on everything, and that is okay. Try to find a decision everyone can live with.
note: Explains compromise through the action it involves.

original: Look for an action game with a tutorial and difficulty settings you can change. Games in the Uncharted series combine action with a story, but comfort with aiming and movement varies. Watching some gameplay can help you decide whether it suits you.
revised: Look for a game with a beginner tutorial and adjustable difficulty. A tutorial teaches the controls as you play. The Uncharted games mix action and story. Watch some gameplay first to see whether the movement and aiming suit you.
note: Explains tutorial and avoids guaranteeing a named game is easy.

original: Start with activities that suit your current fitness and build up gradually. Soccer practice can combine endurance work, ball skills, strength, and agility. A coach can help you plan sessions that fit your level and schedule.
revised: Start at a level that suits your current fitness. Practise ball skills as well as running. Strength work and quick changes of direction can also help. Build up gradually. A coach can help you combine these into a suitable plan.
note: Explains agility and endurance through actual soccer activities.

original: Reflection is when light bounces off a surface. For example, when you look in a mirror, the light from your face bounces off the mirror and back to your eyes, so you can see yourself.
revised: Reflection means light bouncing off a surface. In a mirror, light from your face bounces back toward your eyes. That is why you can see your face in it.
note: Breaks the mirror explanation into short sentences.

original: Let use and dirt guide you. Do laundry when you have enough for a load, and clean bathroom surfaces when they need it. A regular weekly check can help you notice what needs attention; a busy shared bathroom may need more frequent cleaning.
revised: Do laundry when you have enough clothes for a load. Clean bathroom surfaces when they are dirty or need attention. Check the bathroom regularly, such as once a week. A busy shared bathroom may need cleaning more often.
note: Keeps cleaning frequency based on actual use.

original: Weight is the force exerted on an object by gravity, while mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object.
revised: Mass tells us how much matter an object contains. Weight is the pull of gravity on that object. Gravity is the force that pulls objects toward each other. Your mass can stay the same while your weight changes.
note: Explains gravity and retains the mass-versus-weight distinction.

original: No, you would weigh less on the moon because the moon has less gravity than Earth. However, your mass would still be 70 kilograms.
revised: Your mass would still be 70 kilograms. But you would weigh less on the Moon. The Moon pulls you downward less strongly than Earth does.
note: Explains gravity and retains the mass-versus-weight distinction.

original: Follow a tested gluten-free cake recipe and use its specified flour blend. Some blends already contain a binder, such as xanthan gum, so adding more can change the texture.
revised: Use a tested gluten-free cake recipe and the flour mix it names. Some mixes already contain an ingredient that holds the cake together. Xanthan gum is one example of that kind of ingredient. Adding more than the recipe needs can change the cake's texture.
note: Explains binder and makes flour guidance recipe-specific.

original: Buses are a common way to travel to school. Use a seatbelt if one is provided, stay seated where required, and follow the driver’s instructions. Not all buses have seatbelts.
revised: Buses are a common way to get to school. Follow the driver's instructions and stay seated where required. Use a seatbelt if there is one. Not all buses have seatbelts.
note: Keeps bus-specific safety instructions clear.

original: Follow the driver or staff instructions and move away from danger if needed. Notice the marked emergency exits when you board. In an immediate emergency, seek help through the local emergency number.
revised: Follow instructions from the driver or staff. Move away from immediate danger if needed. When you board, notice where the marked emergency exits are. In an urgent emergency, call the local emergency number for help.
note: Keeps bus-specific safety instructions clear.

original: I'd be happy to help you with your shopping list. What items do you need to pick up?
revised: What do you need to buy? I can help put the items into a list.
note: Preserves the memory limit and gives a practical alternative.

original: I can keep them in mind during this conversation: milk, eggs, and bread. I cannot promise they will be saved for a future chat. You could keep a reusable shopping list in a notes app and copy it when needed.
revised: I can remember milk, eggs, and bread during this conversation. I cannot promise they will stay saved for a future chat. Keep a reusable list in your phone's notes app. You can copy it when you need it.
note: Preserves the memory limit and gives a practical alternative.

original: A space rock could pose a risk if its path crosses Earth’s at the same time. NASA tracks nearby objects and estimates their chances of impact. Small pieces often burn up in the atmosphere, but larger objects cannot be assumed to do so.
revised: An object could hit Earth if their paths meet at the same time. NASA tracks nearby space objects and estimates the risk. Many small pieces burn up in the atmosphere. Larger objects may not. Current risk lists are needed to identify any specific threat.
note: Explains collision timing and avoids inventing a current named threat.

original: The right amount depends on your dog’s age, health, fitness, and breed. Choose a pace and length your dog manages comfortably, with time to sniff and rest. A vet can advise on special limits.
revised: The right walk length depends on your dog's age, health, fitness, and breed. Choose a pace your dog can manage comfortably. Allow time to sniff and rest. A vet can advise if your dog has special limits.
note: Keeps walking advice individual rather than assigning a fixed duration.

original: There isn't really an "opposite" of a cube, but some people might consider a sphere as a contrasting shape, since it's curved and has no corners or edges.
revised: A cube has no mathematical opposite. A sphere is a contrasting shape because it is round and has no corners. But it is not formally the opposite of a cube.
note: Separates an informal contrast from a mathematical relationship.

original: Sports psychology studies how thoughts and feelings affect an athlete's performance and well-being.
revised: Sports psychology looks at how thoughts and feelings affect athletes. It studies both performance and how athletes feel in their lives.
note: Explains psychology techniques through a labelled sports example.

original: Athletes may imagine doing a task well, practise encouraging self-talk, or focus on the present through meditation. These can help them handle pressure and pay attention.
revised: Athletes may picture themselves doing a task well. They may practise using encouraging words in their thoughts. Some also train themselves to focus on what is happening now. These methods can help with pressure and attention.
note: Explains psychology techniques through a labelled sports example.

original: One simple way to visualize is to close your eyes, imagine yourself successfully performing a specific task or game, and focus on the sights, sounds, and feelings of success.
revised: Imagine practising a free throw in basketball. Picture holding the ball, bending your knees, and making the shot. Think about the movement and what you would see and hear. This kind of mental practice is called visualization.
note: Explains psychology techniques through a labelled sports example.

original: Radishes, lettuce, and bush beans are common beginner options, but the best choice depends on your climate, season, and sunlight. Tomatoes and cucumbers need suitable warmth and light. No vegetable thrives in every condition.
revised: Radishes, lettuce, and bush beans are common beginner choices. The best option depends on your season, climate, and sunlight. Tomatoes and cucumbers need suitable warmth and light. Choose plants that fit your conditions.
note: Explains bed layout and preserves need-based watering.

original: Rows, raised beds, and containers can all work. Follow the spacing on the seed packet or plant label, since different vegetables need very different amounts of room. Avoid crowding and leave access for watering and harvesting.
revised: You can use rows, raised beds, or containers. A raised bed holds soil above the surrounding ground. Follow the spacing on the seed packet or plant label. Leave room to reach the plants for watering and picking.
note: Explains bed layout and preserves need-based watering.

original: Morning is often convenient because there is less heat and time for wet leaves to dry. Water the soil near the roots and check whether it needs moisture first. If plants need water later in the day, do not leave them dry just because it is not morning.
revised: Morning often works well because it is cooler. Wet leaves also have time to dry. Check whether the soil needs water before adding more. Water near the roots. If plants need water later, do not leave them dry just because morning has passed.
note: Explains bed layout and preserves need-based watering.

original: Measure the space first and think about how much food your household stores. Then choose the features you need, such as an ice maker or water dispenser.
revised: Measure the space for the fridge first. Think about how much food your household stores. Then choose extra features you need, such as an ice maker. Make sure the model fits both the space and your daily use.
note: Explains the energy label and treats reviews as evidence with limits.

original: Yes, look for the ENERGY STAR label, which indicates that the appliance meets energy efficiency standards set by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. This can help you save money on your utility bills.
revised: In the United States, look for the ENERGY STAR mark. It shows that the fridge meets rules for using less energy. Also check the yellow EnergyGuide label. It estimates yearly energy use and running costs. Compare fridges of similar size. The ENERGY STAR mark may appear on the EnergyGuide label too. Your actual costs depend on how you use the fridge and your electricity price.
note: Cross-review factual repair: distinguishes ENERGY STAR certification from the yellow EnergyGuide estimates. Explains comparison and actual-cost limits using FTC and ENERGY STAR guidance.

original: Read customer reviews to learn how well a model works and whether it tends to break. This can help you spot possible problems before buying.
revised: Read reviews about the specific model. Look for repeated reports of faults or poor performance. Reviews can help you spot issues, though one review does not tell the whole story.
note: Explains the energy label and treats reviews as evidence with limits.

original: You can try searching online for "community theater near me" or check local newspapers and event calendars for listings. You can also ask friends, family, or coworkers for recommendations.
revised: Search for community theater near your town. Check local event calendars and newspapers too. Friends or coworkers may know groups nearby.
note: Gives a short concrete search route.

original: Reading quickly for the main ideas gives you a first picture of the topic. The details may then make more sense when you read carefully. It can also save time and help you organize what you learn.
revised: Skimming gives you a quick overview before you read closely. Headings and main sentences show what the text is about. Knowing that outline can help the details make sense later.
note: Explains the overview benefit without optimizing only for reading speed.

original: There are many types of pet grooming tools available, such as brushes, nail clippers, and shampoos.
revised: Common grooming tools include brushes and nail clippers. Shampoos are grooming products too. The right choice depends on the animal and its needs.
note: Separates tools from products and preserves coat-specific advice.

original: The best brush depends on your cat’s coat and tolerance. Use a suitable grooming brush gently, without pulling at mats or scraping the skin. A groomer or vet can help if the coat is badly tangled or you are unsure.
revised: Choose a brush suited to your cat's coat. Use it gently without scraping the skin or pulling at tangled fur. If the fur is badly tangled, ask a groomer or vet for help. Your cat's comfort matters too.
note: Separates tools from products and preserves coat-specific advice.

original: You can find pet grooming brushes at most pet stores or online retailers, such as Petco or Amazon.
revised: Look in pet stores or online pet shops. Petco and Amazon are examples of places that may sell brushes. Check that the brush suits your cat before buying.
note: Separates tools from products and preserves coat-specific advice.

original: Yes, most video call apps allow you to use a virtual background. You can usually find this option in the app's settings.
revised: Many video-call apps can blur or replace your background. A replacement image is called a virtual background. Look in the app's settings for background or effects options.
note: Explains virtual backgrounds and keeps interface steps conditional.

original: Usually, you can select a virtual background before or during a call by clicking on a button or icon that says 'Background' or 'Effects'. Then, you can choose from a list of available backgrounds or upload your own.
revised: Look for a button called Background or Effects before or during the call. Choose an image from the available options. Some apps also let you upload your own. The exact steps depend on your app.
note: Explains virtual backgrounds and keeps interface steps conditional.

original: A simple example is a smile. When you smile at someone, it can convey friendliness and approachability without you saying a word.
revised: A smile is one example. It can show friendliness without spoken words. Its meaning still depends on the person and situation.
note: Explains nonverbal communication without a fixed gesture interpretation.

original: A good length for a power nap is 15-20 minutes. This allows you to recharge without entering deep sleep, which can leave you feeling groggy.
revised: A short nap of about 20 minutes is a common starting point. Longer naps can make some people feel groggy afterwards. Groggy means sleepy and slow to feel alert. The best length varies, so this is not a guarantee.
note: Safety/accuracy review: replaces a guaranteed sleep-stage claim with a short example and variable grogginess; Mayo guidance checked.

original: Power naps can improve alertness, boost memory, and increase productivity. They can also help reduce stress and fatigue.
revised: A short nap may help you feel more awake and less tired. It can also support attention and memory. Some people find it reduces stress. The effects vary from person to person.
note: Removes an unsupported exact screen cutoff and avoids guaranteed sleep-stage claims.

original: Try to create a quiet and comfortable environment, and avoid screens for at least 10 minutes before your nap. You can also try deep breathing exercises to relax your mind and body.
revised: Choose a quiet, comfortable place and set an alarm. Put away your screen so you can settle down. Try a few slow, comfortable breaths. You do not need to force yourself to fall asleep immediately.
note: Removes an unsupported exact screen cutoff and avoids guaranteed sleep-stage claims.

original: The front end is the part of a website people see and use in a browser, such as buttons and pages. The back end runs on a server and handles work such as storing data and checking sign-ins. Languages such as JavaScript and Python can be used on the back end.
revised: The front end is what people see and use on a website. Buttons, menus, and pages are examples. The back end does work on a server, a computer that provides the website's services. It may store data or check sign-ins. JavaScript and Python can be used for back-end work.
note: Explains server and gives concrete tasks for each side.

original: Sunshine is wonderful, isn't it? It's also a great source of solar energy. Many people use solar panels to convert sunlight into electricity.
revised: A sunny day can be lovely. Sunlight can also provide energy. Solar panels turn some of that light into electricity.
note: Keeps the casual reply short and explains the energy link.

original: Examples include bodyweight squats, wall push-ups, and lunges. With dumbbells or bands, you can also try simple curls or rows after learning the movement. Choose exercises you can do comfortably and ask a qualified trainer for help with technique.
revised: You could try squats, wall push-ups, or lunges. Start with versions you can do comfortably. Weights or exercise bands give you other options. Learn each movement first, and ask a trainer if you need help with your form.
note: Explains the practical beginner sequence without a dense exercise list.

original: Gentle calf, hip, and back-of-thigh stretches can help work on flexibility. Move slowly and choose a comfortable range. Calf raises mainly build strength rather than serving as a stretch.
revised: Try gentle stretches for your calves, hips, and the backs of your thighs. Your calves are the muscles at the back of your lower legs. Move slowly and stop before the stretch hurts. Calf raises mainly build strength; they are not the same as a stretch.
note: Explains calf and preserves stretching versus strengthening.

original: That sounds like a great idea! Retro gaming is a wonderful hobby. There are many classic consoles and games you can play again, like the NES, SNES, or even arcade games.
revised: You could return to retro gaming, which means playing older-style games. Original NES or SNES games are examples. Old arcade games may also bring back memories. Start with a game you remember enjoying.
note: Explains retro and gives a concrete starting choice.

original: Personal style often evolves as you get older and your lifestyle changes. For example, you may dress more formally for work or more casually in your free time. Your style may also be influenced by trends, experiences, and the people around you.
revised: Your style can change as your life and preferences change. You may need different clothes for work or new activities. Trends, experiences, and people around you can also influence what you enjoy wearing.
note: Avoids a mandatory wardrobe template and explains lasting usefulness.

original: Yes. Preferences can change with experience, lifestyle, or mood. Neutral colors are not more mature than bright ones; choose what feels right to you now.
revised: Yes. Your taste can change with your life, mood, or experiences. Neutral colors are not more mature than bright ones. Choose the colors you like now.
note: Avoids a mandatory wardrobe template and explains lasting usefulness.

original: Start by investing in a few high-quality, essential pieces that fit well, such as a classic coat, a good pair of jeans, and a simple white shirt. From there, you can add more statement pieces that reflect your personal style.
revised: Start with well-made clothes that fit and suit your daily life. Examples might include a coat, jeans, and a simple shirt. Choose pieces you can wear in several outfits. Then add more distinctive items if you enjoy them.
note: Avoids a mandatory wardrobe template and explains lasting usefulness.

original: Electricity involves electric charges. Charges can build up in one place, as with static electricity, or move through a circuit as a current. Electrical energy powers many devices.
revised: Electricity involves electric charges, a property of tiny particles in matter. Charges can build up in one place, making static electricity. They can also move through a circuit, forming an electric current. A circuit is a connected path. Electrical energy powers many everyday devices.
note: Explains charge, current, and circuit in simple connected sentences.

original: Cotton, fleece, and modal are common choices. Cotton and modal are fibers used to make fabric; fleece is a soft, fuzzy type of fabric that can be made from different fibers. Feel the material and check its weight, since comfort varies.
revised: Cotton, fleece, and modal are common in loungewear. Cotton and modal are fibers used to make cloth. Fleece is a soft, fuzzy fabric made from various fibers. Feel the fabric and check how thick it is. Comfort differs between garments.
note: Explains fabric categories while preserving comfort variation.

original: You can search online for breed-specific rescues in your area, or check websites like Petfinder or Adoptapet.com, which allow you to filter by breed and location.
revised: Search for rescue groups for that breed near your town. Petfinder and Adoptapet.com may also help you search by breed and location. Check the group's details before contacting it.
note: Makes the breed-rescue search concrete.

original: Traditionally, a black bow tie is worn for a black-tie event, but some events may allow for other colors or patterns.
revised: Black is the traditional bow-tie color for black tie. Follow the event's dress code. Other colors or patterns are suitable only if the hosts allow them.
note: Makes the formal default and possible exception clear.

original: That's great! You can stay close to your grandparents by calling or video chatting with them regularly, sharing stories and photos, or helping them with tasks and errands.
revised: Call or video-chat regularly if they enjoy that. Share photos and stories from your life. You can also help with a task or errand when needed.
note: Keeps consent and makes preserving stories step-by-step.

original: You can do things like baking, gardening, or playing board games together. You can also ask them about their childhood and listen to their stories.
revised: You could bake, garden, or play board games together. Choose something everyone feels comfortable doing. Asking about their childhood can also lead to good conversations.
note: Keeps consent and makes preserving stories step-by-step.

original: With their permission, record the stories or write them down. Add names, places, and dates when you can. Keep a backup, and ask before sharing personal stories with other people.
revised: Ask permission before recording their stories. You can also write them down. Add names, places, and dates when possible. Keep a backup copy. Ask before sharing private stories with anyone else.
note: Keeps consent and makes preserving stories step-by-step.

original: Remove dangerous items and lock away harmful substances. Block places the pet should not enter. Set up areas for food, water, and sleep.
revised: Remove dangerous items and lock away harmful substances. Block places the pet should not enter. Set up areas for food, water, and sleep.
note: Already clear safety steps with familiar words.

original: Some popular breakfast meats are bacon, sausage, and ham.
revised: Some popular breakfast meats are bacon, sausage, and ham.
note: Both turns are already brief clear examples.

original: Yes, there are others like Canadian bacon and chorizo.
revised: Yes, there are others like Canadian bacon and chorizo.
note: Both turns are already brief clear examples.

original: The Olympic Village is where athletes and team officials stay during the Olympics. It's usually a specially built area with accommodations, dining, and recreational facilities.
revised: The Olympic Village is where athletes and team staff stay during the Games. It has places to sleep and eat. There are usually shared spaces for rest and other activities too.
note: Explains accommodation and recreational facilities plainly.

original: Organic gardening focuses on soil health, compost, and methods such as crop rotation and physical pest control. It avoids many synthetic inputs. Natural products still need careful use.
revised: Organic gardening aims to care for the soil and avoid many manufactured chemicals. Gardeners may add compost and change which crops grow in each bed. They may also remove pests by hand or use barriers. Natural products still need careful use.
note: Explains growing methods and preserves the safety and nutrition limits.

original: It can build soil, encourage useful wildlife, and reduce reliance on some pesticides. It does not automatically make every crop safer or more nutritious. Good care and safe handling still matter.
revised: It can improve soil and support helpful wildlife. It may reduce the need for some pest-control chemicals. But organic growing does not automatically make food safer or more nutritious. Careful growing and food handling still matter.
note: Explains growing methods and preserves the safety and nutrition limits.

original: Choose something suited to your space and season, such as beans, lettuce, or a herb. Organic describes how it is grown, not a special type of tomato. Start with a small bed or container.
revised: Start with a small bed or pot. Choose a plant that suits the space and season, such as lettuce or beans. Organic describes the growing method. It is not a special type of plant.
note: Explains growing methods and preserves the safety and nutrition limits.

original: At family celebrations, achievements are often recognized through speeches, awards, or personalized gifts. You could also create a photo album or a customized video showcasing your sister's accomplishments.
revised: You could give a short speech about something your sister achieved. A personal gift or small award is another option. You might also make a photo album or video showing her school years. Choose something she would enjoy sharing with the family.
note: Turns recognition into concrete celebration choices.

original: Sorry to hear that. Poor internet connection is often the cause of bad video call quality. Are you using a stable internet connection?
revised: An unstable internet connection can cause poor video quality. Does the picture freeze or look blurry? Are you using a stable connection?
note: Keeps troubleshooting conditional and distinguishes connection from Wi-Fi quality.

original: It could be. Wi-Fi can still be weak even when you are connected. Try moving closer to the router, improving the light on your face, and checking the camera settings. Then see whether the problem happens in other apps too.
revised: Yes, the camera could matter, but being on Wi-Fi does not guarantee a strong signal. Try moving closer to the router. Add light in front of your face and check camera settings. Then test another app to see whether the problem happens there too.
note: Keeps troubleshooting conditional and distinguishes connection from Wi-Fi quality.

original: Tokyo has many great spots for night photography. Some popular locations include the Tokyo Tower, Shibuya Crossing, and the neon-lit streets of Shinjuku.
revised: Tokyo Tower, Shibuya Crossing, and the bright streets of Shinjuku are familiar night-photo locations. Each offers different views of city lights.
note: Explains ISO, shutter, aperture, and exposure through their visible effects.

original: For still city scenes, try a tripod and a low ISO, which reduces image noise. A slower shutter can turn moving lights into trails. Take a test photo and adjust the exposure so bright signs do not lose all detail.
revised: For a still scene, use a tripod to hold the camera steady. Try a low ISO setting to reduce grainy specks in the picture. A slower shutter keeps the camera collecting light longer. Moving lights can then form trails. Take a test photo and adjust so bright signs still show detail.
note: Explains ISO, shutter, aperture, and exposure through their visible effects.

original: Choose a dark place away from city lights. Use a wide lens, a wide aperture to let in light, and a tripod. Take test shots and shorten the exposure if stars become streaks; the useful settings depend on your lens and camera.
revised: Find a dark place away from city lights. Use a tripod and a lens that captures a wide view. A wide aperture is a larger lens opening that lets in more light. Take test photos. Shorten the exposure time if stars turn into lines instead of points.
note: Explains ISO, shutter, aperture, and exposure through their visible effects.

original: With a black suit, you can't go wrong with a classic choice like a white or light-colored tie. However, if you want to add some personality, a burgundy or dark blue tie can also look great.
revised: A light-colored, burgundy, or dark blue tie can work with a black suit. Choose one that also suits your shirt and the wedding's dress code.
note: Explains accessories and avoids making cufflinks necessary for every shirt.

original: A white or light-colored pocket square is a safe choice that will complement your tie and suit. You can also match your pocket square to your tie for a more cohesive look.
revised: A white pocket square is a simple choice. A pocket square is the folded cloth in a jacket's chest pocket. It can go with the colors of your tie without matching exactly.
note: Explains accessories and avoids making cufflinks necessary for every shirt.

original: For a black suit, simple and elegant cufflinks like silver or mother-of-pearl are great choices. They'll add a touch of sophistication without drawing attention away from the rest of your outfit.
revised: If your shirt needs cufflinks, simple silver-colored ones can work well. Cufflinks fasten the shirt cuffs instead of buttons. Choose a quiet design that fits the rest of the outfit.
note: Explains accessories and avoids making cufflinks necessary for every shirt.

original: You're welcome! I hope you look great at the wedding!
revised: You're welcome. Enjoy the wedding.
note: Explains accessories and avoids making cufflinks necessary for every shirt.

original: A circle is a flat, round shape. Every point on its boundary is the same distance from its center, and it has no corners.
revised: A circle is a flat, round shape with no corners. Every point on its edge is the same distance from the center.
note: Explains boundary as edge while retaining the defining property.

original: Brown rice is a popular choice to pair with lentils. They complement each other well in terms of texture and flavor.
revised: Brown rice goes well with lentils. Its flavor and firmer texture can work well alongside them.
note: Explains the texture difference without making one lentil type mandatory.

original: Green lentils usually hold their shape, while split red lentils soften and break down more quickly. Either can go with brown rice; choose the texture you want and follow the cooking time for that type.
revised: Green lentils usually keep their shape when cooked. Split red lentils soften and break apart more quickly. Either can go with brown rice. Choose the texture you want and follow the cooking instructions for that type.
note: Explains the texture difference without making one lentil type mandatory.

original: Yes, virtual concerts have gained popularity, especially during the pandemic. Many artists have performed online, and it's a great way to enjoy live music from anywhere.
revised: Virtual concerts are concerts you watch online. Many artists used them during the pandemic. They let people watch from places far from the venue, if they have internet access.
note: Explains the format without claiming a current popularity level.

original: Powder is loose, dry snow, usually found in colder conditions. Wetter snow contains more liquid water and sticks together more easily, so it is better for snowballs. Temperature and the snow’s history affect its texture.
revised: Powder is loose, dry snow, often found in colder conditions. Wet snow has more liquid water in it. It sticks together more easily, which helps when making snowballs. Temperature and past weather affect how the snow feels.
note: Explains snow texture through snowball behavior.

original: Tofu is made from soy milk and is usually softer. Tempeh is firmer and tastes nuttier. It is made from soybeans changed by helpful microbes, a process called fermentation.
revised: Both are commonly made from soy. Tofu is made from soy milk and is usually softer. Tempeh is firmer and often has a nutty taste. Helpful microbes change the soybeans during its production. That process is called fermentation.
note: Explains fermentation in short sentences.

original: Yes, you can try marinating tempeh in your favorite seasonings and grilling or pan-frying it. You can also crumble it into stir-fries or salads for added protein.
revised: Slice the tempeh and let it sit in a sauce or seasoning mix. This is called marinating. Then pan-fry or grill it, following its cooking instructions. You can also crumble cooked tempeh into a stir-fry or salad.
note: Explains marinating and makes cooked preparation explicit.

original: Reach for fruits, carrot sticks with hummus, or a handful of almonds. They're all nutritious and easy to grab on the go.
revised: Try fruit, carrots with hummus, or a small handful of almonds. Hummus is a spread usually made from chickpeas. Choose something that fits your needs and is easy to take with you.
note: Explains hummus and avoids universal snack suitability.

original: A second is a unit of time. There are 60 seconds in a minute. Scientists define it using a very steady pattern in caesium atoms, so clocks can measure it accurately.
revised: A second is a unit for measuring time. Sixty seconds make one minute. Scientists define it using a steady pattern in atoms of an element called caesium. That gives clocks a precise standard to follow.
note: Preserves the scientific definition and then gives the requested familiar explanation.

original: Watch a clock with a second hand: one small tick is usually one second. Sixty of those ticks make a minute. A blink is usually shorter than a full second.
revised: Look at a clock with a ticking second hand. One small tick is usually one second. Count sixty ticks and a minute has passed. A blink is usually quicker than one full second.
note: Preserves the scientific definition and then gives the requested familiar explanation.

original: Some do, but you may need to enable offline access and download files first. Check the app's instructions. Changes can then sync after you reconnect, if that feature is supported.
revised: Some apps work without internet access, but others do not. You may need to turn on offline access and download files first. Check the app's instructions. If supported, it can copy your changes to other devices when you reconnect.
note: Explains offline and sync behavior with conditions.

original: You can try searching online for local parks or recreation centers that offer pickup games. You can also check social media or sports apps to find groups of people playing in your area.
revised: Ask local parks or recreation centers about informal games. Search social media or local sports groups too. Check the time, place, and who can join before going.
note: Explains the informal-game search through concrete checks.

original: Imagine two lines across your photo and two from top to bottom, dividing it into nine equal boxes. Place the main subject along a line or where two lines meet. This is the rule of thirds. It can help a photo look balanced.
revised: Imagine a grid over your photo with nine equal boxes. Two lines go across, and two go from top to bottom. Put the main subject near a line or where two lines meet. This guide is called the rule of thirds. It can help balance a photo, but you do not have to follow it every time.
note: Explains the grid step by step and frames the rule as guidance.

original: Time lets us describe when events happen and how long they last. A clock measures time by counting a repeated process, such as the swings of a pendulum or changes in atoms. In physics, time is also linked to space and motion.
revised: Time helps us describe when things happen and how long they last. A clock measures time by counting something that repeats. A pendulum's swings are one example. Modern clocks can count regular changes in atoms. In physics, time is also linked to space and motion.
note: Explains clock measurement through repeated events.

original: Label containers and shelves so you can find things quickly. Wipe the shelves regularly to remove dust and keep them clean.
revised: Label containers and shelves so you can find things quickly. Wipe the shelves regularly to remove dust and keep them clean.
note: Already short actionable pantry guidance.

original: Camels have wide feet that help them walk on sand. Antarctic penguins have closely packed feathers that keep them warm. These features are adaptations. They are passed from parents to young and become common over many generations.
revised: Camels have wide feet that help them walk on sand. Antarctic penguins have tightly packed feathers that help keep them warm. These features are adaptations. They help living things survive in their surroundings. They are passed from parents to young over many generations.
note: Explains adaptation while preserving inheritance.

original: Yes. Plants release water from their leaves into the air. This helps move water through the water cycle and supports life.
revised: Yes. Transpiration is water leaving plant leaves and entering the air. This is one part of the water cycle. It helps move water through the environment.
note: Restates the term and explains its role clearly.

original: Congratulations on your upcoming graduation. The graduation cap and gown are traditional attire worn to signify academic achievement and unity among graduates. They also add a formal touch to the ceremony.
revised: The cap and gown are traditional clothes for graduation. They mark the completion of a stage of study. Wearing them together also shows that the graduates belong to the same group. They make the ceremony feel formal.
note: Explains attire and academic achievement in ordinary words.

original: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds and the spaces between them. It helps you feel when notes happen. Clapping the pattern of a song is one way to hear its rhythm.
revised: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds and the spaces between them. It helps you feel when notes happen. Clapping the pattern of a song is one way to hear its rhythm.
note: Already explains rhythm with a concrete clapping example.

original: Leaves can be oval, triangular, or heart-shaped. Maple leaves have pointed tips and several rounded or pointed sections called lobes.
revised: Leaves can be oval, triangular, or shaped like a heart. Maple leaves have sections that stick out from the main leaf. Those sections are called lobes. Their tips may be pointed or rounded.
note: Explains lobe through the visible shape.

original: That is called refraction. Light changes speed when it enters a different material, such as when it moves between air and water. It can also change direction, making it look as if it bends.
