revised: It is called refraction. Light changes speed when it moves between materials, such as air and water. It can also change direction. That change in direction looks like a bend.
note: Explains the apparent bend while retaining the optical cause.

original: Light from the part of the straw under water bends as it leaves the water and enters the air. Your eyes trace that light back in a straight line, so the underwater part appears shifted. That makes the straw look bent at the surface.
revised: Light from the underwater part of the straw changes direction as it enters the air. Your brain treats the light as if it followed a straight path. So the underwater part looks shifted to one side. The straw itself has not bent.
note: Explains the apparent bend while retaining the optical cause.

original: You're welcome! I'm glad that helped.
revised: You're welcome! I'm glad that helped.
note: Explains the apparent bend while retaining the optical cause.

original: There are several composition rules in photography, but some of the most important ones are the Rule of Thirds, Leading Lines, and Framing. The Rule of Thirds involves dividing your image into thirds both horizontally and vertically and placing your subject along those lines.
revised: Composition means choosing where things go in your photo. One guide is the rule of thirds. Imagine a grid of nine equal boxes and place your subject near a grid line. Leading lines guide the eye toward the subject, like a path through a scene. Framing uses something around the subject, such as a doorway.
note: Explains all three named composition ideas.

original: Large planned shopping centres spread during the 20th century. Southdale Center opened in Minnesota in 1956. It is known as the first fully enclosed US mall with controlled indoor heating and cooling.
revised: Large planned shopping centers became more common in the 1900s. Southdale Center opened in Minnesota in 1956. It is known as the first fully enclosed US mall with indoor heating and cooling.
note: Keeps historical specificity and avoids age-based assumptions about facilities.

original: The mix varies. Some newer malls emphasize dining and entertainment, while others focus on shops. Older malls can also have those features, so age alone does not tell you what to expect.
revised: There is no single difference that fits every mall. Some newer malls focus on food and entertainment. Others mainly offer shops. Older malls can have all of these features too.
note: Keeps historical specificity and avoids age-based assumptions about facilities.

original: You will probably find shops, places to eat, and perhaps entertainment. Check the mall's website or social media for events and offers before you go.
revised: You will probably find shops and places to eat. There may also be entertainment or special events. Check your mall's website before visiting to see what is available.
note: Keeps historical specificity and avoids age-based assumptions about facilities.

original: Some popular brands for car stereo systems include Pioneer, Kenwood, and JVC. They offer a wide range of features and price options.
revised: Pioneer, Kenwood, and JVC are examples of car-audio brands. Their models differ in features and price. Check that the unit fits your car.
note: Keeps the brand list clear and adds relevant fit context.

original: Not always exactly two. It needs at least two complete clauses, each with a subject and a verb, but there can be more. The same person can be the subject in both clauses: "I cooked, and I washed up."
revised: Not exactly. A compound sentence has at least two complete clauses. A clause is a part with a subject and a verb. There can be more than two. The subjects can name the same person: 'I cooked, and I washed up.'
note: Explains clause and keeps the correction to exactly two.

original: You may be able to use a public pool or a community-center pool without a gym membership. Check the entry fee, opening hours, and available sessions. A beginner class can help if you are not yet confident in the water.
revised: No, a gym membership may not be needed. You may be able to pay to use a public or community pool. Check entry prices, opening times, and available sessions. If you are not confident in water, a beginner class can help.
note: Answers the requirement question directly and preserves local availability.

original: A compatible smart thermostat can schedule temperatures and allow remote control; some can learn routines. Savings depend on your heating system, settings, and previous habits.
revised: A compatible smart thermostat can set temperatures on a schedule. It may also let you change them from your phone. Some learn your usual routine. Energy savings depend on your heating system, settings, and previous habits.
note: Explains controls and preserves compatibility and savings limits.

original: Use less water, choose energy from sources such as sunlight or wind, and protect forests and wetlands. These natural places help water move through the water cycle.
revised: Use water carefully and protect forests and wetlands. Wetlands are areas where the ground is covered or soaked with water. These places help store and move water. Choosing cleaner energy, such as wind or solar power, can also help protect the climate that affects the cycle.
note: Explains wetlands and connects the actions to water movement.

original: Yes, game-based learning can be adapted to different age groups and subjects. For example, younger students can use games to learn basic literacy skills, while older students can use games to learn complex historical concepts.
revised: Yes. Choose a game that fits the learners and the topic. Young children might practise reading words through a game. Older students might use a game to explore events in history. The game still needs clear learning goals.
note: Uses age-specific examples without unexplained literacy terms.

original: Mountains can have many different colors, but they're often shades of brown, gray, and green. These colors come from the rocks, soil, and plants that cover the mountains.
revised: Mountains do not have one fixed color. Rocks and soil can look brown or gray. Plants may make slopes look green. Light and weather can also change how those colors appear.
note: Explains the sources of visible mountain colors.

original: Van Gogh is known for Post-Impressionism, a style that emphasizes bold colors and emotional expression.
revised: Van Gogh is linked with Post-Impressionism. This was an art movement that developed after Impressionism. His paintings often use strong colors and clear brush marks to express feeling.
note: Explains the movement through time and visible features.

original: Yes, you can try looking at food blogs, social media, or cooking websites for ideas. You can also experiment with different cuisines, such as Korean or Indian, to add new flavors to your classic recipes.
revised: Browse a food blog, cooking website, or recipe video. Pick an ingredient you enjoy and look for a new way to cook it. You could also try a recipe from another cooking tradition, such as Korean or Indian food.
note: Turns inspiration into a specific search approach.

original: When choosing a yoga mat, consider the material, grip, thickness, and eco-friendliness. You may also want to think about your personal preferences, such as color and texture.
revised: Check that the mat grips the floor and does not let your hands slip. Think about how much padding feels comfortable. Also consider its weight, material, and how easy it is to clean. If environmental impact matters to you, look for clear material information rather than vague claims.
note: Explains grip and thickness through practical checks.

original: Based on what you said, the birth order in your family is: your older brother, you, and then your younger sister.
revised: Your older brother is first, you are second, and your younger sister is third. That makes you the middle child of the three.
note: Makes the birth order explicit.

original: Try scrambled eggs: beat eggs with a little salt, pour into a lightly greased pan over gentle heat, and stir slowly until set. Serve with toast or vegetables.
revised: Try scrambled eggs. Beat the eggs with a little salt. Pour them into a lightly greased pan over gentle heat. Stir slowly until the eggs are set. Serve with toast or vegetables.
note: Separates the recipe into short cooking steps.

original: German business communication is often described as fairly direct, but that is only a broad tendency. People within any country differ, and a work meeting may be very different from a family conversation. Treat the person's own words and preferences as your best guide.
revised: German business communication is often described as fairly direct. That means people may state their point plainly. But it is only a broad tendency. People differ, and a work meeting is not the same as a family talk. Follow the person's own words and preferences rather than a stereotype.
note: Explains direct speech and preserves within-country variation.

original: Use clear routines so students know what to do next, and keep needed materials easy to find. Reduce unnecessary visual or background noise where possible. Ask students what helps them focus; music or headphones help some people but distract others.
revised: Use clear routines so students know what comes next. Keep needed materials easy to find. Reduce unnecessary noise and busy displays where possible. Ask students what helps them focus. Music or headphones help some students but distract others.
note: Makes classroom changes clear and keeps learner differences.

original: Use a strong, unique password and keep your browser and device updated. Check that the store is real and that the address is correct. HTTPS protects the connection, but it does not prove that a seller is honest.
revised: Use a strong password that you do not use elsewhere. Keep your browser and device updated. Check the shop's web address and whether the business is real. HTTPS protects the connection to a website. It does not prove the seller is honest.
note: Separates connection protection from seller trust and keeps concrete precautions.

original: If you are unsure about a public network, mobile data can be a simpler choice. HTTPS still protects the connection on public Wi-Fi, but do not ignore browser security warnings or install anything a network asks for unexpectedly. A private network alone does not make a fraudulent shop safe.
revised: If you do not trust the public network, use mobile data instead. HTTPS can still protect a connection on public Wi-Fi. Do not ignore browser security warnings. Do not install unexpected software a network asks for. Even a private network cannot make a fake shop trustworthy.
note: Separates connection protection from seller trust and keeps concrete precautions.

original: A butterfly starts as an egg, hatches as a caterpillar, then becomes a chrysalis while its body changes. Finally, an adult butterfly emerges. These four stages often take weeks or months.
revised: A butterfly has four main life stages. First comes an egg. It hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar becomes a chrysalis, a stage when its body changes. An adult butterfly then comes out. The timing varies and may take weeks or months.
note: Explains chrysalis and avoids treating the two life cycles as identical stages.

original: A human's life cycle is birth, growth, adulthood, and old age. It's a longer process that can take many decades. But like butterflies, humans also go through different stages of development as they grow and age.
revised: Humans also grow through several stages, but our life cycle takes much longer. A simple list is birth, childhood, adulthood, and old age. Unlike a butterfly, a human does not have a caterpillar or chrysalis stage.
note: Explains chrysalis and avoids treating the two life cycles as identical stages.

original: Exactly! Both butterflies and humans go through different stages, but the length of time it takes to complete each stage is much longer for humans.
revised: Yes. Both have stages, but the stages are different in form as well as length. Human development usually takes much longer overall.
note: Explains chrysalis and avoids treating the two life cycles as identical stages.

original: You can find many online tutorials and videos on YouTube and painting websites. You can also visit your local library or art store for books and guidance.
revised: Look for beginner books about Impressionism at your library. Museum websites can explain paintings and their history. For practical painting lessons, try a clear tutorial video or ask an art shop about classes.
note: Separates learning art history from practising painting.

original: You can search online for "reading challenges" or visit your local library's website to see if they have any ongoing challenges. You can also check out websites like Goodreads, which offers different reading challenges throughout the year.
revised: Check your library's website or ask a librarian. Search online for reading challenges that match your interests. Goodreads is another place to look. Read the rules before joining so the goal feels manageable.
note: Makes challenge finding into clear steps.

original: When choosing running shoes, look for a comfortable fit, sufficient arch support, and cushioning. It's also important to consider the terrain you'll be running on and your personal running style.
revised: Look for shoes that feel comfortable while you move. Your heel should feel secure, with enough room for your toes. Padding and support should suit your feet. Also choose shoes made for the surface you will run on.
note: Explains fit and preserves the road-running condition without unnecessary brands.

original: Try several models made for road running. Look for a secure heel, enough room for your toes, and comfort while moving. The fit of the specific shoe matters more than the brand.
revised: Try several models made for road running. Check that your heel stays secure and your toes have room. Walk or jog a little in them if possible. The fit of the specific shoe matters more than its brand.
note: Explains fit and preserves the road-running condition without unnecessary brands.

original: Yes, there are several techniques that can help. Deep breathing exercises, meditation, and yoga are popular methods for reducing stress. Would you like to know more about any of these?
revised: You could try slow breathing, a quiet walk, or gentle yoga. Another option is sitting quietly and noticing your breathing. Different things help different people. Which would you like to try?
note: Explains relaxation choices and preserves the professional-therapy distinction.

original: Listening to music you find calming may help you relax. Music therapy is different: it involves working with a trained therapist toward specific goals. A relaxation playlist is not the same as professional music therapy.
revised: Music you find calming may help you relax. Music therapy is more specific. It means working with a trained therapist toward particular goals. Listening to a relaxing playlist is not the same service.
note: Explains relaxation choices and preserves the professional-therapy distinction.

original: You can enjoy looking at products and displays without needing to buy. It can also give you ideas for later.
revised: You can enjoy looking at products and displays without needing to buy. It can also give you ideas for later.
note: Keeps casual shopping language and conditional photo permission.

original: Handle products carefully and avoid touching them more than needed. Keep entrances and aisles clear. Be respectful to staff and other shoppers.
revised: Handle products carefully and keep aisles and entrances clear. Be polite to staff and other shoppers. You do not need to buy something simply because you looked.
note: Keeps casual shopping language and conditional photo permission.

original: Ask staff whether photos are allowed, especially if you want to share them online. Many shops allow photos for personal use.
revised: Ask the staff first. Some shops allow photos for personal use, while others have restrictions. Also ask before sharing a photo online if the rules are unclear.
note: Keeps casual shopping language and conditional photo permission.

original: Check the serving size first, then compare similar foods. Look at fibre and nutrients such as calcium. Compare added sugar, salt or sodium, and saturated fat too. The food with the fewest calories is not always the best choice.
revised:
Check the serving size first. It tells you how much food the numbers describe. Compare similar foods using the same amount.

Look for fiber, which helps food move through your gut. Calcium helps keep bones strong. Also compare added sugar, salt, and saturated fat. Added sugar means sugar put into the food during making or cooking. Saturated fat is common in foods such as butter. Health guides advise eating less of it. They also advise limiting added sugar and salt. US labels list sodium, a part of salt.

Calories measure how much energy food gives you. Fewer calories do not always mean a better choice.
note: Cross-review: replaces the circular saturated-fat definition with a familiar example and actionable guidance. Explains serving size, fiber, sodium and calories; preserves calcium and the warning against judging food only by calories. Verified against FDA label guidance and NHS fat guidance.

original: On US labels, percent Daily Value compares one serving with a standard daily amount. If vitamin C says 10%, a serving provides one tenth of that amount. It is a general guide, not your exact personal need.
revised: On US labels, percent Daily Value compares one serving with a standard daily amount. For example, 10 percent for vitamin C means one tenth of that amount. The figure is a general guide. It is not your exact personal need.
note: Explains serving comparisons and preserves the US label and personal-need limits.

original: You're welcome. Ask if any part of a label is unclear.
revised: You're welcome. Ask if any part of a label is unclear.
note: Explains serving comparisons and preserves the US label and personal-need limits.

original: Some popular cooking shows include MasterChef, Hell's Kitchen, and Chopped. They're all fun to watch and offer great recipe ideas.
revised: MasterChef, Hell's Kitchen, and Chopped are well-known examples. They mix cooking with competition. Watch an episode to see which format you enjoy.
note: Avoids claiming personal viewing preferences or guaranteed enjoyment.

original: Yes, definitely check out Anthony Bourdain's Parts Unknown and Gordon Ramsay's Uncharted. They're both great shows that combine travel and food.
revised: Anthony Bourdain's Parts Unknown and Gordon Ramsay's Uncharted combine travel with food. Both explore places through local dishes and the people who make them.
note: Avoids claiming personal viewing preferences or guaranteed enjoyment.

original: Many people enjoy watching chefs like Jamie Oliver and Giada De Laurentiis. They're both great at sharing recipes and cooking tips in a friendly and approachable way.
revised: I do not have personal favorites. Jamie Oliver and Giada De Laurentiis are examples of cooks to explore. Their shows and recipes may give you ideas for home cooking.
note: Avoids claiming personal viewing preferences or guaranteed enjoyment.

original: Watch the heat and move the food often enough for even cooking. If it starts browning too quickly, lower the heat. Do not overcrowd the pan, and do not assume extra oil will fix a pan that is too hot.
revised: Watch the heat and move the food so it cooks evenly. Lower the heat if the food browns too quickly. Leave enough room in the pan. Adding more oil will not fix every problem caused by too much heat.
note: Separates sauteing controls and preserves the oil caveat.

original: Some of Elvis' most popular songs include "Hound Dog," "Jailhouse Rock," "Love Me Tender," and "Heartbreak Hotel."
revised: Some of Elvis' most popular songs include "Hound Dog," "Jailhouse Rock," "Love Me Tender," and "Heartbreak Hotel."
note: Already a clear short list of named songs.

original: Ask a gym staff member to show you the treadmill’s controls and emergency stop. Follow that machine’s instructions, begin at a slow walking speed, and increase it only when you feel steady. Do not step onto a fast-moving belt.
revised: Ask gym staff to show you the controls and emergency stop. Follow the instructions for that machine. Start at a slow walking speed. Increase it only when you feel steady. Never step onto a fast-moving belt.
note: Explains form and preserves the machine and symptom precautions.

original: When lifting weights, start with lighter weights and gradually increase the load as you become stronger. It's also a good idea to ask a gym staff member for guidance or work with a personal trainer.
revised: Ask a trainer to show you the movement before lifting. Start with a light weight you can control. Increase it gradually when you can keep good form. Good form means moving in the safe, intended way for that exercise.
note: Explains form and preserves the machine and symptom precautions.

original: Start gently, learn the movements, and take breaks when you need them. Stop if you feel pain, faintness, or unusual discomfort. A qualified instructor can help you choose a routine that fits your experience.
revised: Start gently and take breaks when needed. Stop if you feel pain, faint, or unusually uncomfortable. A qualified instructor can help choose a routine for your level.
note: Explains form and preserves the machine and symptom precautions.

original: Keep unopened canned food in its original cans and group them in shallow bins or on shelves. Put older cans at the front so you use them first. You do not need to transfer unopened canned food into airtight containers.
revised: Keep unopened food in its original cans. Put the cans on shelves or in shallow bins. Place older cans at the front so you use them first. There is no need to open them and move the food into other containers.
note: Makes the storage sequence clear and retains the unopened-can distinction.

original: There are many varieties, but some popular types include Espresso, Cappuccino, Latte, and Mocha.
revised: Espresso is a small, strong coffee. A latte combines espresso with milk. A cappuccino also has milk and a layer of milk foam. A mocha usually adds chocolate.
note: Explains the drink names rather than only listing them.

original: A map shows an area on a flat surface, such as paper or a screen. A globe is a round model of Earth that shows its shape and features.
revised: A map shows an area on a flat surface, such as paper or a screen. A globe is a round model of Earth that shows its shape and features.
note: Already explains the map/globe distinction with familiar words.

original: Fela Kuti and drummer Tony Allen are important figures to start with. Listen to how the drums, bass, and horns build a repeating groove together.
revised: Start with Fela Kuti and drummer Tony Allen. They are important figures in Afrobeat. Listen to how the drums, bass, and horns repeat patterns together. Those patterns help create the music's steady movement.
note: Explains groove through repeated musical parts.

original: Let the potting mix dry appropriately for the species, then water thoroughly and let excess drain away. Frequency depends on light, temperature, pot size, and season. Avoid following a fixed weekly rule.
revised: Let the soil dry as much as your particular plant needs. Then water well and let extra water drain out. The timing depends on light, heat, pot size, and season. Do not assume every succulent needs water once a week.
note: Explains watering clearly and preserves species-specific timing.

original: No, they're not the same. The Winter Olympics feature sports like ice skating, skiing, and ice hockey, while the Summer Olympics feature sports like swimming, track and field, and gymnastics.
revised: No. The Winter Olympics focus on snow and ice sports. Examples include skiing, ice skating, and ice hockey. The Summer Olympics include sports such as swimming, athletics, and gymnastics. They are separate events.
note: Explains the seasonal sports distinction.

original: People often grow tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots, lettuce, and herbs. Which are easy depends on the season, sunlight, and soil where you garden.
revised: People often grow tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots, lettuce, and herbs. What grows easily depends on your sunlight, soil, and season.
note: Preserves variety-dependent ripeness and gentle handling.

original: Look for the ripe color expected for your variety, which may be red, yellow, orange, or another color. A ripe tomato often has a slight give. Remove it gently rather than pulling hard on the plant.
revised: Check which color your tomato variety has when ripe. It may be red, yellow, orange, or another color. A ripe tomato often gives slightly when gently pressed. Pick it carefully rather than pulling hard on the plant.
note: Preserves variety-dependent ripeness and gentle handling.

original: Snake plants are pretty versatile, so you can use different pots. Just make sure it has good drainage holes to prevent waterlogged soil. A simple ceramic or terracotta pot would work well.
revised: Choose a pot with holes that let extra water drain out. This helps keep the soil from staying too wet. Ceramic or terracotta pots can work. Terracotta is a porous clay material.
note: Explains drainage and the pot material.

original: These are useful things nature does for us. Examples include providing food, helping keep air and water clean, and reducing flood damage.
revised: Ecosystem services are useful things nature does for people. Nature provides food and helps clean air and water. Wetlands and other natural areas can also reduce flood damage.
note: Explains the term through concrete benefits.

original: Limestone is one example. It often forms as old shells and remains of sea life build up and are pressed together. Much of this material is calcium carbonate, the substance found in many shells.
revised: Limestone is one example. It often forms from shells and remains of sea life. These build up and are pressed together over time. Much of limestone is calcium carbonate, the same material found in many shells.
note: Breaks rock formation into clear stages.

original: A giraffe's long neck lets it reach leaves high in trees. It can eat food that shorter animals cannot reach.
revised: A giraffe's long neck lets it reach leaves high in trees. It can eat food that shorter animals cannot reach.
note: Already clear adaptation example with a concrete advantage.

original: Yes, the Roman numeral for 1000 is M.
revised: Yes, the Roman numeral for 1000 is M.
note: Already answers the numeral question directly.

original: You can start by practicing self-awareness, such as recognizing how you feel and why. You can also try active listening, which means paying attention to others and understanding their feelings.
revised: Notice what you feel and what may have caused it. This is part of self-awareness. When someone else speaks, listen without interrupting. Ask questions instead of guessing how they feel. These habits can help you understand emotions better.
note: Explains self-awareness and listening through actions.

original: A synthesizer is an electronic instrument that creates sound electronically, often used in music production and live performances.
revised: A synthesizer is an instrument that makes sound using electronics. It can create many different tones. Musicians use it when recording music and playing live.
note: Explains the instrument without repeating electronically twice.

original: No. Gravity depends on mass and distance. It is weaker on the Moon than on Earth. Even on Earth it changes slightly from place to place, and it gets weaker as you move farther away.
revised: No. Gravity depends on how much mass objects have and how far apart they are. Mass means the amount of matter in an object. The Moon's pull is weaker than Earth's. Even Earth's gravity changes slightly from place to place. It also weakens as you move farther away.
note: Explains mass and preserves location and distance effects.

original: Yes, I can suggest a few. Deep breathing exercises, progressive muscle relaxation, and meditation are all great ways to reduce stress and promote relaxation. Would you like to know more about any of these?
revised: You could try a few slow breaths or sit quietly for a short time. Another option is gently tightening and relaxing muscles in turn. This is called progressive muscle relaxation. These methods help some people feel calmer. Which would you like explained?
note: Explains rather than lists the unfamiliar relaxation term.

original: There are mainly three types of cutting boards: wood, plastic, and bamboo. Each has its own advantages and disadvantages.
revised: Common cutting-board materials include wood, plastic, and bamboo. They differ in how they feel and how you care for them. Check the cleaning instructions for the board you choose.
note: Avoids claiming only three types exist.

original: Common causes include exhaust from vehicles, pollution from factories, and burning fuels such as coal and oil.
revised: Vehicle exhaust, factory pollution, and burning fuels are common causes. Exhaust is the gas released by an engine. Burning coal and oil can add harmful gases and particles to the air.
note: Explains exhaust and connects burning to air pollution.

original: Kinetic energy is the energy of movement. Potential energy is stored because of position or arrangement, such as in a raised object. Thermal energy is linked to the random movement of tiny particles in a material. Electrical energy and energy stored in chemicals are other types.
revised: Kinetic energy is the energy of movement, such as a rolling ball. Potential energy is stored because of position or arrangement. A raised weight is one example. Thermal energy comes from the movement of tiny particles in a material. Electricity and energy stored in chemicals are other examples.
note: Pairs the energy terms with simple meanings and examples.

original: Spaced repetition means reviewing something several times, with breaks between reviews. You might review a new word tomorrow, then a few days later, then again after a longer gap.
revised: Spaced repetition means practising the same material again after breaks. For a new word, try recalling its meaning the next day. Review it again a few days later. Leave longer gaps as you remember it more easily. Those times are examples, not a fixed rule.
note: Explains the learning method without copying the style-guide example.

original: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest bone. It runs from the hip to the knee.
revised: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest bone. It runs from the hip to the knee.
note: Already explains femur with the familiar name and location.

original: Some popular pet toys include squeaky chew toys, plush toys, and interactive puzzle toys. They're great for keeping your dog entertained and stimulated.
revised: Try a chew toy, soft toy, or puzzle toy suited to your dog. A puzzle toy gives the dog a task, such as finding a treat. Choose toys that match its size and chewing habits.
note: Explains puzzle and clicker roles while retaining supervision.

original: Treat toys can make practice more interesting. A clicker is a training tool, not a toy: its sound marks a behavior before a reward. Choose equipment that suits your dog and supervise play.
revised: Treat toys can make practice interesting. A clicker is a training tool rather than a toy. You click when the dog does the wanted action, then give a reward. Choose suitable equipment and watch your dog during play.
note: Explains puzzle and clicker roles while retaining supervision.

original: Some benefits include access to industry events, training and development opportunities, and networking with potential employers or business partners.
revised: A professional association is a group for people in the same field. It may offer events, courses, and chances to meet others. You could meet future employers or people to work with. Benefits differ between groups.
note: Explains association and conditional benefits.

original: Divide the top number by the bottom number, then multiply by 100. For 1/2, calculate 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5. Then 0.5 × 100 = 50, so the answer is 50%.
revised: Divide the top number by the bottom number, then multiply by 100. For 1/2, calculate 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5. Then 0.5 × 100 = 50, so the answer is 50%.
note: Already a clear worked percentage example.

original: Cycling can give you exercise and reduce the pollution caused by car trips.
revised: It can be a good option if the route and distance suit you. Cycling gives you exercise and avoids pollution from that car trip. Think about a safe route and where you can leave the bike.
note: Preserves possible benefits and adds practical suitability conditions.

original: I'm just a language model, I don't have personal preferences, but many people enjoy the holiday displays during winter, especially Christmas and New Year's.
revised: I do not have a personal favorite. Winter holiday displays are something many people enjoy. Christmas and New Year displays often give shops a different look.
note: Keeps the preference limit without unnecessary model jargon.

original: One common system groups foods into fruits, vegetables, grains, protein foods, and dairy or suitable alternatives. Food guides vary between countries. Whole grains, such as oats and brown rice, are one kind of grain food.
revised: One common guide has five groups: fruit, vegetables, grains, protein foods, and dairy or suitable alternatives. Grain foods include bread, oats, and rice. Protein foods include beans, eggs, fish, and meat. Food guides differ between countries.
note: Explains group names with familiar foods and keeps country variation.

original: Yes, planning your meals in advance can help you avoid buying unnecessary items and reduce food waste. Consider making a weekly meal plan and sticking to it.
revised: Plan meals before you shop. Check which ingredients you already have. Make a list for the meals and buy what you need. This can reduce extra purchases and wasted food.
note: Makes budgeting advice actionable.

original: One tip is to start by brainstorming your ideas and then create an outline. This can help you organize your thoughts and write more clearly.
revised: Write down your ideas before worrying about perfect sentences. Then put related ideas together. Choose an order for them. This short plan is an outline. Use it to write one section at a time.
note: Explains brainstorming and outline through actions.

original: Salt water is an example. When salt dissolves fully, it spreads evenly through the water. Sugar dissolved in water to make a simple syrup is another example.
revised: Salt water is an example of a solution. When salt dissolves fully, it spreads evenly through the water. Dissolved sugar does the same. Water with dissolved sugar can be used to make a simple syrup.
note: Explains solution and dissolved material using supplied examples.

original: Animals do not understand human language the way we do. But some, such as dogs and horses, can learn to respond to certain words or commands. This is different from understanding the full language.
revised: Some animals, such as dogs and horses, can learn to respond to certain words. They may also respond to commands. That is different from understanding a whole human language as people do.
note: Keeps the recognition-versus-language distinction.

original: The backswing puts your body and club in position for the swing toward the ball. A controlled turn can help you create speed and make repeatable contact.
revised: The backswing moves your club and body into position before you swing at the ball. A controlled turn helps prepare the forward swing. It can help you make contact more consistently.
note: Explains the swing phase without promising speed from any backswing.

original: In one kind of supernova, a very massive star's centre collapses because it can no longer support itself. Much of the outer star is thrown into space. The centre may become a neutron star, a very small, dense star, or a black hole. Other kinds of supernova happen differently.
revised: In one type of supernova, a very massive star's center collapses. It can no longer hold itself up. Much of the outer star is thrown into space. The center may become a neutron star, which packs a lot of matter into a tiny space. It may instead become a black hole. Other types of supernova happen differently.
note: Explains the collapse and neutron star while preserving the type-specific account.

original: Yes, I can suggest a few exercises. You can start with burpees, mountain climbers, push-ups, squats, and lunges. These exercises work multiple muscle groups and can be done with minimal equipment.
revised: You could combine easier push-ups, squats, and lunges. These use several parts of your body. Burpees and mountain climbers are harder options. Learn each movement and choose versions that suit your fitness. Most basic versions need little or no equipment.
note: Explains reps and sets and changes the schedule into a conditional example.

original: Begin with a small number of controlled repetitions and use easier versions if needed. Rest when your form starts to slip. Build up gradually instead of forcing a fixed target for every exercise.
revised: A rep means doing a movement once. A set is a group of reps. Start with a small number you can do with control. Rest when you can no longer keep the movement steady. Build up gradually instead of forcing the same target for every exercise.
note: Explains reps and sets and changes the schedule into a conditional example.

original: It's recommended to take rest days in between. Doing this routine 2-3 times a week, with at least one day of rest in between, will allow your muscles to recover and rebuild. This will help you see better results and prevent burnout.
revised: Leave rest days between hard sessions so your muscles can recover. Two or three sessions a week is one possible starting pattern. Adjust the routine to your fitness and how you recover. You do not need a hard full-body workout every day.
note: Explains reps and sets and changes the schedule into a conditional example.

original: Humans eat plants and animals, so we are omnivores. People can be top predators when hunting. But that does not describe every human diet or food web. Our place depends on what we eat and the living things around us.
revised: Humans are omnivores, which means we eat both plants and animals. People can act as top predators when they hunt. But not every human diet puts us at the top of a food web. Our place depends on what we eat and the living things around us.
note: Explains omnivore and keeps food-web dependence.

original: Android and iOS are two different operating systems. Android is used by many phone manufacturers like Samsung and Google, while iOS is exclusive to Apple devices like iPhones. They have different interfaces and features.
revised: Android and iOS are operating systems, the main software that runs a phone. Many brands, including Samsung and Google, use Android. iPhones use Apple's iOS. Their menus, features, and available apps differ.
note: Explains operating system and preserves the need for current regional evidence.

original: Android is used on phones from many brands, while iOS is used on iPhones. Which is more popular depends on the place and time. For a current comparison, look at recent figures for the country you care about.
revised: It depends on the country and when you measure it. Android is used by many phone brands, while iOS is used on iPhones. For a current answer, check recent figures for the place you mean.
note: Explains operating system and preserves the need for current regional evidence.

original: Basic bike maintenance includes checking tire pressure, lubricating the chain, and cleaning the brakes.
revised: Basic care includes checking tire pressure and keeping the bike clean. The chain needs suitable oil, and the brakes need regular checks. Follow the bike maker's care instructions.
note: Keeps brake cleaning tied to the actual system and avoids assumed purchase.

original: The right method depends on whether you have rim brakes or disc brakes. Follow the brake maker’s cleaning instructions and keep chain oil away from braking surfaces. If braking is weak or you are unsure what to use, ask a bike mechanic.
revised: First check whether your bike has rim brakes or disc brakes. Follow the brake maker's cleaning instructions. Keep chain oil off the surfaces that do the braking. If the brakes feel weak or you are unsure, ask a bike mechanic.
note: Keeps brake cleaning tied to the actual system and avoids assumed purchase.

original: You're welcome! Enjoy your new bike and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any more questions.
revised: You're welcome. I hope you enjoy cycling.
note: Keeps brake cleaning tied to the actual system and avoids assumed purchase.

original: Circuit training means doing several exercises one after another, with little rest between them. It uses energy and can train your heart and lungs.
revised: Circuit training means doing a series of exercises one after another. You usually take only short breaks between them. Then you may repeat the series. It can challenge your heart, lungs, and muscles, depending on the exercises.
note: Explains the sequence and repetition clearly.

original: You can search online for "co-working spaces near me" or check websites like WeWork, Regus, or local listings in your area. Many cities also have co-working space directories or maps that can help you find one that suits your needs.
revised: Search for co-working spaces in your town. These are offices shared by people from different businesses. Local listings or providers such as WeWork and Regus may help. Compare location, cost, and the kind of space you need.
note: Explains co-working and gives relevant search criteria.

original: Shelters may have mixed-breed dogs, dogs of specific breeds, and cats with varied backgrounds. Availability differs by shelter. Focus on an animal’s needs and fit with your home rather than popularity alone.
revised: Availability changes between shelters. You may find mixed-breed dogs, dogs of particular breeds, and cats with different backgrounds. Ask local shelters what animals need homes. Focus on whether you can meet an animal's needs rather than its popularity.
note: Keeps adoption availability uncertain and care-based.

original: Try writing down many ideas or drawing a map that connects them. Take breaks to rest too. Books, workshops, and online lessons can give you ideas from other people.
revised: Write down several possible ways to solve one problem. You could draw lines between related ideas. Take a break and return with fresh attention. Books, classes, and other people's work may give you new ideas too.
note: Explains brainstorming steps and keeps the timer illustrative.

original: Set a timer for 10–15 minutes and write as many ideas as you can about one topic. You can also write without stopping, checking spelling, or fixing grammar. This is called freewriting.
revised: Choose one topic and set a short timer, perhaps for 10 to 15 minutes. Write down ideas without judging them yet. You can also keep writing without stopping to fix spelling. This is called freewriting.
note: Explains brainstorming steps and keeps the timer illustrative.

original: Group similar ideas, then ask three questions: Can I do this? Would it help? Does it fit my goal? Pick one promising idea and try a small version first.
revised: Put similar ideas together. For each group, ask: Can I do it? Would it help? Does it fit my goal? Choose one promising idea and try a small version first.
note: Explains brainstorming steps and keeps the timer illustrative.

original: Smart lighting options are also available, such as Wi-Fi enabled lamps or smart bulbs that can be controlled through your smartphone or voice assistant.
revised: Smart bulbs and lamps can connect to your phone or a voice assistant. You may be able to switch them on, dim them, or set a schedule. Available controls depend on the light and system.
note: Explains smart-light actions and preserves device differences.

original: Burning fuel is one example, called combustion. In a car engine, gasoline reacts with oxygen and releases heat. The engine uses that energy to move the car. The reaction also produces carbon dioxide and water vapour, which is water in gas form.
revised: Burning fuel is a chemical reaction called combustion. In a car engine, gasoline reacts with oxygen and releases heat. The engine uses that energy to move the car. The reaction also makes carbon dioxide and water vapor. Water vapor is water in gas form.
note: Explains combustion and water vapor through the engine example.

original: You can cover part of the journey while sleeping. This may save daytime travel and a night in a hotel, but compare the train fare and sleeping options before deciding.
revised: You can travel while you sleep. This may save daytime hours and replace a night in a hotel. Compare the train price and sleeping space before choosing. Not every overnight train offers the same comfort.
note: Keeps benefits conditional and sleeping options relevant.

original: Web pages commonly use HTML for structure, CSS for appearance, and JavaScript for interactive behavior. HTML and CSS are not programming languages in the same sense as JavaScript. Servers behind web apps may use languages such as Python, JavaScript, or Java.
revised: Web apps often use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in the browser. HTML describes page parts, while CSS controls how they look. JavaScript adds actions, such as reacting to a click. HTML and CSS are not programming languages in the same sense. Work on the server may use Python, JavaScript, or Java.
note: Explains each web technology through its purpose.

original: Yes, there are several popular running communities. Some well-known ones include Nike Run Club, Running Room, and local running groups on Meetup.com.
revised: Nike Run Club, Running Room, and local Meetup groups are examples to explore. Check what is available near you and whether the group welcomes beginners.
note: Explains community benefits without accountability jargon.

original: Joining a running community can provide motivation, accountability, and support from fellow runners. It's also a great way to meet new people and learn new running tips and techniques.
revised: Running with others can help you keep a routine. You can share tips and encourage one another. It is also a way to meet people. Choose a group whose pace and atmosphere suit you.
note: Explains community benefits without accountability jargon.

original: You can search for local running groups on Meetup.com or Facebook Groups. You can also check with local running stores or gyms in your area to see if they host or know of any running groups.
revised: Search Meetup or local Facebook groups. Ask a running shop or gym whether it knows a beginner group. Before joining, check the usual distance and pace.
note: Explains community benefits without accountability jargon.

original: Thousands of languages are used around the world. Counts vary because researchers may classify language varieties differently and include different kinds of languages.
revised: There are thousands of languages around the world. The exact count depends on how researchers group them. For example, they may disagree about whether two varieties are separate languages or dialects.
note: Explains why counts differ without inventing a precise total.

original: A bistro is usually a small, casual restaurant that serves simple, classic dishes, often with a cozy atmosphere. A restaurant can be any size and serve a wide variety of cuisines.
revised: A bistro is one type of restaurant. It is usually small and relaxed, with fairly simple dishes. Restaurant is the broader word. Restaurants can be large or small and serve many kinds of food.
note: Explains the category relationship.

original: The main cause of global warming is the increasing levels of greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide and methane, in the Earth's atmosphere. These gases trap heat from the sun, leading to a rise in global temperatures.
revised: The main cause is the rise in heat-trapping gases from human activities. Carbon dioxide and methane are examples. These gases slow the escape of heat from Earth into space. That raises the planet's average temperature.
note: Factual repair: greenhouse gases reduce outgoing heat loss from Earth; they do not simply trap incoming sunlight. NASA explanation checked.

original: Wearable devices can be used to share a worker's location or measure conditions around them. Some systems are designed to warn about hazards. The features and limits depend on the device.
revised: Yes. Some wearable devices show where a worker is on a site. Others measure nearby conditions and may warn about danger. A wearable device is something worn on the body. Its abilities and limits depend on the product.
note: Explains wearable technology and keeps hazard warnings conditional.

original: You can search for job sharing opportunities on job boards, company websites, or professional networks like LinkedIn. You can also talk to your HR department or manager to see if job sharing is an option in your current role.
revised: Search job websites and company career pages for job sharing. LinkedIn may also have listings or contacts. If you want to share your current role, ask your manager or human-resources team whether it is possible.
note: Expands HR and gives distinct new-job/current-role routes.

original: Squats, lunges, and leg press can help improve your leg strength, while exercises like push-ups and planks can improve your core and upper body strength. It's also essential to include exercises that target your agility and flexibility, such as shuttle runs and leg swings.
revised: Squats, lunges, and leg presses can help build leg strength. Push-ups work the upper body. Planks help train the muscles around your middle. Quick shuttle runs practise changes of direction. Learn the movements and choose a workload suited to your level.
note: Separates strength from direction-changing work and explains core.

original: Some popular types of custards include crème brûlée, flan, and crema catalana. They're all delicious and rich desserts.
revised: Crème brûlée, flan, and crema catalana are examples. Custards are mixtures that become thick and smooth when prepared. These desserts differ in their flavor, texture, and topping.
note: Explains the dessert category without empty taste praise.

original: Cleopatra VII ruled Egypt from 51 BC until her death in 30 BC. She was a ruler of the Ptolemaic dynasty and formed important political ties with the Roman leaders Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.
revised: Cleopatra VII ruled Egypt from 51 BC to 30 BC. She belonged to the Ptolemaic dynasty, a family of rulers. She formed important political ties with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony. Both were powerful Roman leaders.
note: Explains dynasty and separates dates from political relationships.

original: Negative numbers are numbers that are less than zero. They have a minus sign (-) in front of them, like -1, -2, or -3.
revised: Negative numbers are less than zero. They have a minus sign, such as -1, -2, and -3. A temperature of -2 degrees is two degrees below zero.
note: Adds a familiar negative-temperature example.

original: Possible developments include longer battery life, better sensors, and displays that add information to what you see. These are areas of development, not promises that every future device will include them.
revised: Future devices may have batteries that last longer or better measuring sensors. Some may show extra information in your view. These are areas people are developing. They are not promises about every future product.
note: Explains possible development without treating predictions as facts.

original: Yes, setting clear boundaries between work and personal time is key. Try allocating specific hours for work and sticking to them, and schedule time for exercise and relaxation.
revised: Decide when you can finish work and protect some time outside those hours. Plan small spaces for exercise and rest. Choose a routine that fits your actual responsibilities. Clear limits can help, even if the plan is not perfect every day.
note: Makes work-life advice practical without assuming total schedule control.

original: Try short walks or gentle movement breaks that fit between tasks. Pick something you enjoy and start with an amount that feels manageable. A small, regular activity is easier to fit into a busy day than an ambitious plan you cannot keep.
revised: Try a short walk or gentle movement between tasks. Choose something you enjoy and can manage. Small, regular activity may fit your day better than a large plan you cannot keep.
note: Makes work-life advice practical without assuming total schedule control.

original: Sort tasks by two things: importance and urgency. Do urgent, important work first, then make time for important work before it becomes urgent. Delegate or reduce low-value tasks when possible.
revised: Ask two questions: How important is this task? How soon does it need doing? Start with work that is both important and urgent. Then plan time for important work before its deadline gets close. Ask for help with or reduce less useful tasks when possible.
note: Explains urgency and priority through direct questions.

original: If you like Tarantino, you might enjoy the work of directors like Martin Scorsese, known for Goodfellas, or Guy Ritchie, known for Snatch and Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels.
revised: You might enjoy Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas or Guy Ritchie's Snatch. Ritchie also directed Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels. These are possible next choices if you liked Pulp Fiction.
note: Keeps film suggestions direct without claiming identical styles.

original: PEMDAS helps you remember the order of a calculation: Parentheses, Exponents, Multiplication and Division, then Addition and Subtraction. Parentheses are brackets like ( ). Exponents are powers, such as the 2 in 3².
revised: PEMDAS stands for Parentheses, Exponents, Multiplication, Division, Addition, and Subtraction. It helps you order the steps in a calculation. Parentheses are brackets like ( ). Exponents are powers, such as the 2 in 3². Multiplication and division share a level, as do addition and subtraction.
note: Explains equal priority and gives a worked same-level example.

original: Start inside parentheses, then work out powers. Next, do multiplication and division from left to right. They have equal priority. Finally, do addition and subtraction from left to right; those also have equal priority.
revised: First work inside parentheses, then calculate powers. Next do multiplication and division from left to right. Neither automatically comes before the other. Finally do addition and subtraction from left to right. These two also share the same level.
note: Explains equal priority and gives a worked same-level example.

original: Work from left to right. Do the leftmost calculation of that priority first, then the next.
revised: Work from left to right among operations at that same level. For example, calculate 2 × 3 × 4 as 6 × 4. The result is 24.
note: Explains equal priority and gives a worked same-level example.

original: One strategy is to make a shopping list before you go to the store and stick to it. This can help you avoid impulse buys.
revised: Make a list before shopping. Check it before adding something to your basket. This can help you avoid buying things only because they caught your eye.
note: Explains impulse buying and unit price with useful conditions.

original: Plan which aisles contain the items on your list and avoid browsing areas you do not need. The middle aisles can still contain useful foods such as beans, oats, or rice. Focus on what you need rather than a rule about the edge of the store.
revised: Go to the aisles that contain items on your list. Skip browsing areas you do not need. Useful foods such as beans, oats, and rice may be in the middle aisles. There is no need to avoid them just because of their location.
note: Explains impulse buying and unit price with useful conditions.

original: Plan meals around ingredients you already have and compare the price per unit. Buying a larger pack helps only if it costs less per unit and you will use or store it before it spoils. A small pack can be the better choice when it prevents waste.
revised: Plan meals using food you already have. Compare unit prices, such as the price per kilogram. A larger pack saves money only if it is cheaper per unit and you can use it. A smaller pack may avoid waste.
note: Explains impulse buying and unit price with useful conditions.

original: Monopoly is one classic option, especially for a family that enjoys buying, trading, and longer games. The best choice depends on the players’ ages and how long they want to play.
revised: Monopoly is a classic option for families who enjoy buying and trading. It can take a while to play. The best game depends on everyone's age, interests, and available time.
note: Keeps suitability dependent on players and edition.

original: The standard version is generally aimed at older children, so check the age label on the edition. For younger children, a simple matching or racing game may be easier.
revised: Check the age label on your edition. Standard Monopoly is generally aimed at older children. A simple matching or racing game may be easier for younger players.
note: Keeps suitability dependent on players and edition.

original: Follow a tested recipe for your cooker, cut of meat, and roast size. Pot roast is usually cooked slowly with liquid until tender. Temperature alone does not tell you when tough connective tissue has softened.
revised: Use a tested recipe for your cooker and the size of the roast. Pot roast usually cooks slowly with liquid until tender. The meat can reach a temperature before its tough parts soften. So temperature alone does not tell you whether it is ready to eat as a tender roast.
note: Explains connective tissue as tough parts and preserves recipe-specific guidance.

original: Yes, some popular options include "Toy Story," "The Jungle Book," and "Frozen." They're all fun and kid-friendly.
revised: Toy Story, The Jungle Book, and Frozen are possible choices. Check the age rating and which version you plan to watch. What suits your children depends on their ages and what they find upsetting.
note: Avoids the blanket all-kid-friendly claim.

original: That sounds like fun! There are many ways to decorate a cake, but a simple way to start is by using frosting and adding some colorful sprinkles or candies on top.
revised: Start with a simple layer of frosting. Smooth it over the cooled cake. Then add sprinkles or a few candies. You can arrange them into your sister's initial or a simple pattern.
note: Gives specific decorating steps and an optional personal detail.

original: A router is a device that connects multiple computers and devices to the internet and manages the flow of data between them.
revised: A router directs data between networks. At home, it helps your devices share an internet connection. It sends information toward the device or network that needs it. Many home routers also provide Wi-Fi.
note: Explains routing rather than equating all routers with internet modems.

original: Yes. Look at shoe shops' websites or social media pages to see their collections without going to the mall.
revised: Yes. Look at shoe shops' websites or social media pages to see their collections without going to the mall.
note: Keeps online browsing clear and save-feature availability conditional.

original: You can start with popular e-commerce websites like Amazon, Zappos, or the official websites of your favorite shoe brands. There are also apps like Pinterest or Instagram where you can browse and save your favorite shoe styles.
revised: Try shoe shops such as Zappos, larger stores such as Amazon, or a brand's own website. Pinterest and Instagram can also help you collect style ideas.
note: Keeps online browsing clear and save-feature availability conditional.

original: Yes. Most let you save items to a wish list or favourites list, usually after creating an account. You can then find them again later.
revised: Many sites let you save items to a wish list or favorites list. You may need an account. If that feature is missing, save the page as a browser bookmark.
note: Keeps online browsing clear and save-feature availability conditional.

original: Social media analytics studies data from social media. It shows how people respond to posts and helps measure whether an online campaign is working.
revised: Social media analytics means studying numbers and other information from social media. It can show how people respond to posts. A business can use it to check whether its online work is meeting its goals.
note: Explains analytics and sentiment while preserving measurement limits.

original: You can measure new followers, how many people see a post, and how many respond. You can also study whether comments sound positive or negative. That is called sentiment analysis.
revised: You can count followers, views, clicks, and replies. You can also study whether comments seem positive or negative. That is called sentiment analysis. It estimates the feeling in the words, but it can make mistakes.
note: Explains analytics and sentiment while preserving measurement limits.

original: Yes. It can show small businesses what works online and what needs to improve. They can use the results to plan posts, get more responses, and reach possible customers.
revised: Yes. It can help show which posts people notice or respond to. A small business can use that information when planning new posts. The numbers should be compared with what the business wants to achieve.
note: Explains analytics and sentiment while preserving measurement limits.

original: Establishing a consistent bedtime routine can help. Try reading a book before bed to relax your mind and create a calming atmosphere.
revised: Try a quiet routine you can repeat before bed. You might read a few pages of a book or do another calming activity. Keep the routine simple and choose something that helps you settle.
note: Makes the routine concrete without guaranteeing sleep.

original: In women's artistic gymnastics, the four events are the vault, uneven bars, balance beam, and floor exercise.
revised: The four events are vault, uneven bars, balance beam, and floor exercise. Vault involves jumping over a piece of equipment. Uneven bars uses two bars at different heights. The beam is a narrow raised surface. Floor routines use a large mat.
note: Explains each gymnastics event name briefly.

original: Quentin Tarantino is known for directing films like Pulp Fiction, Reservoir Dogs, and Kill Bill.
revised: Quentin Tarantino is known for directing films like Pulp Fiction, Reservoir Dogs, and Kill Bill.
note: Already a direct list of named films.

original: Popular options for comfortable home wear include sweatpants, hoodies, and t-shirts made from soft fabrics like cotton, fleece, or bamboo.
revised: Sweatpants, hoodies, and T-shirts are common choices. Look for soft fabric and a fit that lets you move comfortably. Cotton or soft fleece may suit you. Feel the actual garment, since fabric labels alone do not tell you how it feels.
note: Explains comfort through fit and feel rather than blanket material claims.

original: Different kinds of storms use different naming systems. For Atlantic tropical storms, names come from lists maintained through the World Meteorological Organization. Names make it easier to discuss a storm and share warnings.
revised: Different storms use different naming systems. Atlantic tropical storms use name lists maintained through the World Meteorological Organization. This organization helps countries work together on weather information. Names make storms easier to discuss and warnings easier to follow.
note: Explains retired names and preserves the regional naming scope.

original: For Atlantic tropical storms, the lists normally repeat every six years. The name of a very deadly or destructive storm can be retired and replaced. Other regions and other kinds of storms may follow different rules.
revised: For Atlantic tropical storms, the lists normally repeat every six years. A name can be retired after a very deadly or damaging storm. Retired means it is removed from future lists and replaced. Other regions may follow different rules.
note: Explains retired names and preserves the regional naming scope.

original: Yes, that describes the Atlantic tropical-storm system. Reusing lists keeps the system organized, while retiring names avoids repeating names linked to major disasters.
revised: Yes, that is how the Atlantic tropical-storm system works. Most names can return when the list is reused. Names linked with major disasters may be removed permanently.
note: Explains retired names and preserves the regional naming scope.

original: Common ingredients include vegetables like bell peppers, carrots, and broccoli, proteins like chicken, beef, or tofu, and seasonings like soy sauce and garlic.
revised: Common vegetables include peppers, carrots, and broccoli. You can add chicken, beef, or tofu. Tofu is made from soybeans. Soy sauce and garlic add flavor. Choose a recipe so the different ingredients cook properly together.
note: Cross-review: removes the unnecessary protein label and explains tofu. Keeps the original ingredient examples and recipe guidance.

original: A crisp usually has a crunchy oat topping, while a cobbler has a thicker, more biscuit-like topping.
revised: A crisp usually has a crunchy topping, often made with oats. A cobbler has a thicker topping, more like soft biscuits or dough. The main difference is the topping over the fruit.
note: Explains the visible dessert distinction.

original: Common options include flat mops, string mops, sponge mops, and steam mops. Choose one that suits your floor. Steam can damage some surfaces, so check the flooring and mop instructions first.
revised: Common choices include flat, string, sponge, and steam mops. Choose one made for your floor type. Steam can damage some floors. Read both the floor-care guide and the mop instructions before using it.
note: Keeps floor compatibility and steam caution clear.

original: You will usually meet your manager and colleagues, tour the lab, and learn its safety rules and ways of working.
revised: You will usually meet your manager and coworkers. They may show you around the lab and explain how it works. Expect safety training before you start unfamiliar tasks.
note: Keeps lab protection task-specific and training required.

original: The right protective equipment depends on the lab and the task. You may need a lab coat, suitable gloves, and eye protection, but your supervisor should explain exactly what is required. Do not start unfamiliar work before your safety training.
revised: It depends on the lab and the task. You may need a lab coat, gloves, and eye protection. Your supervisor should tell you exactly which kinds to use. Do not start unfamiliar work before the required safety training.
note: Keeps lab protection task-specific and training required.

original: Ask your manager or colleagues whenever you are unsure about a safety rule or task.
revised: Ask your manager or colleagues whenever you are unsure about a safety rule or task.
note: Keeps lab protection task-specific and training required.

original: Spring and autumn can be comfortable for sightseeing, while summer offers long days but can be hot and busy. Winter can also work if you prefer indoor activities. Choose around your budget and plans, and check the forecast near your trip.
revised: Spring and autumn can be comfortable for visiting sights. Summer has long days but may be hot and crowded. Winter may suit trips focused on museums and other indoor activities. Choose based on your budget and plans. Check the weather forecast near the travel date.
note: Explains itinerary organization through clear group-planning steps.

original: Some popular group activities in Paris include a guided tour of the Louvre Museum, a Seine River cruise, and a visit to the Eiffel Tower. You can also consider a cooking class or a wine tasting experience.
revised: You could tour the Louvre, take a Seine boat trip, or visit the Eiffel Tower. A cooking class or wine tasting is another option. Choose activities that suit the whole group's interests.
note: Explains itinerary organization through clear group-planning steps.

original: Make one shared list of places, costs, and must-do activities. Group nearby sights on the same day and leave free time. For bookings, use official attraction pages when possible and check group rules before paying.
revised: Make one shared list of places, prices, and top choices. Visit nearby sights on the same day and leave some free time. Use official attraction websites for bookings when possible. Check group rules and cancellation terms before paying.
note: Explains itinerary organization through clear group-planning steps.

original: Look for airbags, brakes that help prevent wheels from locking, and electronic stability control, which helps keep the car under control. Warnings when you leave a lane or when a car is in your blind spot can help too.
revised: Look for airbags and anti-lock brakes. Anti-lock brakes help stop wheels from locking during hard braking. Electronic stability control helps the car stay under control if it starts to slide. Lane warnings and blind-spot warnings can also help. A blind spot is an area you cannot easily see in your mirrors.
note: Explains safety-feature names and blind spot.

original: Yes, Elaborative Rehearsal is a study technique where you relate new information to something you already know or find meaningful. This helps create associations in your memory, making it easier to recall the information later.
revised: Elaborative rehearsal means linking new information to something you already understand. You think about its meaning instead of only repeating the words. Those links can help you remember it later.
note: Explains the study term with a distinct concrete mathematics example.

original: Suppose you learn that a rectangle’s area is length times width. Picture floor tiles: count the tiles in one row, then multiply by the number of rows. Connecting the formula to something familiar helps explain why it works.
revised: Suppose you learn that a rectangle's area is length times width. Picture a floor covered with equal square tiles. Count the tiles in one row, then count the rows. Multiplying those numbers tells you how many tiles cover the floor. This connects the formula to something you can picture.
note: Explains the study term with a distinct concrete mathematics example.

original: Wear what feels comfortable and fits the look you want. If you want to highlight your waist, try a fitted top, a belt, or a wrap dress. These are options, not rules for your body shape.
revised: Choose clothes that feel comfortable and give you the look you want. To highlight your waist, you could try a belt, fitted top, or wrap dress. These are choices, not rules for your body shape.
note: Keeps fashion advice optional and body-neutral.

original: She can choose any style she likes. If she wants a more defined waist, she could try a belt or a wrap top. A straight, loose fit is another option if that feels better. There is no need to make her body look a different shape.
revised: She can wear any style she likes. A belt or wrap top can draw attention to her waist if she wants. A straight, loose fit is another option. She does not need to make her body look a different shape.
note: Keeps fashion advice optional and body-neutral.

original: They are different console families, made by Sony and Microsoft. Compare the games, controller, services, and total cost. Games once tied to one brand may later appear elsewhere, so check individual titles.
revised: PlayStation is Sony's console family, while Xbox is Microsoft's. Compare the games, controllers, services, and full cost. Check the specific games you want. A game sold on only one system today may appear on another later.
note: Explains console differences and preserves exact-model and game availability limits.

original: The original Switch can suit people who want portable play and Nintendo games. Whether it is a good choice depends on the games you want and the price compared with other options.
revised: The original Switch can suit casual play and people who want Nintendo games. It also allows play away from a TV. Whether it is a good buy depends on the games and price. Compare the exact model with other options.
note: Explains console differences and preserves exact-model and game availability limits.

original: Examples include games from the Mario, Zelda, and Pokémon series, plus many independent and third-party games. Check that a particular title supports the exact Switch model you are buying.
revised: Examples include Mario, Zelda, and Pokémon games. Many smaller studios and other publishers make Switch games too. Check that each game works with the exact Switch model you plan to buy.
note: Explains console differences and preserves exact-model and game availability limits.

original: You can try using Gochujang in a marinade for chicken or beef, mixed with soy sauce and brown sugar. It's also great in stir-fries and noodle dishes.
revised: Gochujang is a sweet, spicy Korean chili paste. Mix some with soy sauce and brown sugar for a meat marinade. A marinade is a sauce food sits in before cooking. You can also stir gochujang into noodles or a stir-fry.
note: Explains both gochujang and marinade.

original: Common summer accessories include sunglasses, hats, and light bags. You could add a lightweight scarf or simple jewelry if you like. Choose things that suit your activities and feel comfortable.
revised: Sunglasses, hats, and light bags are common choices. You could also add a light scarf or simple jewelry. Choose things that feel comfortable and suit what you will be doing.
note: Keeps the accessory advice direct and conditional.

original: Siblings can communicate in many ways. Some speak very directly, while others are quieter or need more time to explain their feelings. Family size alone does not tell you how people communicate.
revised: Some siblings speak directly, while others are quieter. Some need more time to explain their feelings. A large family does not automatically have one communication style.
note: Explains listening while preserving the distinction between arguments and harm.

original: Disagreements happen in many families. What matters is that everyone feels safe and respected. Making up is useful, but threats, fear, or physical harm should not be treated as normal.
revised: Arguments happen in many families. What matters is that people feel safe and respected. Making up afterwards is useful. But threats, fear, or physical harm should not be accepted as normal.
note: Explains listening while preserving the distinction between arguments and harm.

original: One way to improve communication is to practice active listening. Make an effort to really hear and understand what your siblings are saying, and try to respond thoughtfully.
revised: Let your siblings finish before you reply. Listen for their main point and ask if you understood it correctly. This is active listening. It can help you answer what they mean, instead of only reacting to their tone.
note: Explains listening while preserving the distinction between arguments and harm.

original: One popular international ingredient is Gochujang, a Korean chili paste. It adds a sweet and spicy flavor to dishes.
revised: Try gochujang, a Korean chili paste. It adds both sweetness and heat to food. You can use a little in a sauce or stir-fry.
note: Explains the ingredient with a concrete use.

original: Yes, you could try making pasta with marinara sauce and roasted vegetables. It's easy and delicious.
revised: Try pasta with tomato sauce and roasted vegetables. Marinara is one kind of tomato sauce. Use a vegetarian sauce and serve the vegetables over the pasta.
note: Explains marinara and makes roast timing approximate.

original: You can use cherry tomatoes, zucchini, and bell peppers. Just toss them with olive oil, salt, and pepper, and roast in the oven at 400°F for about 20 minutes.
revised: Cherry tomatoes, zucchini, and bell peppers can work. Coat them lightly with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at about 400°F, or 200°C, for roughly 20 minutes. Check them as they cook. The time depends on piece size and your oven.
note: Explains marinara and makes roast timing approximate.

original: Yes, you could make a fruit salad with your favorite fruits, such as strawberries, grapes, and pineapple. Just cut them up and mix together in a bowl.
revised: Make a fruit salad. Wash the fruit and cut larger pieces into small pieces. Mix them in a bowl. Strawberries, grapes, and pineapple are possible choices.
note: Explains marinara and makes roast timing approximate.

original: Both are voice-assistant systems that can answer requests and control compatible devices. Their features and supported services change, so compare the functions you need on the actual speaker model.
revised: Both are voice assistants that respond to spoken requests. They can also control compatible smart devices. Their services and features change. Check the exact speaker for the tasks you want it to do.
note: Explains voice assistant and keeps comparison model-specific.

original: Honey, maple syrup, and coconut sugar still add sugar. If you want less sugar, try a recipe designed for that or reduce the amount a little at a time. Sugar also affects texture and browning, so large changes can alter the result.
revised: Honey, maple syrup, and coconut sugar still count as added sugar. Try a recipe designed to use less sugar. Or reduce a recipe's sugar a little at a time. Sugar also affects browning and texture. A large change may alter how the bake turns out.
note: Preserves total-sugar and recipe-function caveats in short sentences.

original: Yes, they can change flavor, moisture, and texture. Reducing the total amount may also make the result less sweet. Try a small change and keep notes rather than expecting any sweetener to behave exactly like sugar.
revised: Yes. Different sweeteners can change the flavor and how moist the food is. They can also change its texture. Using less usually makes the result less sweet. Try one small change and note what happens.
note: Preserves total-sugar and recipe-function caveats in short sentences.

original: Mashed banana or unsweetened applesauce can add sweetness and moisture in some recipes. They are not direct replacements in every bake. Use a recipe written for them, especially when you are starting out.
